Caring for one’s parents is something practitioners of the Way avoid; why not each go your separate ways? At the beginning of the Zhonghe era, Xuanzhong first stayed at the north of the stupa and traveled about.
After a long time, he returned south and settled in Yuzhang. Zhong Wang of Nanping treated him with the etiquette of a disciple.
Disliking living in a city, Xuanzhong had Wang purchase Mount Mo to build a vihāra called Longji to welcome him there. Students gathered like clouds.
In the third year of the Gui-mao cycle (May, Li Kuei-yung defeated Huang Chao and recovered Chang’an),
the Chan Master Da-an, a descendant of Baizhang’s lineage, passed away at Qingyuan Temple in Fuzhou.
An succeeded to the seat of Míushān. Cúigōng, the Imperial Commissioner of Yùzhāng, deeply honored his reputation and virtue.

Within his quarters, An would frequently ask the monks, "There is a phrase, there is no phrase—like a vine clinging to a tree. What is the meaning of this? A monk asked, "If the army of Huáng Cháo comes, what will you do, Master?"
"Where can one evade it? An said, "In the mountains of the five aggregates. The monk asked, "What if one is suddenly caught by it?
An said, "It will disturb the General. At the age of ninety-one, on the twenty-second day of the tenth month, he passed away while sitting upright in his quarters at Mount Yi.
He was posthumously bestowed the title of Grand Master Yuanzhi, and his stupa was named Zhengzhen.
Bo-ling, the Minister of Works and Chancellor of the State, as well as the poet Zhou Pu, admired him with profound reverence and composed poems,

This was during the fourth year of Jiachen, the first year of Guangqi (Yi-si), and the second year (Bing-wu).

there he shattered Xuefeng’s lacquer bucket. When he carried his bowl before the hall, he struck Deshan’s 'poisoned drum' once more.

The Patriarch then struck him and said, "Vinaya Master Kebin, you have been defeated in the battle of Dharma. You must pay a fine of five strings of cash. He then set up [the fine].

A meal of steamed rice was served in one hall. On the following day, the Patriarch himself struck the wooden mallet and said, "Venerable Kebin, as the head of the assembly, you have not been victorious in the Dharma-battle;
you shall not eat this meal and must leave the monastery immediately."
In the first year of the Wende era (824), on the wu-shen day, Chan Master Daowu’s successor, Shichuang Qingzhu, entered nirvana.
Qingzhu had inherited the Dharma from Daowu and did not leave the Shichuang monastery for twenty years; among his many disciples, there were those who practiced constant seated meditation.
He lay down, as motionless as a tree stump. The world called him the "Master of the Withered Tree. Qi Ji, Guan Xiu, Tai, Bu Na, and others were all among his disciples;
they all took the practice of poetic composition as their Buddhist service. Yet Tai exerted himself even more in the study of Chan.

The man said, "I have sought the skillful and found it nowhere; from where does the unskillful come? At this, Zhuo attained realization and presented a verse, saying: "Radiant, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges;

The Master served as the preceptor to Zhuangzong of Later Tang. One day, Zhuangzong said to the Master, "When I captured Daliang, I obtained a single bright pearl, but no one has yet offered a price for it.
The Master replied, "I ask Your Majesty to let me see the pearl. The Emperor reached out his hand and unfolded the ends of his *bōtóu* (head-wrap).
The Master said, "This is the treasure of a sovereign; who would dare to offer a price for it? [The inscription on] the stele states that the Master passed away.

On the twelfth day of the seventh month in the first year of Wende of Emperor Wen of the Tang dynasty—corresponding to the wu-shen year—it was thirty-six years prior to the gui-wei year of the first year of Tongguang of Zhuangzong of the Later Tang;
thus, it is clearly not Zhuangzong. Examining the period now, the one who unfurled the legs of the *fu* headgear was likely Prince Jin Li Kuyong.
This was mistakenly identified as his son, Zhuangzong Cuncu.
According to the records, in the first year of Guangming of Emperor Xizong, the *gengzi* year, Huang Chao entered Chang’an and the Emperor fled to Xingyuan.
In the second year of Zhonghe, the *renyin* year, Li Kuyong led the Shatuo troops toward Hezhong. In the fifth month of the third year, the *guiyou* year, Li Kuyong defeated [Huang Chao].
Huang Chao recaptured Chang’an. An imperial edict appointed Li Kuei-yung as the Military Governor of Hedong.
In the fifth month of the fourth year, the Jia-chen year, Huang Chao hurried toward Bianzhou; Li Kuei-yung pursued and struck him down, achieving a great victory.
In the seventh month of autumn, Shi Pu presented Huang Chao’s head. In the eighth month, Li Kuei-yung was promoted to the rank of Prince of Longxi. (From the *Beishi*).
This is what the *Denglu* (Lamp Records) refers to as "receiving a priceless jewel from Daliang.
As for the title "Zhen" (Emperor), it is an error for Zhuangzong.

Stele. Furthermore, the inscription on the left side of the Patriarch’s Stūpa Stele states:

Six hundred years after those sages of the Eastern Land had passed away, the teaching of the Western Sage reached the Eastern Land.
After further years had elapsed, the Eastern Land obtained the transmission of the Dharma from the Western Sage—a transmission that had not been passed down [by others].
The Mind-Seal. Furthermore, over the course of many years, the five schools of the Eastern Land arose to correspond to the auspicious omen of the Single Flower.

They are recorded in the eighth hundred and sixty-eighth fascicle of the *Wenyuan Yinghua*, in the section on Stele Inscriptions.

Twenty-fifth. The Nineteenth Stele Inscription for the Venerable Monk. Following the stele inscription for the temple in Xinxiung County, Xuanchou, is recorded the stele inscription for the stupa of the late Chan Master of Great Virtue, Master Jiang, of Wei Prefecture.
The author is Gongsheng Yi. The inscription states: "The Upādhyāya’s surname was Kong and his courtesy name was Cunjiang.
His family was originally from the region of Zoulu; he was a descendant of the lineage of the Queli [Confucius]. He lived in seclusion in the south for many years."
I wish to assemble the Sangha’s treasures to present as evidence; my intention is primarily to recover what has been lost and to supplement what is deficient.
However, Gongsheng Yi’s “Stele for the Xinghua Pagoda” does not merely recover the lost and supplement the deficient;

it clarifies the similarities and differences between the teachings and institutions of the Sage of the Western Land and the Sage of the Eastern Land, thereby providing a means for future generations to harmonize their understanding and rectify vulgar learning.
To distinguish the divergent paths and establish the eyes and ears of humans and devas, it truly lies herein. At Panshan’s Sweet Spring, he recorded his withdrawal from official life;
at the lecture halls of the Three Dynasties, he clarified the "Tiger of Meaning. Whether in the capital or the water-lands, he manifested his traces of travel.
At Mount Yang, he struck his finger to signal resonance; at Lingji, he resided at Guanyin Temple in Jiangxi’s Chan monastery.

The supplementary records of Bao-shou state that before long he passed away. His cremation rites were performed with full ceremony, and it was verified that the three holy ones had attended him together.
Outside the Southern Brick Gate, to the left of the main thoroughfare, upon the old foundations of Xinghua Temple, over one thousand śarīra relics were found.
His virtuous demeanor was most extraordinary; thus, a stupa was erected in Xunfeng Li of Guixiang County, south of the prefecture, to be enshrined alongside his predecessors.
This is the stele for the Master’s stupa. Throughout the father’s life and the son’s passing, from beginning to end there has been no interval;

this shall be clearly transmitted through ten thousand ages. I am particularly saddened that those who receive the teachings of the Sage of the Eastern Land all run contrary to the mind-dharma of that Sage, yet they stand aloof and claim to hold fast to the Sage’s teaching as if it were a physical object.
They used arms and shields to defend against it. Alas! How strange this is! Now, the Sage of the Eastern Land was the Master Confucius;

From the third year of the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty, the year Guihai, until the Gengzi year of the Xianping era of the Song dynasty, more than ninety years had passed; thus, three generations resided at Tong-an, Feng-xi, and Lian-shan.

Regarding the three periods of time, each is calculated as thirty years to establish the lineage and succession. Although minor details may have been omitted and subtle points lack corroborating evidence, the essential principles remain clearly intact. These are preserved here to await future scholars who shall examine and finalize them.
Chan Master Daojian succeeded him at Yunju.
Daojian was a native of Fanyang. Having shaved his head as a novice, he received the full precepts and traveled extensively among various monastic communities. Later, he visited Yunju;
after conversing with him for three consecutive days, [Yunju] marveled greatly at him and instructed him to serve the community with diligent austerity. Thereupon, Daojian personally...

He himself performed the tasks of the mortar and pestle and joined in the labor of chopping wood for the hearth. He oversaw all temple affairs while simultaneously engaging in the discussion of ancient and modern matters;
yet none among the assembly were aware of this. Because his seniority in the monastic order was high, he was appointed as the First Seat (Dìyīzuò) of the hall.

Previously, the spirit of Gāo'ān Dòngshān was extremely powerful; when the Patriarch Yúnjū resided at Sānfēng, the spirit served him. Now that [Yúnjū] had come to Yúnjū [Monastery], the spirit likewise...
He followed him there. They stayed beneath a withered tree, yet the tree flourished; it was called the "Tree Spirit of Peace and Bliss.

When Yunju was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, the administrative monk asked, "If the Master does not decline [to designate a successor], who should succeed you? He replied, "The one currently serving as hall steward—my intention does not lie in this steward.
I mean that you should select someone capable of preaching the Dharma. Everyone agreed, saying, "The second [candidate]."

"Your appointment is acceptable. However, let us first request Jian. If Jian declines, we must decline. Since Jian had previously received the prediction of his future enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*), he immediately took charge of the assembly and expounded the Dharma.
The administrators were greatly discouraged. Jian perceived their intent and one night fled away. That same evening, the tree deity of Anle wept aloud.
At dawn the next day, the assembly pursued him to Mazhuang. They repented their error and welcomed him back, hearing voices in the air crying out repeatedly.
He called out, "The Master is coming! A monk asked, "What is the Master’s house style? He replied, "Attaining mastery wherever one is.
The monk asked, "Is it not true that Vimalakīrti was a Golden Grain Tathāgata? He said, "Yes. The monk asked, "Why then did he listen to the Dharma under Śākyamuni?
He replied, "He did not contend over self and others. The monk asked, "When encountering a fierce tiger on the road..."
“How is it? he asked. [The Master] replied, “A thousand people, ten thousand people do not encounter it; why then do you, O *ācārya*, encounter it alone?
He asked, “What is it like when one dwells alone on a solitary peak? [The Master] replied, “I leave the seven bays of the monks’ hall unoccupied;
who told you to dwell alone on a solitary peak? He asked, “An ancient said: ‘If you would maintain this matter, you must go directly to the summit of the highest mountain.’”
He stood up. "Walking on the bottom of the deepest sea—what is the meaning of this? He replied, "High peaks and deep seas are utterly remote, solitary, and perilous.
Is it like the soft warmth within your inner chambers? His discernment was refined and his realization profound;

his practice was clearly verified, and his responses to stimuli and engagement with phenomena transcended all measure. The masters of the world took him as their model. He lived for over eighty years and passed away without illness.

Jiazi, the first year of Tianyou (August: Zhu Quanzhong assassinated the Emperor at the Jiao Hall; he enthroned the Crown Prince Zhu as Emperor Zhaoxuan. Although he was established as emperor, no new era name was adopted;

The second year, the year of Yi-chou (825).
Chan Master Changsha’s fourth-generation descendant, Xuedou Changtong Jie, succeeded Changsha Cen.
Residing at Xuedou, his transformative influence flourished profoundly. In the seventh month, he assembled the congregation and, burning incense, transmitted [the Dharma].
Having finished his instructions, he joined his palms and passed away.
In the third year of the Bingyin cycle,
Chan Master Youzhang resided at Ruilong.
Zhāng received the "Seal of the Benevolent Heart" from Băishuǐ. He dwelt in seclusion at Tiantái.

Encountering famine and pestilence in eastern Zhejiang, Zhāng collected and buried thousands of exposed bones across the three prefectures of Wēn, Tái, and Míng; he was then known as the Great Being Pīzēng.
When Qián Wén established Ruìlóng Monastery, he invited Zhāng to serve as its abbot.
Chan Master Huileng resided at Zhaoqing.

Chan Master Wensui resided at Qishan.
Sui was a successor of Dongshan Zu and lived at Qishan in Lishu. One day, Juling came to seek instruction. When asked, "At the moment when a single arrow pierces the three barriers, what then?
[Wensui] replied, "Release the master within the barrier and look. [Juling] said, "If that is so, then one knows one's transgression."
“[I] must change [the arrow]. [Daowu] asked, “When shall we wait for another time? [Daowu] said, “A fine arrow; it cannot be released anywhere. As soon as he finished speaking, [Xuanzui] came out.

Xuanzui said, “Come here first, *ācārya*. Liang turned his head back. Xuanzui stepped down from the meditation seat, seized him, and said, “Setting aside for a moment the matter of ‘one shaft piercing the three barriers,’ try shooting an arrow for Qinshan and see.
Liang hesitated. Xuanzui struck him seven times with his staff and said:
Now listen to this reckless fellow. He has been suspicious for thirty years.

*Dingmao* (4th year). [After the fourth month: the first year of Kai Ping of the Liang dynasty. This was the year the Tang fell. There were five kingdoms: Liang, Jin, Qi, Huainan, and Xichuan. There were five prefectures: Wuyue, Hunan, Jingnan, Fujian, and Lingnan.
In this year, Jin, Qi, and Huainan still used the era name Tian You of the Tang; Xichuan used Tian Fu; all others followed the calendar of the Liang.
Chan Master Deqian resided at Mingzhao Mountain.
Having received the seal of transmission from Luoshan, he did not remain confined to any single corner [of the tradition], but vigorously propagated the profound principles.

All the veteran masters feared his quick-wittedness; among those of later learning, few dared to meet his sharp edge. His reputation spread far and wide, and the assembly requested that he reside in Wuyuan.
In Mingzhao Mountain of the prefecture, Chan Master Daofu resided at Jingqing.
Daofu was a successor of Xuefeng; while residing at Jingqing, students flocked to him from all directions.
Chan Master Xingxiu lived in seclusion at Siming.

He was the son of Chen of Southern Quan; his mother dreamed of swallowing the sun and awoke in surprise to give birth to him. His ears were long and hung down to his shoulders, and an extraordinary fragrance filled the room.
At the age of seven, he did not speak. When someone asked him, "Are you mute? he suddenly replied with a voice, "No."

He encountered a master of the Way; it was merely a matter of him having broken through the smoke-filled tower. People marveled at him even more. As he grew up, he read books, achieving mastery upon a single reading.

He extended his studies to the Buddhist scriptures (*nèidiǎn*), perusing the entire Tripiṭaka. Suddenly, he resolved to travel beyond the mundane world, donning straw sandals to visit famous mountains.
Upon reaching Waguan Temple in Jinling, he shaved his head and received full ordination. There he studied under Xuefeng and obtained the transmission of the mind-seal.
While traveling to Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai, he rested by a cliff one day; fierce tigers and giant snakes came and went at his side, yet they remained docile and did not leave.
Upon reaching Siming, he dwelt alone beneath a pine tree, where celestial flowers fell like rain. He further sat in meditation at Huangwei Rock.
He thatched a hut for shelter; a hundred birds brought him flowers. The hollow where his knees rested upon the flat rock he sat upon became a depression.

Wuchen (the fifth year of Tianyou in the Tang dynasty—known as Huainan in Jin and Kaiping Year 2 in Liang—and the first year of Wucheng in the reign of Wang Jian of Shu; this was the year when Western Sichuan was called Shu).
The Chan Master Dingshan passed away at Fuzhou Xuefeng, where the Great Master Zhenjue Yicun resided.
Yicun’s Way filled the world; Emperor Xi Zong admired his reputation and bestowed upon him the title of Great Master Zhenjue.
He also wore a purple *kāṣāya*. The Ruler of Min treated him with great honor and reverence, seeking the Dharma and offering his sincere devotion.

Prior to his passing, [the Master] himself composed an inscription for his stupa, including the preface. On the third month, he manifested illness; the Ruler of Min dispatched physicians to present medicine.

Xuanzang said, "I am not ill," and ultimately refused to take the medicine. He left behind a verse of entrustment. On the second day of the fifth month, he went out to walk in Lantian in the morning and returned at evening.
He returned to bathe his body and entered nirvana at midnight. He was eighty-seven years of age and fifty-nine years of *dharma*-years.
At that time, Chan Master Zongyi Shibei of Xuansha under Xuefeng passed away in Fuzhou.
Beis succeeded Xuefeng and resided at Meixi; later, he dwelt at Xuansha. At that time, the assembly of the sea all admired and submitted to him upon hearing his reputation.
He had a thousand disciples and spent thirty years responding to the capacities of others and engaging with sentient beings.

On the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month, he manifested illness and passed away. He was seventy-five years old and forty-four years since his ordination. He was posthumously granted the title Zongyi.
Chan Master Wenyuan traveled extensively to study under various masters; upon reaching Lingshu, he served as the First Seat and subsequently succeeded him on that seat.
After receiving the Dharma seal from Xuefeng, Wenyuan left the mountain range to visit masters throughout the various regions, vigorously engaging in spirited debates.

the first year of Shunyi of Emperor Wu Ruihuang Yang Pu of the Wu state), he was invited by the Magistrate of Zhangzhou, Duke Wang, to reside at Dizang Monastery on Mount Shi in the western city.
Chan Master Jueji of Jiufeng Da’jue was a Dharma heir of Letan under Shishuang. Da’jue succeeded Shishuang Zhu.
Initially, Baizhang interred Mazu’s relics at Shimeng in Haihun and maintained the stupa there for over ten years;
however, once he took up residence at Baizhang, he no longer returned to Shimeng. Da’jue traveled from Jiufeng to visit him.
Thus he established the Dharma assembly and became the first patriarch of Letan. In that year, he passed away while sitting in meditation; he was posthumously titled Dajue (Great Awakening).
His attendant at Xinghua, Shoukuo, traveled to various regions to test his realization and clarify the teachings. [The note states:

"Although it has been thirty years since the passing of the patriarch Xinghua, he is still referred to as 'the attendant of Xinghua' to show that he did not fail his role as the patriarch’s attendant. Generally, those who record their official duties do so without shame before their office."

Kuo, who had attained the Dharma and was a successor in the lineage of Master Xinghua, traveled on foot to Deshan. He asked the Master, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Deshan replied, "What? What?
Kuo said, "The imperial decree summons the flying dragon’s horse; yet the lame tortoise sticks its head out. Deshan then ceased speaking.
The following day, after Deshan had finished his bath, Kuo went to offer him tea. As he did so, Deshan patted him on the back.
Yixia said, "What about yesterday's *gong'an*? [Jiashan] said, "This old fellow has only just begun to see clearly today.
Jiashan then left. Later, Huikong traveled on foot to the assembly at Huayan Monastery in Xiangzhou.
One day, Huayan ascended the hall and addressed the great assembly: "Today, as for Linji, Deshan, Gaoteng, Dayu, Niaoke, and Chuanshou..."
"Disciples and descendants, there is no need for 'how' or 'what. I request that you enter directly with a single blade. Huayan shall provide you with verification.
Kuo stepped forward, prostrated, and upon rising, let out a shout. Huayan also shouted. Kuo shouted again; Huayan shouted once more.
Kuo then said, "The assembly, look at this old fellow’s total defeat! He let out another shout, clapped his hands, and returned to his place.
After the assembly had finished their formal duties, Yan descended from his seat and returned to the Abbot’s quarters. At that time, Yanzhao was serving as the *vinaya-dhara* (Vina).
When Yan went up to inquire after him, Yan said, "Vina, you have come. It is truly intolerable that Shoukuo just now twisted and squeezed me;
I intended to assemble the community and give him a beating and drive him out. Yanzhao replied, "It is too late to drive him out now. From this point on, it is the Master who has spoken improperly."
He is a descendant of Linji; his fundamental nature is thus. Yanfang ceased his anger. Zhaopai recounted this to Guokuan.
Guokuan said, "For what reason do you urge this fellow? Before I even asked, he already wanted to eat my staff so that my words might be put into practice.
If he does not strike now, he will surely suppress these words of mine. Zhaopai said, "Even so," and so on.
Having already traveled throughout the world, Huairang arrived at Rumon. One day, seeing Buzhou at Rumon, he asked, "What are you doing all day long, looking so disheveled and distracted?
Buzhou replied, "Do you see me looking disheveled and distracted, Master?
Rumon then gave a shout; Buzhou also shouted. Both of them then ceased their activity. Huairang said, "Look at this!"

"Two blind men! He then shouted. Returning to the abbot's quarters at Lumen, he ordered an attendant to invite Guok up and said, "Just now, the old monk and Chan Master Chu engaged in a meeting of host and guest. What was the failure?"
[The monk] said, "I see that your illness has grown deep. The Master said, "Since I first met Xinghua, I have understood it myself.
[The monk] said, "When you were at Xinghua, Shoukuo was the attendant; do you remember what was said at that time? [The Master] said, "Please cite it for me."
Kuo then recounted how Xinghua asked the Master, "From where have you come? The Master replied, "From Wutai.
Xinghua asked, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The Master then shouted. Xinghua said, "I asked you whether or not you saw Mañjuśrī;
why do you flare up in anger again? The Master shouted once more. Xinghua was left speechless. The Master then paid him homage.
The next day, Xinghua arrived. Jiaoshou Kuang called out, "The Master has already departed.
Xinghua ascended the hall and said, "Look at this monk, carrying a broken rope over his shoulder, heading south.
Later on, he will say that he came to see Xinghua. Today’s public case is exactly like that moment. It is called "Xinghua."
At that time, he remained speechless. [The Master] said, "Because I saw that you did not understand the phrase of host and guest, you were speechless.

When you wished to call upon me to engage in debate, I, the Master, had already departed. The next day, Lumen specifically prepared tea for the assembly and addressed them during the evening discourse.
The Chronological Record of the Lineage of the Doctrine, Volume Seventeen;
The Chronological Record of the Lineage of the Doctrine, Volume Eighteen.
The Year of Renwu (the second year of Longde of the Liang Dynasty).
Chan Master Yanzhao went to Nanyuan.
Yanzhao was preeminent and possessed a heroic spirit; there was no book he did not read, yet he lacked any intention to serve the world.

His father and elder brother compelled him to take office, so he once traveled to the capital to sit for the imperial examinations, but upon returning east, he followed Zhi Gong of Kaiyuan Temple to study the Vinaya.

The Master shaved his head and donned the dyed robes. Having received full ordination, he traveled to lecture halls where he studied the *Fahua xuanyi* (Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra) and cultivated the samādhi and wisdom of *śamatha-vipaśyanā*.

Senior masters vied with one another to yield to him. He departed and traveled to famous mountains, staying at Xuefeng for five years before visiting Ruiyan, yet he remained without lingering attachment there.
Arriving in Yuezhou, he called upon Jingqing, who marveled at his brilliant and transcendent character. He then went to Huayan Monastery to serve as the *karmadāna* (steward). It so happened that...
Attendant Shoukuo came from Nan-yuan; Zhaoxin marveled at him and formed a friendship with him. Consequently, Shoukuo silently realized the essential meaning of the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan).
He sighed, saying, "Is this how Linji employs his Dharma? Thereupon he went to visit the Patriarch (Xuefeng). Upon entering the gate, he did not prostrate.
The Patriarch said, "Entering the gate, one must discern the host. Zhaoxin said, "I ask the Master to distinguish it for me definitively. The Patriarch [pointed] to the left.
Zhuo snapped his fingers with his knee. Zhaozhou then shouted. The Master snapped his fingers with his right knee. Zhaozhou shouted again.
The Master said, "Setting aside that snap with the left knee, what about this snap with the right? Zhaozhou said, "Blind! The Master then raised his staff.
Zhaozhou said, "Do not wield the blind lash and the sightless blow! I will seize and strike you, Master! Do not say I did not warn you. The Master threw down the staff.
Baizhang said, "Today I have been thoroughly outwitted by this yellow-faced monk from Zhejiang.
Guizhao said, "The Master is much like someone who cannot manage his almsbowl and falsely claims he is not hungry. Baizhang said, "Have you ever been here before, Layman?
Guizhao said, "What kind of question is that? Baizhang said, "I am simply asking you a straightforward question. Guizhao said, "That, too, will not do."
[The Master] let it pass. He then went down to attend the hall, and subsequently went up to the Dharma Hall to perform prostrations and repentance.
The Patriarch asked, "Disciple, whom have you studied under? Zhao replied, "I was at Huayan in Xiangzhou, where I spent the summer retreat together with Attendant Kuang. The Patriarch said:
"Come, meet a true master! He asked again, "What did he say to you? Zhaomo replied, "From beginning to end, he only taught me to always act as the host.
The Patriarch then struck him and pushed him out of the abbot's quarters, saying, "What use is there for a fellow such as this, who brings such disgrace?
Thereupon, Zhaomo took the teaching to heart and served as the garden head. One day, the Patriarch went to the garden.
A questioner asked, "Regarding 'a single blow from the south,' how do you deliberate upon it? Zhaò said, "Deliberate upon it as something extraordinary.
After a long silence, Zhaò then asked, "How do you deliberate upon it here, Master? The Patriarch raised his staff and said, "Beneath the blow is the patience of non-arising;
when facing the critical moment, one does not see the teacher. At these words, Zhaò attained a great realization of the profound principle and thereafter remained in attendance.

Six years later, An-yin said, "Under the staff is the patience of non-arising (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti); when facing the critical moment, one sees no teacher. This is the essential meaning of the profound pivot.
Although Fengxue had awakened to the Three Mysteries under Attendant Kuò, he had not yet reached the essential point; how could he have avoided this?
Is there a further awakening? Because of this, a monk asked Fengyang, "What is the place where the student gains strength?
He replied, "Beating the great elephant in Jia Prefecture. "What is the place where the student turns the body?
He replied, "Bathing the iron ox in Shan Prefecture. "What is the place where the student is intimate? He replied, "Playing with the lion in Xihe. Then he said: "If..."
If a person understands these three phrases, the Three Mysteries have already been clarified. Furthermore, there remain the Three Essentials; you must realize them.
This is the true sequence within that which has no sequence, and the true gain and loss within that which has no gain or loss. The Caodong school also says:
"View the commoners and nobles, the dukes and marquises, as one and the same path; distinguish the ranks of the high and low, the honorable and the humble. One who knows this may...
This speaks to the fundamental purport.
Xiangfu Yin said, "Fenyang once further remarked: 'The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are difficult to distinguish;
when one attains the meaning and forgets the words, the Way is easy to approach. Viewing these together, one may speak of a single phrase. Zhao Yinglin [commented on this].
Qi! Originally, everywhere else lacked any serious attention to this matter. As soon as one accepted the Master’s word with devotion, one would immediately become a garden head.
Those of today who travel about accepting titles and positions from others, and who arrange themselves among bright windows and clean desks—how far removed they are from that!
What could the plot you have devised possibly be for? Master Zhao ought to know shame upon seeing this.
As for Chan Master Wen Yi, who attained enlightenment while enduring snow at Mount Dizang:
Yi was the son of the Lu family of Yuhang; he was naturally brilliant from birth, received the tonsure at the age of seven, and took full ordination in his youth. He investigated...
Vinai (Vini) explored the Confucian classics and, shaking his mendicant’s staff, traveled south. Upon reaching Fuzhou, he visited Changqing, yet did not achieve great realization.
Later, together with three others—Shaofa and Xuejin—he traveled from Zhangzhou to the region beyond Lake Hu.

Encountering rain and snow, with mountain streams swelling into torrents, they unpacked their belongings and took rest in an ancient temple at a corner of the district. Entering the hall, they found an elderly monk sitting by a brazier.
The three men sat by the fire in succession. The old monk asked Zhiyi, "Where are you going on this journey?
Zhiyi replied, "I am traveling for practice. The monk asked, "What is the matter of traveling for practice? Zhiyi said, "I do not know. The monk said, "Not knowing is most intimate.

They then recited together with the other three the *Zhao Lun* (Treatise of Zhaoming). Upon reaching the passage, "Heaven and earth share the same root as I," the old monk said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great..."
Dishi asked, "Are you the same as or different from the other elders? Guishan Yi said, "Different. The old monk held up two fingers. Yi said, "The same.
The old monk again held up two fingers and then rose to leave. Guishan was greatly astonished.
As he walked around the corridors, he read the temple plaque, which said "Shishan Dizang," and thus realized it was Chan Master Guichen. When the snow cleared, he took his leave; [this was] Guichen.
As Fayun was being escorted out through the gate, [Dongshan] asked him, "The Elder usually says that the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only.
Now, point to this stone in the courtyard and tell me: does it reside within the mind or outside the mind? Fayun replied, "It resides within the mind.
Dongshan laughed and said, "Travelling monk, for what reason do you place a mere stone upon your head? Fayun was speechless.
Stumped and unable to respond, Yi finally took his leave of Xiu and Jin. He immediately opened his bag and sat beneath the mats to seek decisive instruction.
For nearly a month, he presented his insights and expounded upon the principles of the Dharma. Baolin said to him, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this.
Yi replied, "I am at the end of my words and the exhaustion of my reasoning. Baolin said, "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, all views—"
[Cheng] attained great enlightenment beneath the words [of the master].
Chan Master Huiqing resided at Bajiao Mountain.
Qing had received the Dharma from Shiting Yong; while residing at Bajiao Mountain, he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "You all..."
"Staff! I give you this staff. You have no staff, so I take it away from you.
Relying on the staff, descend from the seat."

In the year Guiwei (after the fourth month of the third year of Liang Longde; the first year of Tongguang of Zhuangzong Li Cunxun of Later Tang), Chan Master Longya Judu, a descendant of the Dongshan lineage, passed away.
In the year Jiashen (the second year of the Later Tang Tongguang era), the Patriarch transmitted the Seal of the True Dharma to Yanzhao.
One day, the Patriarch asked Zhao, "Explain for me the four kinds of critical examination (*liaojian*). What dharma do they examine? He replied, "Ordinary..."
If speech does not transcend ordinary sentiment, one immediately falls into the conceptual understanding of the sages; this is a great malady for students.

The former sages were concerned about this and provided skillful means, like using one wedge to extract another. Because of this, the Patriarch asked: "What is it to take away the person but not the environment? He replied:
A newly forged golden bullet from the furnace has shattered the Zen master’s iron mask. He asked again: “What is ‘seizing the environment but not seizing the person’?
He replied: “The straw mat has just been divided; the head is split open, yet amidst the first parting of the chaotic clouds, the shadow still remains.
He asked again: “What is ‘seizing both the person and the environment’? He replied: “Stepping forward with bated breath, one must act with urgency.”
"Urgent! Seize the whip at the collar; do not delay! He was asked again, "What is it like when both the person and the environment are not taken away?
He replied, "I always remember that in the third month in Jiangnan, where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fragrant. He was asked again, "Linji had three phrases.
On that day, someone asked, 'What is the first phrase? Linji said, 'The seal of the three essentials is opened.'"
The red dot is narrow; there is no room for deliberation to distinguish host from guest. Zhao followed this with a shout. He then asked, "What is the second phrase?
Linji said, "How could a wondrous understanding fail to admit of a question from Wuzhuo? How could the layman fail to match the power of cutting off the stream?
Zhao said, "Before you even asked, it was already wrong. He asked again, "What is the third phrase? Linji said, "Just..."
"Behold the puppeteer performing with puppets; the movements of the head depend entirely upon the person inside. Zhao said, "If it were exposed too clearly, it would be unsatisfactory.
Thereupon, the Master considered him capable of sustaining the Linji school and entrusted him with the seal of the Dharma.
Chan Master Huiji resided at Huanglong;
Huiji was a dharma successor of Xuanquan Yan, who also resided at Huanglong. One day, the Immortal Lü Yan traveled along the road and passed through Mount Huanglong.

Seeing purple clouds forming a canopy, he suspected there was an extraordinary person within and entered to pay his respects. He encountered the master ascending the hall while the drum was being struck;
his spiritual insight led him to believe this must be Master Lü. Desiring to test and guide him further, [Zhaozhou] said in a stern voice, "There is one here by the seat who is stealing the Dharma.
Yunyan stepped out resolutely and said, "I am a man of the clouds and water. Zhaozhou asked, "What will you do when suddenly the clouds have vanished and the water has dried up? Yunyan had no reply.
[Zhao] Yan: “Correct. He requested a substitute phrase. [Zhao]yan asked as before. Jueji said: “The Yellow Dragon appears. [Zhao]yan asked:

“A world is hidden within a single grain of millet; mountains and rivers are boiled within a half-measure of cauldron. Tell me, what is the meaning of this? Jueji pointed and said: “This is a corpse-guarding ghost.
[Zhao]yan said: “But what can be done? There is the medicine of longevity and immortality within his bag. Jueji said: “Even if one passes through...”
"Even after eighty thousand kalpas, one ultimately falls into emptiness and extinction. When [Zhao]yan was struck by a flying sword at his ribs, the sword could not penetrate him.
He then prostrated himself and requested instruction on the ultimate goal. Dajue said, "I shall not ask about boiling mountains and rivers within a half-seer cauldron;
how is it that a world is hidden within a single grain of millet? At these words, Yan attained sudden realization and composed a verse, saying: "I cast away my gourd-bag..."
He shattered his zither. Now he no longer clings to mercury within gold. Since first meeting Huanglong, he has finally realized that all his previous efforts were misplaced.
May this instruction on the pivot of awakening be protected. [His style name was] Dongbin; he was from Jingchuan.

The year of Yiyou (the third year of Tongguang). The year of Bingxu (from the fourth month of the fourth year of Tongguang, following the first year of Mingzong’s Tiānchéng, corresponding to the first year of Yueshi Zhengyuan).
In the year Dinghai (the second year of Tiānchéng of the Later Táng / the first year of Qiánzhēn of Wú),
and in the year Wuzi (the third year of Tiānchéng / the first year of Dàyǒu of Hàn),
the Chan Master Zhēnyìng Guìchén, a descendant of Xuánshā, passed away at Luóhàn Yúan in Zhāngzhōu.
Later, Baochen was promoted to the rank of Arhat. When he sat at ease on his simple frame bed, if he saw a monk approaching, he would immediately raise his whisk and ask, "Do you understand?
The monk would reply, "I thank the Master for this instruction. Baochen said, "You see me raise my whisk and then thank me for the instruction.
Every day you see mountains and see waters; do these not instruct you? Again, seeing a monk approach, he raised [his whisk].
[He held up] a whisk (*vīraṇaka*). The monk prostrated and offered praise. Zhenchen said, "When you saw me raise my whisk, you immediately prostrated and praised it.

But when I was sweeping the floor and raised my broom, why did you not offer praise then? He lived for sixty-two years and sat in meditation for forty-two summer retreats. He bathed and passed away while seated.
His remains were cremated, and his relics (*śarīra*) were collected to build a stupa. He was posthumously titled Zhenyi (True Response).
Chan Master Xingchong resided at Gushan.
Chong was a Dharma successor of Baofu Zhan and lived at Gushan Ba’en Temple. He said to his disciples:
"Although I am no longer here, I have never failed to act for the sake of you brothers. If you fully understand how I have always acted for others while at Ba’en, I grant you my approval."

To emerge from conceptual thoughts and attain understanding regarding the field of the five aggregates and the body—should you fail to master this, it means you have not yet emerged from the conceptual thoughts and understanding of your own mind.
This is why the ancients called it "the livelihood of ghosts" or being "a guest beneath the frog's robe.
If you wish to achieve swift resonance, then realize it right now where you stand; examine it and recognize it for yourself. What is there?
This is a transgression. It is not so that your faculties and thoughts are slow or hesitant; rather, you have been investigating for both day and night.
Suddenly, one day you caught sight of it—do not be satisfied with what is slight, but continue to investigate until you reach the ultimate limit.
Even in brothels and taverns, whether things are defiled or pure, good or bad, observe them with what you see until they are fully understood as being entirely such.
This realm enters as one enters the Vinaya. If one perceives even a single dharma as much as a hair’s breadth and fails to see this matter, I call it the cataract-obscuration of ignorance.
One must simply not see that there is any dharma that is separate; only then can one attain perfect completion.
Reaching this point, one can further exercise mastery in turning and casting [phenomena] at will, such that their opening and closing leave no trace or seam. It is like...
It is like water entering water, fire entering fire, wind entering wind, and space entering space.
If one can act in this way, one may directly draw a single sword and sever the net of doubt of all people under heaven, such that there is no longer even a semblance of "one-ness" or "non-action."
Therefore, the ancients said: "When great functions are extensively activated, every action must be entirely true.
If there were such a man who reached this kind of realm, who would dare to step forward and speak of right or wrong? Why is this? Because this person is a true man.
It transcends all limits and measurements, penetrating beyond cause and effect; no place whatsoever can restrain such a person.
If you can act in this way, it will suffice. If you have not yet attained this, you must watch carefully;
do not speak or breathe recklessly, lest you sink back down and waste immeasurable kalpas. Do not wait until such a time has come before you say, "I have not spoken of repaying my debt."
The first patriarch who originally established the Fayan school was named Wenyi.
Dizang succeeded him. He was the son of the Lu family of Yuhang; his brilliance emerged at the age of seven.
He received the tonsure under the Vinaya Master Quanwei of Xinjian and proceeded to Kaiyuan Monastery in Zhaozhou to receive full ordination from Vinaya Master Xijue.
Jie first visited Changqing, but attained no realization. Later, he sought instruction from Dizang Chen and inherited his Dharma lineage.
Initially, he resided at Chongshou; subsequently, he resided at Qingliang in Jinling.
The first patriarch of the Fayen school under the ninth generation of Dajian (Mazu) was the one who first established the Fayen tradition (the calligraphy is identical to that of Yunmen).
An Yiren said: "It is like casting vessels from gold; the bell, the basin, the cauldron, and the tripod are all gold, yet the cauldron is not the bell."
A *yu* (basin) is not a *nai* (cauldron); their uses differ. Ganjiang and Moye are employed for cutting and slicing; Linji and Yunmen approximate this.
The precious mirror of the Qin palace is employed for comprehensive governance; Caodong, Guiyang, and Shishuang resemble this. Fayan, however, is the *ding* (tripod/cauldron). The *I Ching* says:
"The tripod breaks its feet and overturns the lord’s stew. This is because a tripod stands upon three legs; to lack one is to fail.
The first [aspect] is "inclining. Yantou [Huiqiu] likened it to the three dots of the character *yi* (一), which roughly resembles the approach of the Chan school.

Fayan [Wenyi], however, established the Six Aspects of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* as his school's fundamental tenet. His intention was profound, for he feared that students of later generations would become biased and limited by focusing on only one aspect.

These six aspects are: totality (*zong*), particularity (*bie*), sameness (*tong*), difference (*yi*), completion (*cheng*), and destruction (*huai*). Yet, totality is not particularity, and difference is not...

This is the same: they act as parent and child to one another, exhausting the vast nature of the Dharma-realm through the transformations of opening and closing, like a palindrome poem woven from silk—where a single character yields a hundred verses.
The complete body and great function of the Patriarchs were fully manifested once the Five Houses were established.
Xuan Sha’s school of thought possesses a functional application with an unchanging pivot, which corresponds to the six characteristics (*ṣaḍ-lakṣaṇa*).

The characteristics of meaning manifest and conceal one another. Master Facheng was exceptionally skilled in this, down to the time of Fayan, who exclusively employed this pedagogical device to engage others.
Thus, the Way of Xuansha reached its full maturity only with Fayan. However, students have failed to investigate this with meticulous care;
before many generations had passed, the *Zongjing* (Mirror of the Source) appeared, and exegetical śramaṇas relied upon it for their doctrines—a situation that is truly lamentable.
Chan Master Taihang Lingyao Ciji Zao, a descendant of Xuefeng’s lineage, passed away previously.
He was the son of the Mr. Weng of Xin’feng. His mother dreamed of a Buddhist monk of radiant and majestic spirit, carrying a mendicant’s staff and seeking lodging;

at the time of her conception, a fragrant mist filled the room. Initially, he engaged in the study and exposition of the teachings, but later he abandoned that path to visit Xuefeng. Xuefeng remarked of him, saying: “My son...”
On another day, he became the teacher of a king. A divine being offered him land, where he established the Dharma seat at Ruiyan (Auspicious Rock).

Two tigers attended by his side; in summer he wore paper garments, and in winter he bathed by striking the ice. People called him the "Ancient Buddha Who Strikes the Ice. Later, while residing at Lingyao, he ascended the hall and said:
"The fourfold assembly has gathered like clouds; what can this old monk say? He then descended from the seat. This is [the account].

In the winter of that year, the King of Min invited him into his inner hall to inquire about the Dharma. During the tea service, [the Master] first lifted up his bag and asked, "Does Your Majesty understand?
The King replied, "I do not. He said, "The King of Men and the King of Dharma each illuminate for themselves. He remained for ten days, then declined on the grounds of illness.
On the second day of the twelfth month, he bathed, ascended the hall, and passed away after addressing the assembly. His body was cremated, and auspicious signs appeared.
The light illuminated the mountains, and five-colored śarīras were obtained. He was posthumously titled Ciji (Compassionate Aid).
This occurred in the year Jichou (the fourth year of Tang Tiānchéng and the first year of Wú Tàihé), and again in the year Gengyin (the first year of Tang Chángxǐng).
The third generation descendant of Linji, Nanyuan (also known as Baoying) of Ruzhou, passed away [the *Gangmu* records this as the year Renzi, which is an error].

Before his passing, the Master ascended the hall and said: "Those in other quarters possess only the eye for the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching, but they do not possess the function of the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching.
A monk then asked: "What is the function of the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching? The Master replied: "A master does not peck and hatch."
"Simultaneous pecking and hatching—lost! [The monk] said, "This is still not where I was asking. The Patriarch asked, "How is it at the place where you were asking?
The monk said, "Lost. The Patriarch then struck him. That monk did not accept it. Later, while under the assembly of Yunmen, he heard two monks raise this story.
One monk said, "At that time, Nan-yuan’s staff must have broken! At this, the monk suddenly [realized].
Having attained realization, he hurried back to visit his master, only to find that the Master had already passed away. He then went to see Fengxue.

Upon seeing him, Fengxue immediately asked, "Monk, are you the one who at that time questioned the former Master about the saying, 'The chick and the hen peck at the same moment'? The monk replied, "I am.
Fengxue said, "How did you understand it then? The monk said, "At that time, I was as if in the shadow of a lamp."
The "Inner Practice" (Lixing) is similar [to this]. Xuexue said, "You understand.
Yang Yin remarked, "At the end of the Tang and during the Five Dynasties, the Bodhisattva King reigned over Jiangnan from Mount Jinzi;
the Buddha-dharma flourished greatly throughout Zhejiang and Fujian. It was only then that the 'lame-legged master' (Baizhang) first rose to prominence in Lingnan."
Furthermore, the Dharma-eye first set forth from Jiangyou, and herein the tradition of the Chan garden flourished most greatly.
Yet the Patriarch stood like a thousand-fathom cliff, remaining unmoving in either voice or expression; he sat with dignified composure, shaking the world through his presence.

Following the widespread dissemination of the "Chang-pai" (Song and Response) style by Dongshan and Tongan at Xinfeng, Fengyun and Tidaohua likewise followed the Way, their flowered balustrades and jade-like mechanisms [of teaching] being thus established.

He knew that the transmission and maintenance of the orthodox lineage did not reside in the formal arrangements of the monastic gate; rather, the true wind continued unbroken, beyond the reach of any name.
Master Yi resided at Chongshou Monastery.

The Patriarch resided at Chongshou Monastery in Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the entire world of the ten directions, all is brilliantly clear, without so much as a single thread.
If there were a single thread, it would remain a single thread."
The fourth-generation patriarch of Linji, whose name was Yanzhao, was the son of the Liu family of Yuhang. He attended Nan’uan for six years, after which Nan’uan passed away.
He then resided at Fengxue in Ruzhou.
The second year, the *xinmao* year.
The fourth generation of Linji, Zu (the Patriarch) Fengxue of Ruzhou, succeeded to the lineage (for forty-three years).
The Patriarch resided at Fengxue.
When the Patriarch was traveling to convert others, he arrived at the Ru River. He saw a few thatched-roofed huts nestled against a mountain, resembling the home of fugitives.
He asked a farmer, "What place is this? The farmer replied, "It is the ancient Fengxue Temple; it has been inhabited by those following the Vinaya, but the monks have passed away."
Furthermore, during a year of famine, the multitude abandoned him and departed; only the Buddha images, drums, and bells remained. The Patriarch said, "May I dwell here?
The farmer replied that it was permissible, and so the Patriarch stayed. During the day he begged for alms in the villages, and at night he burned pine resin for light.
He lived alone in this manner for seven years.
Xiangfu Yin said: "His lofty style is so serene that it can be clearly envisioned. To uphold the ancestral Way, how could it reside within the noisy gates and courtyards [of worldly fame]?
This was in the third year of the Renchen cycle."
The Sandalwood Buddha Image further traveled to Jiangnan.
There, Chan Master Hui-ling of Changqing, a descendant of Xuefeng Zhi, passed away.
Ling had propagated the Dharma in two locations, with a constant assembly of one thousand five hundred followers. His transformative influence spread through Min and Yue for twenty-seven years.
On the day of [the lunar month] in the fifth month, Chan Master Daokuang passed away. Dao Kuang was appointed as the supplementary abbot of Zhaoqing Monastery.
This was the year of Guisi (the fourth year of the Changxing era of the Tang dynasty; the first year of Longqi in Min).
Chan Master Chiru Ji, a descendant of Xuan Sha’s lineage, was the Hermit of Dazhang Mountain.
Having attained realization under Xuan Sha, he lived in seclusion on Xiajie Mountain, hollowing out a large, decayed cypress tree that could barely accommodate his body.
The Chan practitioners Qinghuo and Chongxu visited him together; they were so deeply moved by his lofty discourse that they did not realize night had fallen. Upon seeing—
The jackals and tigers rushed to the front of the hut and naturally circled it in a tame manner. Suddenly, there was a poem that said: "This journey is no ordinary one;
who knows the sentiments of going and staying? A single meal remains yet unsated; ten thousand households find no peace in living. That which is not the Way is difficult to subdue;
do not strive with empty fists. Where the dragon roars, the clouds arise; let out two or three idle cries. The two men sought [him].
He established a hermitage at Dayang and invited Ruru to reside there. He sat alone in both places for fifty-two years before his passing.
Xiangfu Yin said: "In ancient times, when people dwelt in mountain forests, even snakes and tigers were tamed; nowadays, people live in cities."
Those of the same kind become enemies; where, then, can the Way-mind be seen? Please try looking with your own eyes:
since things and self are already one body, how could there be two separate kinds? Outside the mind, no external objects remain; this is what may be called the Way.
The third generation of the Cao-Dong school, Tong’an Pizhu, ended his lineage here in this year (the year of his passing is not recorded in the *Yindu lu*;
therefore, the record is written in this manner).
The fourth patriarch of the Caodong school was named [Hui]zhi.
His birthplace is unknown. He succeeded Xian Tong’an.
The fourth-generation patriarch Fengqi of the Caodong lineage succeeded the dharma-lineage (for thirty years). [He is called Fengqi to distinguish him from the previous Tong’an.]
Formerly, when Ancestral Master Tong’an was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and said: "Before the Many-Sons Stupa, the lineage heirs are outstanding;
before the Five Elders’ Peak, what is the matter? He raised this three times, yet no one responded. Ancestral Master Fengxi stepped forward and said:
"Outside the curtain of night-brightness, they stand in their ranks; ten thousand miles of song and chant proclaim the Great Peace. The Master said: "I must have this donkey-man!"

It was first obtained in the year Jiawu (prior to the fourth month of the first year of Yingshun of Emperor Minding Tang Conghou, and subsequent to the first year of Qingtai of the deposed Emperor Congke; and the first year of Mingde of Meng Zhixiang, the ruler of Shu).
The Tang dynasty established the *shiseng* (examination for monks) system (the examination of monks began from this point).

The Office of Merit and Virtue submitted a memorial stating that the *chanding* (meditative concentration), *jiangjing* (scriptural exposition), *wenzhang yilun* (literary composition and debate), and *chinnian* (recitation and mantra-holding) examinations should be established to test monks.
The Emperor followed the proposal.
Chan Master Shijing lived in seclusion on Mount Tiantai.
When Shijing first visited Xuansha, he encountered the master addressing the assembly, saying:

"If you all can for a lifetime act as if you had lost your parents, I guarantee that you will attain thorough penetration. Shijing followed up on these words and asked: "As it says in the scriptures..."
"One must not use the mind of one's own knowledge to gauge the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed wisdom and insight. [Zhaozhou] asked, "And how about this?
Sandi replied, "If you say you have thoroughly investigated it to the very bottom, can that mind of knowledge still manage to gauge it? From this point on, Jing gained faith and entered the Way.
Later, he resided at Mount Tiantai for over thirty years without descending the mountain. He extensively mastered the three studies and maintained exemplary conduct.

Living in seclusion, during his intervals from meditative stillness, he constantly perused the Dragon Canon (*Nāga-kośa*). He was held in high esteem by those both far and near, and was commonly known as the Venerable Dajing.
Once, someone asked him: "Disciple, whenever I sit in meditation at night, my thoughts fly about in confusion. I do not yet understand the method for subduing them;
I pray that you will deign to grant me instruction. Jing replied: "If, while sitting peacefully at night, your thoughts fly about in confusion, then..."
Take this scattering mind and investigate the place where it scatters. When you investigate and find no such place, then where does the thought of scattering exist?
Turn back and investigate the investigating mind itself; then where is the mind that performs the investigation?

Furthermore, the wisdom that illuminates is fundamentally empty, and the objects upon which it depends are likewise quiescent. That they are "quiescent yet not quiescent" is because there is no person who can bring about this quiescence.

Furthermore, that which "illuminates yet does not illuminate" refers to the absence of any objective realm to be illuminated. When both object and wisdom are quiescent, the mind and its deliberations are at ease.
One does not seek out external branches, nor does one dwell in internal concentration. When these two paths are both extinguished, the single nature is serene.
This is the essential path for returning to the source. At that time, there was also the Venerable Sengjing, who was then known as "Duo Jing" (Two Jings).
He sat [in meditation] and passed away at Tiantai.
This was in the year Yiwu (the second year of Qingtai and the first year of Wutianzhu; 935 CE).

It was the year Bingshen (after the eleventh month of the third year of Qingtai, following the first year of Tianfu under Emperor Gaozu Shi Jingtang of Jin, and the first year of Tongwen under the ruler of Min, Wang Chang; prior to the Jin era, this was called the seventh year of Changxing; 936–937 CE).
In the year Dingyou (the second year of the Tianfu era of the Jin dynasty and the first year of Shengyuan of Emperor Xugao, the founding ruler of Southern Tang),
the Daochang at Fengxue was completed, and the Governor of Ruzhou invited the Master to open the hall for formal instruction.
The Provincial Governor offered full courtesy and requested that he open the Dharma. On the first day of the New Year, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"The former Master said, 'If you wish to attain intimacy, do not come with questions. Do you understand? The question is where the answer lies; the answer is where the question lies.
Even so, there are times when the question is not where the answer lies, and the answer is not where the question lies. If you attempt to deliberate upon this, I, the old monk..."
It is right beneath your heels. Generally speaking, the eyes of one who studies the Way must manifest great function directly before you;
do not confine yourself to minor details. Even if you gain realization prior to words, you still remain stuck in the shell and mired in obscurity.

Even if you master the meaning within the phrases, you cannot avoid wild views wherever you encounter them. This is surely because you have hitherto relied on others for your interpretations, resulting in a state of partial clarity and confusion.
"Both branches—sweep them all away with you! I shall make each one like a lion cub, yawning and gaping, to testify before the assembly.
With a single roar, standing tall as a thousand fathoms, who would dare look upon him with a direct eye?
To look is to blind their own eyes."
Chan Master Xingnian arrived at Fengxue.
Xingnian was the son of the Di family from Lai Prefecture. He was a man of simple gravity and refined discernment who specialized in the practice of dhūta austerities.

As soon as he had received full ordination, he traveled extensively among monastic communities. He constantly recited the Lotus Sūtra in private, and consequently, the assembly came to call him "Nian Fahua" (Lotus-Reciting Nian).

Upon arriving at Fengxue, he served as the guest prefect (*zhikè*). He lived and worked in accordance with the community, yet he never engaged in formal inquiry or consultation. Nevertheless, he harbored a persistent doubt that there was a distinct transmission of the ultimate meaning outside the teachings.
At that time, Daofu of Longce, a descendant of Chan Master Xuefeng, had passed away.
Xuanfu himself moved from Jingqing to Tianlong. Upon seeing him, the Prince of Wuyue remarked, "A true man of the Way.
He further established Longce Monastery and invited him to reside there. Disciples gathered like clouds. On the [blank] day of the eighth month, he passed away.
Chan Master Deshao attained enlightenment at Chongshou Temple and subsequently went to Tiantai.
Deshao was the son of the Chen family of Longquan; his mother dreamed that a white light touched her body, and upon waking, she became pregnant.

When he was fifteen years old, a foreign monk patted him on the back and said, "You shall leave the household life; there is no place for you amidst the dust of the world. Thereupon, he shaved his head.
Having received full ordination, he traveled extensively to visit fifty-four spiritual mentors (kalyāṇamitras), staying with each for only a short time.
Later, he arrived at Linchuan to pay his respects to the Patriarch Chongshou. Upon seeing him, the Patriarch held him in high esteem.

Because Shao had already traversed the various monastic communities, he merely followed the general assembly and had nothing further to inquire about or consult. One day, someone asked him: "What is a single drop from the Cao River source?"
"Water," the Patriarch said. "This is a single drop from the source of Cao. At these words, Huishao attained a sudden and great enlightenment by his side;
the doubts and obstructions of his life were dissolved like melting ice.

Moved to tears that soaked his robes, the Patriarch said, "In the future, you shall serve as a teacher to kings, causing the ancestral Way to shine with great brilliance. Go now, and let there be no hindrance. Thereupon, Huishao took his leave and traveled to Mount Tiantai.
Observing the traces left by the Wise One, they were as if he were still residing there; with lingering affection, they felt a heart resolved to dwell there for the rest of their lives.
The śramaṇa Qiji of Mount Heng was a descendant of the Hu clan from Yiyang.
He left the household life at Daming Mountain, where he upheld the Vinaya and was devoted to poetic composition. Having sought out the Gate of Virtue, he... [sent forth his resolve].
Wu, Yaoqiao, and Shichuang all sought his instruction extensively. Later, while traveling through Jingzhu, he was detained by Jie Du Ji-xing at Longxing Temple.
This was not his true aspiration. He had a goiter on his neck, for which he was popularly known as "The Sack of Poetry."
He loved mountains and rivers and was weary of seeking audiences with officials. He possessed the line: "I have never once brought a single word to easily seek an audience with feudal lords.
He exchanged verses with Zheng Gu, a recluse of Mount Hua. Later, he resided at Jingu Temple on Western Mountain, where his *Bailian ji* (White Lotus Collection) circulated in the world.
He styled himself the Śramaṇa of Mount Heng. (In the late Ming dynasty, Mao Jin of Yinhu in Haiyu carved [this collection], including Qingzhou, Guanyi, and Zhuyu.)
The *Shan Chan Yue Bai Lian Ji* (Mountains, Meditation, Moon, White Lotus Collection), titled the *Poetry Collection of Three Eminent Monks of the Tang*, circulated in the world.

[It was compiled during] the Wuxu year (the third year of Tianfu in the Shu region, the first year of Guangzheng) and the Jihai year (the fourth year of Tianfu in the Min region, the first year of Yonglong).
The year of Gengzi (the fifth year of Tianfu). The year of Xinchou (the sixth year of Tianfu).
The year of Rentyin (the seventh year of Tianfu; the Han ruler was Bian, whose reign title was Guangtian Yuan).

The year of Gui Mao (the eighth year of Tianfu of the Jin dynasty; the first year of Baoyouan of Emperor Jing of Southern Tang; the first year of Tianfu of Wang Yanzheng, the ruler of Yin; and the first year of Qianhe of the ruler of Nanzhao).
Yizhu had moved from Ba’en to Qingliang.
The Ruler of Jinling personally invited him from Chongshou to reside at Ba’en, but before long, he moved again to Qingliang. Addressing the assembly, he said:
Zhaozhou said, "Do not exert effort. These are indeed excellent words. Why not simply continue as before?

Even in worldly dharmas there are gateways; how could the Buddha-dharma lack gateways? Since you do not continue as before, the Buddhas and Patriarchs have attained [enlightenment] solely within the state of continuing as before.
It is like the midnight bell: not a single hair’s breadth of difference is seen. To attain it in such a way is precisely right."

Excellent. When hearing occurs, there is not a single sound that is disturbed. Why? Because it accords with the proper timing. That which is called "death" when the mind is absent is not actually death;
it merely comes to rest within all things. It is simply because one does not remain as before that, suddenly and unexpectedly, the time for hearing arrives.
Everyone was utterly astonished, saying, "The bell is sounding strangely. Furthermore, it would not do to say today that midsummer is gradually becoming hot;
for although only one day has passed, how could there be much difference? To say this on the first day of the fifth month would be a deception;
you must know that one cannot differ by even a hair's breadth. Within these skillful means, I tell the Venerable One: it is not so.

At that time, "the moment" (shi) is merely a deceptive lure; therefore, one does not revert to the old ways. Master Baogong said: "If you can for a moment accept things as they are and cease seeking, how could there have been anything different throughout kalpas from this very day?
Do you understand? This very day is nothing other than the dust of kalpas. Simply wear your robes and eat your meals; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down;
whether attending morning inquiry or evening consultation—let everything remain as it was. This is precisely what it means to be a person of no affairs."
Furthermore, the verse on "The Three Realms are Mind Only" states: The three realms are mind only; all phenomena are consciousness only.

Consciousness only and mind only—sights for the eye, sounds for the ear. Color does not reach the ear; how could sound touch the eye? Through the eye and color, the ear and sound, all phenomena are accomplished.
If all phenomena were not dependent on conditions, how could they be observed as being like illusions? Of the great earth, mountains, and rivers, what is solid and what changes? *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*
The Verse on the Meaning of the Six Characteristics states: In the *Avataṃsaka*’s meaning of the six characteristics, within identity there is still difference.

If difference were distinct from identity, it would entirely fail to accord with the intent of the Buddhas. In the intent of the Buddhas—of the universal and the particular—how could there ever be identity or difference?
When entering meditative concentration within a male body, one does not dwell upon the female body. Not dwelling upon it means cutting off names and words; thus are the ten thousand phenomena.
The principle of luminous non-existence.

Jiachen (the first year of the Kaoyun era of the Jin Prince Chonggui). The *Jiu Tang Shu* was completed (compiled by Grand Master Liu Xu, including records of the extraordinary traces of the Buddhas and patriarchs).
The year of Yi-si (the second year of Kaoyun). The year of Bing-wu (the third year of Kaoyun).

The year of Ding-wei (after the second month of the fourth year of Kaoyun; the Later Han High Ancestor Liu Hao entered Bian and continued to use the ninth year of Tianfu; the fifth year of Qianhe of Liu Sheng of the Han in Lingnan).

In the year Wushen (the first year of Qianyou of Emperor Liu Yan of the Han dynasty, and the sixth year of Qianhe of Liu Sheng of the Han), the Patriarch entrusted the province with the mindfulness of the True Dharma.

The Patriarch often reflected that there was a prophecy concerning Dayang, stating that the Linji school would come to an end with Feng. He feared he might be the one destined by this prediction and pondered it deeply.
He surveyed those beneath him who were capable of carrying on the Way of the Dharma and found none equal to Nan.
One day, while Nan was standing in attendance, the Patriarch shed tears and said, "It is unfortunate that the Way of Linji is about to fall to the ground upon reaching me. Nan replied:

"Observing this assembly, are there no people here? The Master said, "Those who are clever and intelligent are many; those who have realized their nature are few. Huineng asked, "As for someone like me, what of him?
The Master said, "Although I have long looked forward to you, I fear you may still be attached to this scripture and unable to let it go.
Huineng said, "This is indeed a matter of concern. I wish to hear its essential point. Thereupon, the Master ascended the hall.
The World-Honored One raised his blue-lotus eyes and gazed upon the great assembly. At that very moment, tell me:
what did he say? If you say he spoke without speaking, you are once again burying the ancient sages. Before he had finished speaking, Huineng stepped down from the seat.
When the Patriarch returned to the abbot’s quarters, the attendant said, "Why did Huineng not respond to the Master?"
He said, "He understands. The next day, while Nanquan was visiting with the head gardener Zhen to pay their respects, the Patriarch asked Zhen, "What is the Buddha’s 'unspeakable speaking'?
Zhen replied, "The magpie cries atop the tree. The Patriarch said, "Why do you perform such foolish meritorious acts?
Why do you not investigate the meaning of these words? He then asked Nanquan, "As for you..."
Nian said, "To manifest the ancient path through one's countenance is not to fall into the mechanism of silent stillness.
The Patriarch said to Zhen, "Why do you not look at Nian’s commentary on the *Lotus Sūtra*? On another day, as the Patriarch ascended the seat and surveyed the assembly, Nian immediately descended.
When the Patriarch returned to his quarters, Nian thereafter vanished from view and concealed his brilliance; no one knew where he had gone.
One day, Bai Zhao (Baiyun Zhaoguo) arrived at Xuanhua in Ruizhou. Yuan'an (Zhaozhou Nanquan Puyuan) now remembered to send a message to him.
As soon as they met, [Nanquan] held up his sitting mat and asked: "When it is spread out, what is it? When it is not spread out, what is it?
Zhao said: "Look for yourself. Nanquan then gave a shout. Zhao said: "I have personally attended upon teachers of wisdom; I have never dared to act in such a manner."
In the midst of the confusion, Huian said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. Changchou said, "If I see Master Fengxue tomorrow, I shall recount this to him in detail.
Huian said, "Do as you wish; just do not forget it. Huian then returned first and recounted the matter to the Patriarch (Fengxue).
The Patriarch said, "Today you have captured another grass-robber. Huian said, "A truly skilled hand!"
He did not spread his reputation. The following day, when Chu arrived and met him, he brought up the previous conversation.

Linji said, "Not only yesterday; today I have caught you red-handed with the stolen goods. From that time on, his name was celebrated throughout all quarters. Linji then transmitted the True Dharma to him.

(When Linji was taking leave of Guishan, Yangshan was attending at his side. Guishan asked Yangshan, "As for this man’s future path of the Dharma, what will become of it? Yangshan replied, "This man’s future path of the Dharma will flourish greatly in the regions of Wu and Yue. He will encounter...")

The wind immediately ceased. Guishan asked again, "Who will be his successor? Yangshan replied, "There is indeed one, but because the time has been so long, I do not wish to name him to you, Master. Guishan pressed him further, saying, "I also wish to know.

Yangshan said, "Does the Sutra not say: 'Offer this very body and mind to every dust-mote world; this is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness'? It is through this that one knows Xingnian was the later incarnation of Yangshan."

Xiangfu Yin said: "Although the Way does not reside solely in outward practice, one who has not attained stability and density in their conduct cannot fully uphold the Great Dharma of the World-Honored One.

As for those whom the Buddha entrusted with his final instructions—those venerable ones of ascetic practice—and as for the Patriarchs who were able to scrutinize and restore the thread of the lineage on the verge of collapse, none can compare to those who diligently cultivate the dhūta practices and contemplate the *Lotus Sūtra*. This is what can be seen in the transmission."
The power of the Way lies in cultivation and realization. It is like a precious ship: when it catches the wind, it travels a thousand li in an instant.
Yet, if one cultivates and realizes without clarifying the Way, that effort belongs to defilement. This is why Nanyue said: "Cultivation and realization are not non-existent;
however, defilement is not permissible. With a profound mind, he traversed lands as numerous as motes of dust, vowing to return once more—Daguan.
He may truly be called one who repays the Buddha’s kindness.
Chan Master Shouchu first resided at Dongshan.
When he first visited Master Yunmen, the Master asked, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Chadu. The Master then asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat?"
[The Master] said, "From Baoci in Hunan. [The monk] said, "When did you leave there? [The monk] said, "On the twenty-fifth of the eighth month.

[The Master] said, "I grant you three blows of the staff. At first, [the monk] was bewildered; on the following day, he went up to pay his respects and asked, "Yesterday I received the Master’s three blows of the staff;
I do not know where my fault lay. [The Master] said, "You rice-bag! In Jiangxi and Hunan, they simply act like this."
"How can one go? At these words, he attained great enlightenment. He then said, "In the future, I shall dwell in a place where there is no human habitation;

I will not store a single grain of rice nor plant a single stalk of vegetable. I will receive those who come and go from the ten directions and for them all extract their nails and pull out their wedges.
I will strip away their 'burnt-fat' hats and cast off their 'vulture-stench' cloth robes, so that they may be free and easy."
"To be a monk of non-action—how joyful that would be! [The Master] said, "Your body is as small as a coconut, yet you open such a wide mouth.
At this, [the man] immediately prostrated himself and departed that very day. He traveled north to Xianghan and resided at Dongshan.
Addressing the assembly: Words do not manifest the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who follow words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded.
The Patriarch himself, Fengxue, avoided the disturbances by traveling to Yingzhou.
The Prefectural Governor, Yanzu, ascended the seat in the prefectural study hall and said: "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox:
when it moves, it is sealed; when it stays still, it is broken. But as for neither moving nor staying still—is it sealing?
Is it not sealing? Is there anyone who can say? At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked: "I, a student..."

"You possess the mechanism of the iron ox; I request that you do not merely apply the seal. The Patriarch said, "One accustomed to fishing for whales and leviathans in vast depths, yet pities the frog-like stride mired in the mud and sand.
[The monk] poured forth his thoughts. The Patriarch shouted, "Elder, why do you not proceed with your words?"
When Baishan Pei was about to deliberate upon his response, Guishan Zuxiu struck him once with his whisk and asked, "Do you still remember the point of the teaching?
As Pei was about to open his mouth, Zuxiu struck him again with the whisk. At that moment, the Prefect said, "I now know that the Buddha-dharma and the royal law are one and the same.
Zuxiu asked, "What principle have you seen? The Prefect replied, "If one hesitates to act when it is time to decide, it will instead invite chaos."
The Patriarch then descended from the seat.
In the year Jǐyǒu (the second year of Qiānyòu of the Later Hàn, the first year of Qiánhé of Nánhàn Shèng), he established the Yunmén school as its first patriarch;
the Great Compassionate Cloud Kuāngzhēn Hóngmíng Patriarch entered nirvana.

When the Patriarch resided at Yunmen, the Lord of Guangzhou served him with the utmost sincerity. On the tenth day of the fourth month, after delivering his final instructions, he sat upright and passed away.
An Yinyin remarked, "Yunmen’s preaching was divinely bestowed; he was like a newborn colt that refuses to accept the bit and bridle."
Truly, he was the Great King of Physicians who opened the school and established the beginning. Deshan said: "When there are words, one seizes the tiger’s head and gathers its tail;
beneath the first phrase, the fundamental principle is clarified. When there are no words, the sharp point of the faculty is exposed, like a flash of lightning or a stroke of a whisk.
Yantou and Xuefeng extensively expounded and illuminated this, until it reached Yunmen, along with Xuansha and Luoshan.
His lineage became increasingly profound, subtle, and esoteric. At that time, when someone asked Wuzu Yan, "What is the matter of the Yunmen school? he replied, "The red banner flashes.
This likely indicates that he had attained the very marrow of both Muzhou and Xuefeng. Regarding his disciples, he refined and forged them so as to transcend both the holy and the mundane;
all emotional views were utterly cleansed, leaving not even a trace of attachment. For this reason, he succeeded to their Dharma.
There were more than seventy such individuals. As they approached the threshold of life and death, it was as if a gate had opened before them; most passed away while sitting in meditation.
Among them, the four elders Deshan Mi, Dongshan Chu, Xianglin Yuan, and Baling Jian were those who transcended their peers.

When Dongshan Chu addressed the assembly, he said: "Words do not unfold the reality of things; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded."
The Yunmen tradition is generally like this.
In the gengxu year (the third year of Qianyou; it was in this year that the Han dynasty fell), and in the xinhai year (the first year of Guangshun of Emperor Taizu Guo Wei of the Later Zhou).
One thousand nine hundred years after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, by imperial decree, the new temple in Ruzhou was granted the name Guanghui.

His ancestors had fled to Yingzhou to avoid bandits; once the rebellion was quelled, a man surnamed Song and holding the rank of Grand Preceptor (Taishi) of the Song dynasty donated his residence [to the temple].
