[The Master] said, "I was just speaking with a guest; why are you laughing? [The Guest] replied, "I am laughing because your eye of wisdom as a guest-in-charge is not yet upright, and your discernment of dharmas is not clear.
Xian said, "Is there a saying for this? The Guest answered with a verse: "A single hare lies across the ancient road."
As soon as the gray falcon saw him, it seized him alive. Later, the hunting dogs lacked any spiritual nature; they searched in vain at the site of the old withered stump.
Xianyin was extraordinary; he formed a friendship with him. Traveling north, he went to Futang in Fuzhou to visit Guangzuo.
He immediately extended his inquiry, saying, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, how can there be transgression? Guangzuo called for Xian to come forward. Xian...
Just as he drew near, Fazu struck him across the mouth with his whisk. Xian was about to open his mouth when Fazu struck him again.
Xian attained sudden enlightenment and remained for five years, mastering the Way in its entirety.
The seventh year was Jiǎyǐn; the eighth year was Yǐmǎo; the ninth year was Bǐngchén;
and the first year of Tiānxī was Dìngyǐ.
During this time, Chan Master Chǔyuán received the patriarch’s transmission and instructions to go to Dòngshān to serve as the First Seat.

Yuan had served for seven years. When he and his peers, including Shizhi, took their leave of the Patriarch, the Patriarch said, "This journey cannot be measured by the number of years since your ordination.
Listen to my verse: 'The sky has no head; outside the city walls of Jizhou, spears and halberds rise.
A general passes through the forest on a single horse; inside the city walls of Yuanzhou, there is a clamor. Yuan suddenly stepped forward from the ranks and asked, "What about Chu-yuan?"
"How could anyone dare to receive such a prediction from the Master? The Patriarch instructed him, saying, "I personally realized samādhi under my former teacher;
you have now attained it as well. You should go to the south and greatly propagate my Way.
Previously, the Patriarch had said to Yuan, "I have traveled everywhere visiting the descendants of Yunmen, yet I have harbored a regret for not having seen Cong. Yuan then [related] his mother's...
Lao then took his leave of the Patriarch and returned to Jūn Prefecture. On the way, he visited Tángmíng Sōng, with whom he found a profound resonance in their exchange of insights;
subsequently, he went to Dòngshān, where Cóng invited him to occupy the seat of the First Seat upon ascending the hall.
An-yin Ren said: "Among the seventy-one seekers of true knowledge who visited Fenzhou, they still harbored regret for not having met Master Cong.
Since Ciming had already realized the Way that transcends emotion, he further relied upon Cong for three years; this can be called the 'convergence of a hundred rivers into the sea.
Thus, it is no wonder he was held in such high esteem by his contemporaries."
The second year, Wumǔ (978).
Chan Master Shǒuzhī resided at Dàgū.
Having personally received the mind-seal of Fényáng, Zhī took his leave to travel south and settled at Dàgū in Gāo'ān. A monk asked: "As for suchness..."
"What is the Buddha? Zhi said, "A saw cutting a weight.
Later, Chan Master Chongxian appeared in the world at Cuifeng.
Having attained the gate of wisdom for himself, he then traveled extensively to visit various masters, including Dongshan, Dazhu Huihai, Nanyue Huairang, and Dayu.
The Patriarchal Master (Zongzhang) Chanhui, a former scholar-official, was on close terms with Xian. While they were meeting by the Huai River, Chanhui asked Xian where he was going.
Xian replied, "I intend to travel to Qiantang, cross Westing, and ascend Mount Tiantai and Yandang. Chanhui said, "Lingyin is a most excellent place in the world;
Master Shan is an old friend of mine. He then wrote a letter of recommendation for Xian. Xian arrived at Lingyin and remained there for three years.
Sunken among the multitude like land submerged by water, he suddenly encountered Zonghui while on an official mission to Western Zhejiang.

He went to visit Xian at Lingyin Monastery, but no one recognized him. At that time, there were over a thousand monks in the hall; the envoy’s officials searched through the bedding and examined various items until they finally found him.

The envoy asked about the letter he had previously entrusted to him. Xian tucked it into his sleeve and said, "Your honor’s intent is earnest; however, as a wandering monk, I have no worldly desires. How could I dare—"
"How rare is this recommendation! Huì laughed heartily. Shàn was struck by his insight. When the seat at Cui Fēng on Wú Jiāng became vacant, he was appointed as the abbot;
he burned incense and became a Dharma heir of Běi Tǎ.
Shending Yin preached the *Prajñāpāramitā* Sūtras.
Residing at Shending, his austere simplicity was beyond compare; he had but a single bed of withered wood upon which he sat at night.
About thirty people would sit in a circle to listen to his instructions. A śramaṇa from Zhidu Temple named Benyan visited Yin and spoke with him at night; upon returning, he said:
The Prefect said, "Master Yin is what is called a 'venerable elder of true substance. It is a pity that he has remained submerged in the mountains.

I wish to invite him with due ceremony to open a Dharma seat. Yin declined, but could not refuse. He then ascended the seat and preached the Dharma; both monastics and laypeople cheered and cried out, "We have never before experienced such a thing!
Thereupon, Yin’s fame spread far and wide.
In the third year, Jiwei,
and the fourth year, Gengshen,
Chan Master Chuyuan opened the Dharma at Nanyuan.
Yuan served as the head of the assembly at Dongshan for three years before departing to travel to Yangshan.
Yang Yi sent a letter to Huang Zongdan, the Governor of Yichun, requesting that Yuan be appointed to propagate the Dharma at Nanyuan.

Chan Master Fayuan came to Taiyang to receive the patriarch’s entrustment (Yuan came to Taiyang; because this concerns the Dharma-lineage of the Dong lineage, the word "to" [zhì] is used, a term expressing joy).
Yuan first visited Sanjiao Song, then visited Fenzhou, and subsequently visited Yexian to receive the transmission of the seal of enlightenment (*kaji*).

During the Tianxi era, he traveled through Xianghan and reached Taiyang in Yingzhou, where his words were in accord with those of Master Zu. Under Master Zu’s assembly, there were two monks named Cheng and Pou who had both passed away previously;
Master Zu sighed that there was no one to succeed the Dongshan lineage and wished to entrust [the dharma] to him.
Huiyuan addressed the Great Master with a formal request for transmission. The Master said, "I am old.
Will the lineage of Dongshan finally have no one to carry it forward? He then showed him the cassock and leather sandals he had worn throughout his life.
Huiyuan said, "I shall take these robes and sandals and seek someone to whom you may entrust them. The Master instructed him, saying, "In the future..."
"If you succeed in finding such a person, bring forth my verse as proof. The verse said: "The grass before Mount Yangguang— Entrust it to you to wait for its price to be set.
Where the strange sprouts flourish most luxuriantly, The profound and secret roots remain firm and numinous. At the end of the writing, he added:
"One who has attained the Dharma must remain hidden from the assembly for ten years before they may propagate it. Yuan then bowed in reverence, accepted his instructions, and departed.
Hegelinn Mon said: "Tàiyáng was strict in purifying the source of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; Yuǎnɡōng was generous in protecting the lineage of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

I have often marveled that when these two elders encountered the extraordinary amidst the ordinary and the transformative, each possessed a subtle and profound intention within them to rectify the Dharma-gate.
Had it not been for Tàiyáng, Yuǎnɡōng would not have been inspired."
Regarding this profound sense of righteousness: were it not for Master Yuanyang, the heavy trust of the Great Sun could not have been fulfilled.
Thus, his lofty character and austere virtue remain preserved to this day. Alas! The hearts of the ancients are truly difficult to emulate.

The single word "generation" (dai)—which the ancients used to exclude the profane—is now used by the present generation to open the door to the profane. How vast is the difference between them, as distant as heaven and the abyss!
Xiangfu Yin said: "People of ancient and modern times do not reach one another; it is the times that make them so.

Those of antiquity clearly perceived the junctures of the waxing and waning of the Dharma-vehicle, and thus they did not hesitate to be strict in order to prevent its abuse. Those of today truly recognize the gravity of maintaining continuity;
therefore, they cannot help but act as their successors to preserve its lineage. In sum, this arises from a perspective on the Way of the Dharma."
Yet there is no need to concern oneself with what lies between them.
In the fifth year of the Xinyou era,
the Dharma Master Shengchang of the Tiantai school was reborn in the Pure Land.

Chang, whose courtesy name was Zaowei, resided at Zhaoqing Monastery during the Chunhua era. Admiring the tradition of Mount Lu, he renamed the Lotus Society as the Pure Conduct Society (Jingxing She).
He formed this society with scholar-officials, headed by Prime Minister Wang Dan.
At that time, one hundred and twenty high-ranking officials, provincial governors, and other dignitaries, along with one thousand bhikṣus, all styled themselves disciples of the Pure Conduct Society.
On a day in the first month, he sat upright in meditation reciting the Buddha’s name. After a short while, he called out in a forceful voice, "The Buddha has come! and passed away peacefully.
The assembly saw that the ground had turned entirely golden, and it remained so for some time before finally fading away.
In the first year of the Qiánxìng era (964), the Dharma Master of the Tiantai school, Fǎhuì Zhīyuán of Gūshān, passed away.
Yuán’s courtesy name was Wúwài; he was styled Zhōngyōngzǐ and also called Qiánfū. He transmitted the Tiantai school to Qīng of Fèngxiān.
He resided on Gushan Island in the West Lake and was a friend of Lin Hejing of Chuzhou.

When Wang Qinruo was sent out to govern Qiantang, Ciyun dispatched a messenger to invite Yuan to go together to welcome him. Yuan smiled and said to the messenger, "On the borders of Qiantang, there is currently one monk staying;
he has long been afflicted by a wasting disease and calls himself a sick man. As for lecturing on the Way or composing poetry..."
Once, feeling weary, he cautioned his disciples in advance, saying: "After my death, do not provide me with a lavish funeral; do not erect a stupa to misrepresent me;
do not petition those in high office for an inscription to falsely glorify me. It would be appropriate to bury me in two joined earthenware vessels.
Simply set up a stone to record my name, dates, and year. On the seventeenth day of the second month, he passed away at the age of forty.

Seventh: His disciples followed his instructions. Fifteen years later, after heavy rains caused a mountain slope to collapse, the disciples opened the earthenware vessel to find that the physical body was intact;
the nails and hair had both grown long. They then dressed him in new robes and reinterred him.
He was prolific in his writings and was posthumously titled Dharma Master Fahui.
Emperor Renzong (personal name Zhen; reigned for forty-one years).
In the first year of Tiānshèng, the Gui-hài year, Nanyuan Yuan visited Shending.
Yuan resided at Nanyuan for three years and then departed. He went to visit Shending Yin;

at that time, Yin’s reputation was preeminent, and among the monks, none of ordinary caliber dared to enter his gate. He had lived on the mountain for thirty years, and his disciples’ prestige eclipsed that of all other quarters.
Yuan did not cut his hair long, wore tattered robes, and spoke with a Chu accent; when he came to announce his arrival, he addressed himself as a "Dharma nephew. One—
The assembly laughed loudly. Yuanzhen sent a novice to ask, "Venerable sir, whose successor are you? Yuan looked up at the roof and said, "I saw Fenyang in person.
Yuanzhen came out leaning on his staff; seeing Yuan’s tall and imposing figure, he asked, "Is there a 'Lion of West River' in Fenzhou?
Yuan pointed behind him and shouted, "The roof is collapsing! The novice fled back, and Yuanzhen turned to look.
Looking back, Yuan looked alert and vigorous; he sat down on the ground, shed one shoe, and gazed at Yi. Yi forgot what he had been asking and lost sight of Yuan’s location.
Yuan rose slowly, adjusted his robes, and as he walked away, said, "Seeing the person is not as good as hearing of their reputation.
He then departed. Yi sent someone to pursue him, but could not catch him. He sighed, saying, "Fenzhou has such a son!"
From this point on, his reputation grew weighty within the monastic forests.
Cui-feng Xian moved to reside at Xue-dou.
Once Zeng-hui took charge of Si-ming, he invited Xian to reside at Xue-dou. Upon his arrival, the style of his school flourished greatly, and he became a dragon among the world’s [monks].
Disciples as eminent as the coiled phoenix gathered at his seat, and he was hailed as the restorer of the Yunmen lineage.

When the founding ancestor of the Linji sixth generation, the Patriarch of Fenzhou, passed away, Li Hou, the Governor of Longde Prefecture, invited him to preside over Chengtian Monastery; however, although the messenger returned three times with the invitation, he did not go, and the messenger was consequently punished.

The messenger returned and said, "He insists that you must go with him; otherwise, he will simply die. Nanyue Zuzhao laughed and said, "I am old and ill, and have already vowed not to leave the mountain.
If you insist on going, we shall proceed one after the other; why must we go together? The messenger replied, "If the Master agrees, you may choose whether to go first or last as you see fit.
Nanyue then ordered food to be prepared, began packing his belongings, and addressed the assembly, saying, "The old monk is leaving."
[The Master asked: "Who can follow me? A monk stepped forward and said, "I can follow you. The Patriarch asked, "How many li do you travel in a day?
The monk replied, "Fifty li. The Patriarch said, "You cannot follow me. Another monk stepped forward and said, "I can follow you.
The Patriarch asked, "How many li do you travel in a day? The monk replied, "Seventy li. The Patriarch said, "You [also cannot follow me]."
"I cannot follow you," [the Master] said. The attendant came forward and said, "I can follow him; wherever the Preceptor goes, I shall go there as well.
The Patriarch replied, "Then you can indeed follow this old monk. Having said this, he told the attendant, "I shall go on ahead first.
He set down his chopsticks and passed away. The attendant immediately attained parinirvāṇa on the spot. They performed the cremation, collected the *śarīra*, and erected a stupa.
Chronological History of the Patriarchal Lineage, Scroll Nineteen;
Chronological History of the Patriarchal Lineage, Scroll Twenty;
The Seventh Patriarch of the Linji Lineage.
His taboo name was Chuyuan. He was the son of the Li family of Qingxiang in Quanzhou and succeeded Fenyang.

In the second year of the Tiānshèng era (1024), the year Jiazi of Emperor Rénzōng’s reign, he became the seventh-generation successor in the Linji lineage as the Dharma heir of Zǔzōng Címíng of Shīshuāng in Tánzhōu (for seventeen years).
When National Teacher Zu resided at Daowu, Chan Master Fanghui assisted him.
The śramaṇa Benyan of Dinglin possessed spiritual practice and was highly esteemed and respected by scholars and officials.
Shending praised Benyan’s insight to the effect that he could revitalize the Linji school. When the seat at Daowu became vacant, Benyan petitioned the local magistrate.
He was appointed as the Abbot. His administration of the laws and regulations was strict and solemn, and those who were willing to sacrifice their lives for the Dharma gathered there.

He moved from Nanyuan to Daowu and then to Shishuang; at all these locations, his assembly assisted him in overseeing the affairs of the monastery. Once, ascending the hall, he said: "A single shout distinguishes guest and host."
"Enlightenment and function operate simultaneously; one must grasp the meaning within this. At midday, he strikes the third watch. Then, letting out a shout, he said:
"Tell me, is this the guest or the host? Is there anyone who can distinguish them?
If you can distinguish them, I shall give you three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred in the evening. If you cannot, I, the old monk, have lost face."
The third year was Yi-chu; the fourth year was Bing-yin;
the fifth year was Ding-mao.
In the fifth year, the sixth patriarch of the Cao-dong school, Danyang Zu of Yingzhou, passed away.
On the sixteenth day of the seventh month, the Master took leave of the assembly. Three days later, he sent a verse to Minister Wang Shu and passed away while his pen was still resting.
He was eighty-five years old.

Investigation and Verification: (According to the records, the seventh patriarch of the Dong lineage, Touzi Qing, returned to Longshu in the sixth year of the Xining era. Monastics and laypeople requested that he reside at Haikai Temple in Baixue;

calculating from the year he received the Dharma until this point, exactly ten years had passed, thereby fulfilling the prophecy of Dayang. This indicates that when Patriarch Touzi Qing received the Dharma from Fushan, it was during the early years of the Zhiting era of Emperor Yingzong. He succeeded to the lineage in that very year.

From the fifth year of the Tiansheng era to the *guimao* year, the eighth year of the Jiayu era, there were thirty-seven intermediate years during which the lineage of the Dongshan school was absent. These facts are clear in the historical records. This is recorded here to preserve the truth).
In the sixth year, the Wuchen year [968], Dharma Master Xingzong Fazhi Zhili of Yanqing in Siming passed away.
Zhili had transmitted the Tiantai teachings to Baoyun Tong, who resided at Chengtian and later moved to Yanqing; his disciples gathered there like a forest. Daily...
The National Preceptor was dispatched by His Majesty to inquire about the essentials of the Dharma.

He composed the *Zhiyao miaozong ercao* (Two Commentaries on the Essential and Subtle Principles), the *Dabei chan yi* (Ritual for the Great Compassion Repentance), as well as commentaries on the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra* and the *Samantamukha Parivarta*, all of which circulate in the world. Among his disciples were the scholar Yang Yi and the Prince Consort Li Zunxu.
He was presented with a purple robe and a posthumous title. He passed away on the fifth day of the first month.
This was the seventh year of Jisi (1109).
Zu received the posthumous title and purple robe from Ciming.
The Commandant Li Zunxü memorialized regarding Zudoxing, who was granted a posthumous title and purple robes.
In the eighth year, the gengwu year,
the Dharma Master Sizhuan once again revitalized the Faxiang school at Changshui.

Xuán was a native of Hájī. He studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* under the Dharma Master Hóngmǐn. Upon reaching the passage concerning the two aspects of motion and stillness—“clearly not arising”—he attained a realization.
Hearing of the spiritual reputation of Lángyá Jué, he hurried to attend him. Just as Jué was ascending the seat, Xuán asked:

“If it is fundamentally pure and tranquil, why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Jué raised his voice and said: “It is fundamentally pure and tranquil. Why? Because... [text continues].

"How has this world of mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arisen? Xuán was suddenly enlightened by these words. He intended to remain and succeed him as his heir, but Huìjué said to him, "Your school has not flourished for a long time;
you should rouse your resolve to support it and repay the Buddha's kindness. Xuán followed these instructions and resided at Chángshuī, where his assembly numbered nearly one thousand.
Based on the tenets of the Xiánshǒu school, he composed commentaries on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and other works that were circulated throughout the world.
Chan Master Xiaocong of Dongshan in Ruizhou was the fourth generation descendant of Yunmen.
Xiaocong succeeded Wenshu Zhen. He personally planted ten thousand pines on the eastern ridge and constantly recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*;
consequently, the people of the mountains named that ridge "Vajra. Xu Shi, a Court Commissioner of the Ministry of Justice, was appointed as the local governor.
In Nanchang, they passed Mount Lianhua. Master Xiang said to him, "Master Congdao is a descendant of Yunmen;

he is the eye of the heavens and the eyes of men. (When Cong was traveling, he served as the lamp-master at Yunju. Once, when a monk asked, "Why did the Great Sage of Sizhou appear in Yangzhou? Cong replied, "A gentleman loves wealth, but he takes it by the proper way.

Upon hearing this, Master Xiang was greatly amazed and said, "A descendant of Yunmen still remains! In the middle of the night, he gazed toward Yunju and prostrated himself. You should go to visit him; he has consented to compose a poem for you.

I send this to you, saying: Your speech flows without obstruction; you tread high upon the tracks of the Patriarchs. Sitting in meditation through the night by the Cloud-Linked Rock, you plant spring pines amidst the rain.
The mirror divides the candlelight of the golden hall; the mountain answers the bell of the moonlit tower. If anyone asks about the meaning of the Westward Coming—
Facing distant peaks from an empty hall. One day, after Chong had ascended the hall to take his leave of the assembly, he again recited a verse.
At its conclusion, he said: "Only the pickaxe knows my intent; when planting pines, it once more ascends the Diamond Peak. Having finished speaking, he passed away in peace.

Xiangfu Yin said: "As soon as Shending met Shichuang, Shichuang’s reputation was immediately established within the monastic community; they praised one another with great refinement, and [Shending] was made to preside over the Dharma seat.
When the Hermitage Master of Lotus Peak heard a single phrase from Dongshan, he was struck with awe and marveled that he was a descendant of Yunmen, and at midnight he prostrated before him.
Upon meeting Duke Xu for the first time, he immediately spoke highly of him. Alas!"
What were the eyes and what were the mental activities of the ancients?
Since Chan Master Zibo succeeded Baoji in presiding over Dongshan, he has been a successor to Wuzu Fojian.
As a person, he was upright and prudent; he maintained the precepts with rigorous discipline. He studied under Wuzu and served as the monastery’s administrator.
One day, Daojie was ill. He instructed his attendant to go to the storehouse to fetch fresh ginger for decocting medicine.

Baofu scolded him, ordering him to take the money back to purchase it himself before taking any from the storehouse. Daojie took this as a sign of profound respect. Later, when he arrived at Dongshan, Baofu treated him with exceptional honor.

Upon Baofu’s death, he left a final testament requesting that Daojie succeed him on the seat. Coincidentally, the Prefectural Governor also sent a letter entrusting Daojie with the appointment. Daojie then accepted the position.
The Knower said, "The man who sells fresh ginger can stay. Thereupon Bao preached the Dharma at Dongshan.
It was the ninth year of Xinwei, the first year of Shengming (Ren-shen).
The Master resided at Shishuang.
Having moved from Daowu to Shishuang, he encountered Zanyuan, who came to seek instruction. Upon seeing him, the Master said, "Excellent! Take care of the stable! Yuan then brayed like a donkey.
The Master remarked, "Truly a vessel of the Dharma," and appointed him as his attendant. He then assisted with the work of pounding grain.
Xin (Shanxin) lived among the masses for ten years.
The Dharma Master Zhiyun Ciyun Zunshi of the Tiantai school passed away. Zunshi’s courtesy name was Zhibai;
his mother dreamed of swallowing a bright pearl before giving birth to him. He received his monastic training under Siming and practiced the Four [Great Vows] with great vigor.
Samādhi. At the beginning of the Chunhua era, he resided at Ciyun Temple, where he lectured tirelessly. On the tenth day of the tenth month, he passed away while reciting the Buddha’s name.
The traces of his spiritual wonders are fully recorded in his original biography.
Xiangfu Yin said: "The Tiantai school reached a point where its transmission was severed like a snapped thread.
Fortunately, Luoxi sought it out in a foreign land and obtained the succession from Baoyun, Siming, and Ciyun. They maintained it through the practice of samādhi and vows of diligent action.
Alas! Is the propagation of the Way not dependent upon the person?"
In the second year, the Guiyou year, the Chief Administrator Fang Hui attained realization of the Way and received his formal entrustment (*shouzhu*).

Having long served as the general administrator of the monastery, he would frequently consult the Patriarch for instruction. The Patriarch would say, "The affairs of the storehouse office are many; go now. Come back another day. Later, [Fang Hui] again...
The Master asked, "Jian-si, in days to come your descendants will fill the world;

why are you in such a hurry? One day, as the Master happened to go out, it suddenly began to rain. Jian-si was searching for him on a narrow path; having found him, he seized him and said, "Old man, you must explain this to me today!
If you do not speak, I shall beat you! The Master replied, "Jian-si, do you know what this is like?"

The matter was then concluded. Before his words were finished, Huì attained great enlightenment; he immediately prostrated himself upon the muddy ground and asked, "What is it like when we meet on a narrow path?

The Patriarch said, "You should just get out of my way; where do you think you are going? Huì returned to his quarters, assumed the full ceremonial regalia, and went to the abbot’s quarters to offer thanks.
The Patriarch rebuked him, saying, "Not yet. Later, as the Patriarch ascended the hall for formal instruction, Huì came forward and asked, "The profound..."
The birds warbled their songs. "When you leave the clouds and enter the jumbled peaks, what then? The Patriarch said, "I am walking through the wild grasses; you, too, have entered a deep village.
Huaihui said, "An official does not allow even a needle to pass; may I ask one more question? The Patriarch then gave a shout.
Huaihui said, "A fine shout! The Patriarch shouted again. Huaihui also shouted. The Patriarch shouted twice in succession. Huaihui bowed. The Patriarch said:
"This matter is something that only an individual can shoulder. [Fengxue] understood and shook his sleeves and departed.
An-yin Ren said, "The enlightenment of future generations must not be a forced exercise of mastery; otherwise, it belongs to mere intellectual conformity.
Among a thousand such instances of enlightenment, there is not one true one."
Xiangfu Yin said: "Fenzhou’s relation to Shishuang, and Shishuang’s relation to Yangqi—this is precisely what constitutes the casting aside of the measuring line.
Let those with the true eye discern it."
In the first year of the Jǐxū era (Jingyòu), the summer retreat concluded at Jīnluán.
Chan Master Zhēn returned to Shíshuāng and attained thorough enlightenment.
Zhēn, confident that he had personally seen Címíng, felt there was no one in the world who could satisfy his mind. Upon arriving at Jīnluán, he stayed together with Attendant Shàn.

[The Master] was sitting out the summer retreat. [Shishuang] spoke with him well, knowing that [the Master’s] realization had not yet been thorough. One day, while walking together in the mountains, they engaged in a sharp exchange of debate.
Shishuang picked up a piece of tile, placed it upon a rock, and said, "If you can utter a single turning word regarding this, I will grant that you have personally seen the Old Teacher.
[The Master] looked left and right, intending to respond. Shishuang rebuked him, saying, "To hesitate and let the mind-stirring mechanism stop—this is the functioning of intellectual emotion."
"My realization has not yet penetrated; I have never even dreamed of it. I am truly ashamed. He returned to Shishuang.

When the Patriarch saw him coming, he scolded him, saying, "A genuine wandering monk must know the proper timing. What urgent business is there that you have come so early, before the summer retreat is over?
Zhen wept and said, "My elder brother Shan harbors a poisonous heart that ultimately obstructs people; therefore, I have come to see the Master. The Patriarch immediately asked:
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? he asked. [The Master] said, "Cloudless sky arises over the peaks; the moon exists within the waves.
The Patriarch scolded him, saying, "With hair white as snow and teeth falling out, you still hold such a view. How will you ever escape birth and death?
The student was truly struck with awe and begged for instruction. The Patriarch said, "Ask me! When the student repeated the previous words to ask the Patriarch, the Patriarch roared.
He shouted, saying: "Cloudless sky arises above the peaks; the full moon descends into the heart of the waves. Zhen attained great enlightenment beneath these words.
Xiangfu Yin said: "Attendant Kuò did not spare his hands or feet at Huayan and Lumén;
now Attendant Shan, with a single tile, has removed the obstruction blocking the true mind at Cuīyán, enabling him to once again turn toward the Patriarchs."
Upon hearing these words, they attained great enlightenment; the two attendants may truly be called the eyes of all quarters.

Lukmen specifically prepared tea for them and addressed the assembly, saying: "You dragon-elephants who study the Way must be thorough and meticulous. When entering the room for decisive discernment, you must not take it lightly.
Do not take up a single phrase and consider it the ultimate limit, thinking, 'I am sharp-witted,' only to be caught by those with clear eyes."

To see through this is to become a source of universal laughter; what is there to be gained? It is solely because of the ignorance of ego-clinging (*māna-avidyā*) that one cannot turn back and draw near to those of superior capacity.
Fortunately, there are enlightened practitioners who, disregarding their own bodies and lives, provide public verification of the truth.
This kindness is difficult to repay. Alas! To reflect on the pain once the pain has subsided—truly, these are words like medicine and stone!
Chan Master Wuzhen succeeded him as the abbot of Daowu;
he was a Dharma heir who had deeply investigated the Patriarchs.
Chan Master Guquan resided at Baozhen.
Quán wandered among the lakes and visited Zǔ on Dàowú Mountain. He ascended the summit of Mount Héng and resided at Lǎnzàn Rock.
He then moved to Bājiāo and later to Bǎozhēn—both of which were the most perilous and remote places in the regions of Héng and Xiāng.
One night, while sitting on the ground at Zhūróng Peak, a great python coiled around him. Quán untied his sash and bound it around its waist; by midnight, the snake was gone. The next day...
He searched for it throughout the mountains and found the sash wrapped around a withered pine tree. He used to carry a large wine gourd on a staff as he traveled through the mountains.
When people asked what was inside the gourd, he replied, "The elixir of the Great Way."
Chan Master Shouzhi of Dayu, a descendant of Fenyang, passed away in silence.
While Zhizhu resided at both Dayu and Cuoyan, his assembly never exceeded thirty members. His buildings were old;

he used wooden props to support those parts that were about to collapse, such that passersby feared they might fall. Carrying his alms bowl, he traveled daily through cities, prefectures, villages, and hamlets. At the monastery...
Like a traveler’s inn, even the supply of gruel and rice is sometimes interrupted. He once composed this verse on Dongshan’s "Three Pounds of Hemp":
Eyes askance as I read Sanskrit script, Tongues clicking as I recite mantras; Blowing the fire with long, pointed beaks, Wood fills the hearth with rising smoke.
Again, he addressed the assembly: "To seek oil from sand is a pitiable matter; it is like Chuiyan chewing his rice and feeding it to an infant.
Only when you understand the ultimate point regarding good and evil at that time will you realize that all the while your face has been covered in ashes."
The second year, the year of Yi Hai (1115), when the Master resided at Fuyan on Mount Nanyue, Huineng entered the inner chamber and attained realization.
Huineng was the son of the Zhang family of Yushan; from childhood he abstained from meat and alcohol and refrained from playing games. He left home to receive full ordination, and whenever he sat...

He sat in the full lotus posture and always walked with his gaze fixed straight ahead. Relying on Létán Chéng, he was assigned a seat to receive visitors, and his reputation spread throughout all quarters.

When Wényuè saw him, he sighed in admiration, saying, "In the South, there is one who possesses the vessel of the Way; it is a pity only that he has not yet been subjected to the hammer and tongs of the true tradition.
Later, they traveled together to the Western Mountains, and during a night conversation regarding the Dharma-way of Yúnmén, Yuè remarked, "Although Master Chéng is indeed of the Yúnmén..."
After the Gate, there is the fruit of the Dharma-way. Nan asked what the difference was between them. [Yunmen] said: "Yunmen is like nine-refined cinnabar;
it can transform iron into gold. Chenggong is like quicksilver; it may be admired from afar, but if placed in the forge, it flows away."
Nan-nu threw his pillow at him. The next day, Yunmen apologized for his transgression. Nan-nu said again, "Yunmen’s bearing was like that of a king;
would he have been willing to die for words that are dead? Master Cheng has a Dharma to bestow upon people, but it is a dead word.
Can a dead word truly bring people to life? He then turned his back and left. Nan-nu pulled him back, saying, "If it is so, then who can satisfy your mind? He replied, "Shi."
"Shuangyuan’s skillful means have spread throughout all quarters; you should go see him, for you must not delay.
Nanmo thought to himself, "Master Yue likes Cuiyan, yet he has sent me to see Shishuang. If I gain something from seeing him, what does it matter to Yue? He then set out for Shishuang.
On the way, he heard that the Patriarch (Shishuang) did not attend to his duties and treated the monastic community with contempt. Thereupon, he ascended Mount Heng.
He went to visit Xian of Fuyan, who appointed him as the record-keeper (*shuji*). Shortly thereafter, Xian passed away, and the Prefectural Governor appointed Zu to fill his position.
Nanxin was pleased and wished to observe the man's character. Once Zu arrived, he disparaged various schools of thought, item by item, labeling them all as heterodox interpretations.
The secret instructions and essential teachings transmitted by Letan were all included among those [teachings] he rejected.
Nanwei Qisuo recalled the words Yuan Yue had spoken on ordinary days and suddenly changed his mind, saying: "How can a great man allow doubt and obstruction to arise within his own heart?
He then went to the master's quarters. The Patriarch said, "The Secretary has already led his disciples to travel abroad; if you have any doubts, you may sit here."
As they were discussing this, Nan-gu declined, his entreaties becoming increasingly earnest. Baizhang said, "The Secretary studies Yunmen Chan;
you must be well-versed in its essential meaning. Regarding the saying, 'Releasing three blows of the staff upon Dongshan'—does he have a share in receiving those blows, or does he not?
Nan-gu replied, "He has a share in receiving them. Baizhang’s expression grew solemn, and he said, "Upon hearing the sound of the three blows of the staff, one is already receiving them."
"Then from morning until evening, whenever a magpie caws or a crow caws, they should all be struck with the staff.
The Master simply sat upright, accepted the incense offered by Nan, and paid his respects. The Master asked again:
"If you have indeed grasped Yunmen’s meaning, then as for Zhaozhou saying, 'The old woman of Mount Tai—I have thoroughly exposed her,' where exactly was it that he exposed her?"
Nan was standing nearby. When Nan could not answer, he hurried out. The following day, Nan went to visit him again. The Patriarch continued to revile and scold him incessantly.
Nan said, "Is reviling truly the compassionate gift of Dharma? The Patriarch smiled and said, "Did you understand that as a scolding?
At these words, Nan attained great enlightenment. He cried out involuntarily, "Lectan’s words were indeed dead words! He then presented a verse, saying: "Standing out from the thicket..."
Linji was Zhaozhou. The old woman’s discernment left him with no recourse. Now the four seas are as clear as a mirror; travelers, do not let the road be your enemy.
The Patriarch pointed to the character "no" (沒), while Nan said it was the character "yes" (有).
The Patriarch nodded his head. He then stayed for over a month before taking his leave. He asked the Patriarch, "Ultimately, how is the Great Matter? The Patriarch scolded him, saying:
Wearing robes and eating rice is not the ultimate; defecating and urinating is not the ultimate.
In the third year of the Bingzi cycle, the lay practitioner Li Zunxu compiled the *Guangdeng lu* (Extended Record of the Lamp), for which the Emperor composed a preface.
Chan Master Yuanlian of Guanghui in Ruizhou, a successor in the lineage of Shoushan Shishuang, passed away.
Initially, Yuanlian relied upon Zhaoqing Huiqiao; while he was reciting the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, Huiqiao asked him, "The scripture is right here;
where is Vimalakīrti? Yuanlian was at a loss for a reply and wept, saying, "A man of great character is being treated by others..."

It was all the same; there were no words to be spoken. How could one not feel ashamed? Thereupon, he visited more than fifty venerable masters in succession, yet none could enable him to realize the essential meaning.
He then proceeded to Shoushan, where on the twenty-sixth day of the first month, he attained awakening.

[Shoushan] displayed four perfect circles, each containing the characters for tiger, dog, rat, and ox, which he had written himself, and hung them upon the gate of the abbot’s quarters. This continued until the ninth month.
On the twenty-sixth day, he passed away in peace. A master of the Jingde era, he was revered by eminent scholar-officials;
moreover, he enjoyed a long life and, foreknowing his time of departure, prepared for his passing. Liai was the preeminent among them.
The fourth year, the *dingchou* year.
The Master resided at Xinghua.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When I, this mountain monk, dwelt at Fuyan, I saw only the realm of Fuyan; I rose late and went to bed early."
At that time, clouds arose from the azure crags and the moon sank into the cold pool. The *śabdaka* birds flew and sang before the Prajñā Terrace;

*sāla* flowers scattered their fragrance beside Mount Zhurong. Grasping a slender cane and sitting upon a flat rock, he would occasionally discuss the profound and subtle with the monks of the Five Lakes.
With his head covered in ash and face smeared with dust, he resided at Xinghua, manifesting only the house style of Xinghua as he welcomed [the visitor].
He was sent away. His gate connected to the city; carriages and horses thronged there. The songs of fishermen echoed through the Xiang River, and the cries of monkeys resounded from Mount Lu.

The sounds of stringed and fluted instruments and popular ballads entered his ears from time to time. Furthermore, he conversed daily on Chan and the Way with eminent men from all quarters of the land, until years and months were entirely forgotten.
Now tell me: does there still exist a distinction between dwelling in the deep mountains and residing within the city walls? Try to say so.
After a long silence, he said: "In this place is Maitreya; there is no gate, and no Sudhana.
The Chan Master Chenggu inherited the lineage from Jianfu.
In his youth, Gu was a scholar of great learning who enjoyed a wide reputation. He left the household life to study under Taiyang Xuan, and later visited Nan...
Yue Ya was granted permission to enter the inner sanctum. He traveled to Mount Lu and resided at the Hongjue Pagoda Courtyard, where he was known as the "Ancient Pagoda Master.
He preached the Dharma on Mount Zhi. When Fan Zhongyan was serving as the governor of Rao, he invited the Ancient Master to reside at Jianfu Temple.
In the first year of the Baoyuan era, the year Wuyin (965), the Master arrived at the capital to meet General Li.

General Li, following the instructions of [Emperor] Zhenzong, dispatched a messenger to invite the Master, saying: "Among the Dharma friends within the realm, there are none but you, Master, and Yang Dainian."
"Alas! Dadian has abandoned me and departed. In recent years, I have suddenly felt my strength decline. I wish to see you one last time before I die.
He then sent a letter to the Governor of Tan, earnestly requesting that he be dispatched. Master Zu was moved with compassion and traveled east by boat.
On his way, he passed through Langye and composed the "Song of the Cowherd" for Jue. Jue silently attained the *samādhi* of "sportive play" (*yōxi sānmèi*). Upon arriving at the capital, he...

It had been little more than a month since the Commandant Li was last seen, when Li indeed passed away. Upon hearing the verses exchanged between them during their final conversation, the Emperor marveled at them with admiration.
By imperial decree, he was granted an official boat to return south; however, midway through the journey, he suffered a stroke.
In the second year, Jǐmǎo (1059),
and in the first year of Kāngdìng, Gēngchén (1042),
the Seventh Generation of Linjì, Master Címíng of Shīshuāng, passed away.
His secular age was fifty-four and his monastic seniority thirty-two. His life and deeds were inscribed at Xinghua, and his entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Shishuang.
He was the eighth-generation patriarch of Linji.
His taboo name was Fanghui. He was the son of the Cold family in Yichun, Yuanzhou, and succeeded Shishuang.
He was the eighth generation descendant of Linji and the successor to the ancestral lineage of Yangqi (for ten years).
The Master resided at Yangqi.
He returned to Jiufeng Pingshi, where the Magistrate of Yichun invited him to reside at Yangqi. In his teaching hall, he asked a monk:
"As for the chestnut thorn, how will you swallow it? As for the diamond ring, how will you penetrate it? When he first took up residence, the old building was in ruins.

The rafters were exposed during the height of winter; snow and sleet filled the beds, and there was no place to dwell. A monk came with sincere devotion, wishing to provide funds for repairs. The Patriarch declined him, saying:
"Our Buddha has said that we live in the Age of Decline (*kaṣāya-yuga*). High cliffs and deep valleys undergo constant change and instability.
How can one expect everything to be perfect and as one wishes? Seek fulfillment within yourself. You who have left the home life to study the Way..."
My hands and feet are not yet steady, and I am already in my forties or fifties; how could I have the leisure to concern myself with grand houses?
He finally declined the offer. On the following day, he ascended the hall and said: "At Yangqi, newly settled, the walls of my house are sparse;
The entire bed is strewn with snow-white pearls. I shrink my neck and sigh in secret, Recalling once more the ancients who dwelt beneath the trees."
Xinsi, the first year of the Qingli era (in the second month, medicinal herbs rained down upon the capital). Renwu, the second year.
Guiwei, the third year.
Chan Master Huinan began teaching the Dharma at Tong’an.
In the fourth year, the cyclical year Jiashen (1044), Chan Master Shouduan came to study under the Patriarch and attained realization.
Duàn had previously undergone tonsure under Chan Master Yu of Chaling; he now came to visit the Patriarch. One day, the Patriarch suddenly asked him about his ordination master.
"Who is your teacher? Mazu asked. Baizhang replied, "The Venerable Yuru of Chaling. Mazu said, "I have heard that he had an awakening after falling while crossing a bridge;
he composed a verse on it that was truly extraordinary. Can you recite it? Baizhang recited: "I possess a bright pearl, Long confined by the dust of worldly toil.
Today, the dust is cleared and the light shines forth, Illuminating ten thousand peaks of mountains and rivers. Mazu smiled.
Duan immediately rose and hurried away. He stood there in a state of stunned alarm, unable to sleep all night long. At dawn, he went to consult his master. It happened to be the end of the year.
The Master asked, "Did you see those people performing the *nuo* exorcism yesterday? Duan replied, "I saw them. The Master said, "In this one matter, you are not their equal.
Duan was even more greatly startled and asked, "What do you mean? The Master said, "They enjoy being laughed at; you fear being laughed at."

Duan Dawu (Yuyin) was enlightened when Yangqi Huazhu raised for him the saying, "Advancing further atop the hundred-foot pole. While investigating this, he suffered a fall and attained realization. He went to visit the Patriarch (Furong Daokai), who certified his attainment. Later, he also succeeded the Patriarch as his dharma heir.
In the fifth year, the Year of Yiyou;
in the sixth year, the Year of Bingxu,
the Master moved from Yangqi to reside at Mount Yungai in Tanzhou.
The seventh year was Dinghai;
the eighth year was Wuzi.
The Great Being Fahua Zhiyan (his dharma heirs are unknown).

He was the son of the Xu family of Shouchun. When Emperor Renzong first fell ill and the succession to the throne had not yet been established, the high ministers requested that a worthy scion of the imperial clan be stationed in the capital.
That night, the Emperor burned incense and prayed silently, saying: "Tomorrow, at the Huacheng Hall, a vegetarian feast shall be prepared.
I reverently invite the Great Being of the Lotus Sutra to descend and attend; do not decline. None of those around him heard this. It was clear.

At dawn, Dao-yi stood solemnly waiting. Suddenly, the attendants reported that Fahua had come straight from the Right Aisle Gate toward the inner palace, and the imperial guards could not stop him despite their protests.
Renzong smiled and said, "I invited him to come. When he arrived, he ascended the imperial dais and sat down.
Renzong asked about the matter of the heir apparent; Fahua took up his brush and wrote the character "Ten" (十) in large characters.
He practiced for thirty-three years and then cast away his writing brush. When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, he was the thirteenth son of Prince An-yi of Pu.
On the twenty-third day of the eleventh month, as he was about to pass away, he said to those around him:
"Since immeasurable kalpas past, I have brought the Śrāvastī realm to fruition and manifested my body to propagate the teachings. Now I am returning south. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
He passed away lying on his right side.
Chan Master Dechang of Daci Xiangguo Monastery was summoned for an audience at the Yanchun Pavilion.
Dechang was a successor of Shishuang. On the first day of the ninth month, an imperial decree invited Dechang to a vegetarian feast below the Yanchun Pavilion, where the Emperor questioned him.
Regarding the Buddha-dharma:
in the first year of the Huangyou era,
the year Jichou (1049 CE), Chan Master Renyong founded Yun'ai Dunwu Monastery.
Yong was dignified in demeanor and profound in talent. From his youth, he was well-versed in the teachings of the Tiantai school. He changed his robes and went to visit Xuedou Xian.
Xuedou, perceiving that Yong was capable of upholding the Great Dharma, rebuked him, saying, "Principal of the Yangxiang Monastery! Enraged and indignant, Yong descended the mountain.

Gazing toward Xuedou, he prostrated himself and said, "In this life, my travels for the sake of the Way and my study of Chan shall not go beyond Xuedou. I swear not to return home. Thereupon, he departed immediately.

Letam had pursued his practice for over ten years, yet his doubts remained unresolved. Hearing that National Teacher Huizhao had moved to Yungai and was able to restrain and guide his disciples, he went directly to his quarters.

Before a single word had been exchanged, Letam suddenly realized the Mind Seal. (Later, he followed National Teacher Duan; he investigated the profound mysteries to their ultimate limit and, upon entering the world, presided over two monasteries, Baoning.)
The eighth-generation successor of Linji, Patriarch Yangqi, passed away.
Hong Juefan said: "Linji’s lineage was transmitted through seven generations to reach Shishuang Yuan. Yuan had two sons:
one was Jicui Nan, and the other was Yangqi Hui. Nan’s deployment of means was like sitting at a crossroads where treasures are gathered."
They treated all manner of strange objects as precious and sold them; even discarded hairpins and fallen earrings were picked up as soon as they were found.
Thus, they gradually fell into the lowest stratum, and those who falsely claimed his lineage became too numerous to count. Eventually, however, it was like a jade-cutter refining the *fanyu* gem:
the common stones (*wufu*) were cast aside. Consequently, his descendants have all been radiant and brilliant, capable of perpetuating the family legacy—truly like the *biluo* (the azure void).
Stele. There is no spurious version.
Chan Master Dezhang again entered the inner palace to present his memorial.
Chan Master Weizheng (also read Zheng) of Jingtu Monastery in Hangzhou, the fourth generation descendant of the Chan Master Fayan lineage, passed away.
While still young, Zheng followed Benru of Qiantang to receive his formal training.

When the people of the commandery wished to open the treasury to bestow ordination certificates (*duòjié*) as alms, Zheng sighed and said, "In antiquity, the conferring of ordination was based on pure spiritual capacity and profound principles; now it is the opposite. We are far removed from the ways of old.
As one who belongs to the Three Jewels, I shall surely find my own time. He then knelt in thanks and refused the offer. When Benru asked for the reason, Zheng replied, "That..."
It is not that I know you personally; it is simply because of my teacher’s words.

To turn back hundreds of thousands upon a single youth and ensure that he can practice giving throughout his entire life without seeking recompense—this is the compassionate protection of the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, whose great vow is to deliver all living beings.
This is precisely the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. You should humble yourself to recite and uphold it; let all your gratitude be directed toward this one source. In this regard:
Yi was contented with his lot, regarding it as a marvel. At the age of eighteen, he became a full monk (*bhikṣu*).
Clad alone in a worn-out woolen robe, there were those who wished to provide him with annual provisions so that he might continue the affairs of the monastery; Yi declined them, saying:

"I have heard of begging for food by alms-round, but I have not heard of sitting at ease to enjoy offerings. I have visited all the patriarchs, yet I have never heard of neglecting study to pursue one's own interests. Moreover..."
"My teeth are still strong and my vigor intact; I am currently at the stage where I should exert my physical strength in performing rituals.

This is not the time for me to attend to a dwelling. Thereupon, he traveled abroad and received the Dharma of the Mind from Weiso (Wei Su). Weiso was the director of the Jingtu Monastery on Mount Gongcheng;

Zheng had assisted him as a high official for a long time and subsequently succeeded him upon the seat. Ye Qingchen, the Palace Secretary, welcomed Zheng to discuss the Way. One day, Ye said to Zheng:
He said, "Tomorrow there is a gathering of guests; I wish for the Master to come and sprinkle them with ambrosia. Zheng gave his word. The next day, he was sent to invite him.
Zheng handed him a verse, saying: "Yesterday was already past, and today has arrived; I step out the door, leaning on my staff, and reflect once more.
As a monk, one should dwell only in mountain valleys; it is most inappropriate to be amidst the banquets of a kingdom. In the end, he did not go.
He used to ride a yellow calf when going out or coming in, with his *kamaṇḍalu*, headcloth, and alms bowl all hung upon its horns; thus, he was popularly called "Zheng the Yellow Ox.
When Imperial Secretary Jiang Tang went to govern Hangzhou, he formed a relationship of "square friendship" (an informal bond between equals) with Zheng.

Whenever Zheng went to visit him, he would dismount his calf at the entrance of the prefectural courtyard and depart after conversing and laughing together for the entire day. Zheng maintained a strict discipline over himself. In winter...
He did not maintain a brazier for warmth; instead, he made balls of reed flowers and tucked his feet inside them. When guests arrived, he shared this with them.

During the summer and autumn, he delighted in gazing at the moon, chanting and laughing until dawn; he took this as his regular practice. Someone once asked the Master why, though bearing the title of "Chan Master," he did not speak of Chan.
He replied, "It is merely a waste of words. I am lazy; I would rather avoid such detours than trouble myself day and night."
The myriad phenomena are merely its unfolding; yet while speech has its limitations, this Dharma of mine is inexhaustible—what is called the inexhaustible treasury of the Creator.
On the first day of the summer month, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Movement is contrasted with stillness, yet from the very beginning there has been no limit."
I have been active for sixty-four years; now I am at rest. Yet, fundamentally, what is there to be called activity or stillness? Thereupon, he passed away peacefully.

(While staying as a guest at the Lulong Mountain Hermitage in Jinling under the shade of Sun Garden, he inscribed a poem on a painting of Zheng Huangniu and presented it to the monk Chao-shan Zhi, saying:

"In the Song dynasty, whether in mountain forests or bustling markets, Green silk and crimson edicts lie beyond the white clouds. To the man of high character, these are but the saliva of a snail; He wanders freely, finding his own natural ease. He loves to ride a yellow calf through grand banquets, With his water jar and scrolls hanging from the tips of its horns. The wind..."

His flowing brushstrokes startle the renowned and wise; every single character and solitary word is vied for and cherished. When inspiration strikes, he wanders at will before the mountains and waters; with long songs and great roars, he laughs at the clouds and mists. He need not pursue his way with a coral whip; how could he compare to one who keeps a fine steed in a golden saddle?

A thousand pine trees stand against the setting sun; returning to the thatched hut, the grasses grow lush and green. His lofty spirit was never intended as a mere eccentricity; his transcendent air has been clamorously passed down through the ages. To view the present compared to the Song dynasty is like the difference between heaven and abyss;

yet my teacher’s legacy remains whether later or earlier. He cleared the weeds and bound a cottage upon the mountain peak; with a *bāo* mat for a seat and a gourd for a vessel, he composed several volumes of verse. Though he lacked the money to buy a yellow calf, what regret is there in meeting him through painted portraits? I ask the boatman of Moling about the withered reeds; within the courtyard—

Autumn rains moisten the moss-covered bricks; I point out the elegant brushstrokes upon the walls. The tea kettle rattles outside the window as red springs flow; beneath Mount Fufei, the Five Lakes stretch on. Upon the misty waves, a single leaf can forget the passing years; with sprouts of *pho* and grains of *gu*, I cook fresh fish with my own hands.

Who are these fishermen and boatmen? They play with the moon in great basins, tracing ripples on the waves. Swarms of gulls and friends of egrets cling to one another in pairs. Would my Master deign to come and stir me from my book-sleep? With reeds surrounding his feet, he stiffens his cold shoulders;

his body enters the painting as a gaunt immortal. Alas! His body enters the painting as a gaunt immortal. Later, he succeeded Lingyin and resided at Lion Mountain (Lishan) in Jinling, where people at the time held his integrity and conduct in high esteem.
The ninth-generation patriarch of Linji, whose name was Shouduan, was the son of the Ge family of Hengyang. In his youth, he devoted himself to calligraphy;
upon reaching adulthood, he received the tonsure under Master Yu of Chaling and subsequently studied under Patriarch Yangqi to inherit the Dharma.
In the second year of the Huangyou era (752 CE),
the ninth generation of Linji, Baiyun Zushi, succeeded to the lineage (for twenty-three years). During this time,
the Master resided at Chengtian Temple.
When the Master traveled to Mount Lu, Chan Master Net of Yuan Tong recommended him for the abbacy of Chengtian Temple; his reputation became exceedingly great. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "In the boiling cauldron, there is no place that is cold. The monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?"
The Patriarch said, "Pressing a gourd to the bottom of the water. [A monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Patriarch said, "The crow flies;
the hare runs.
Chan Master Dezhang requested to spend the remainder of his life in the mountain forests; by imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Lingyin in Hangzhou and was granted the title Mingjue.
Chan Master Jue’ne of Yuan Tong in Jiangzhou declined the imperial decree to reside at Jingyin Temple, proposing the Record Keeper Huailian to serve as his successor.

Jue’ne was the son of the Jian family from Zizhou; he received full ordination after passing the scriptural examinations and became preeminent among lecturers in the two circuits of Sichuan, such that even veteran elders yielded to him.
Later, spurred by a Chan practitioner, he departed from Shu and wandered through Jingzhou and Chu, eventually reaching Rong of Dongshan in Xiangzhou.
(Regarding the succession of the lineage of Yongzhi: He remained under [the master's] guidance for ten years and inherited his Dharma. Later, he traveled to Mount Lu.
Cheng Shimeng, the Prefectural Governor, invited him to reside at Guizong Temple; he subsequently moved to Yuan Tong.

Since the monasteries were destroyed during the Zhou dynasty, the restoration of the two streets (the Buddhist centers) during the Jianlong era of Emperor Taizu consisted only of scholastic studies (*yixue*). Although the scholar-officials were exceptionally brilliant and outstanding...
All [of these] were weary of hearing [discussions on] names and characteristics (*nāma-lakṣaṇa*). Yet, the single school of Shaolin had not yet spread widely.

Yang Yi and Chao Hui of the Hanlin Academy were the first to clarify and promote it. The eunuch Li Yunning submitted a petition to offer a residential estate in Bianzhou for the purpose of establishing a Chan seat.
By imperial decree, it was granted the name Shifang Jingyin Chan Monastery. When the Emperor heard the name of [Fayan] Wenyue, he specifically issued an edict to summon him.
Fǎ declined to attend on the grounds of his severe eye ailment, proposing that Huáilián, the registrar of the monastery, take his place.
Thereupon, an imperial edict was issued to Huáilián. When Huáilián arrived, he was summoned for an audience; his exposition of the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma pleased the Emperor.

An imperial decree was proclaimed ordering him to follow the ritual protocols of the Chan monasteries of the South in opening the hall and expounding the Dharma. Huáilián was granted the title Chan Master Dàjué, and Nè was granted the title Chan Master Zùyìn.
Chan Master Zanyuan resided at Jiangshan.

Zanyuan had served the Patriarch Shishuang for a long time; after the Patriarch passed away, Zanyuan lived in a hut by his stupa and planted trees there for eight years. He subsequently emerged from seclusion to reside at Jiangshan.
When Prime Minister Wang Anshi was observing the mourning period for his mother, he was reciting sutras in the mountains and associated with Zanyuan as if they were brothers.
When asked about the essential meaning of the Patriarch’s intent, Yuan did not answer.
Shi pressed him further, and Yuan said, "You have three obstacles to prajñā and one capacity for the Way. After one or two more lifetimes, you may attain full maturity. Shi asked:
"I wish to hear your explanation. Yuan said, "Your Excellency has received a nature of great vigor, yet your worldly affinities are deep.
With such a vigorous nature encountering deep worldly affinities, you will surely take upon yourself the heavy burden of the world and harbor ambitions for its governance.

If whether you are employed or retired cannot be determined, your mind will not find peace. With a mind that lacks peace, while maintaining your ambition to govern the world, when could you ever [attain your goal]?"

"A single thought lasts ten thousand years! Furthermore, you are prone to anger, yet your studies still cling to intellectual principles; this constitutes ignorance regarding the Way—this is the third [fault].
To regard fame and profit as if shedding one's hair, and to find sweetness in the simple and austere like a dhūta practitioner—this is to draw near to the Way.
For now, it would be well to cause the teachings of the Vehicle to flourish through such practice. Shi bowed twice and received these instructions.
The third year of the Xīnmǎo cycle (1211).
Two thousand years after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, Chan Master Huínán of Guìzōng on Mount Lú entered the mountain and attained realization of wisdom. [Recorded by] Fāmíng (upon the temple fire).
It is not recorded [here]. This record is because Master Nanyuan attained the realization of samādhi while in prison.

While Master Nanyuan was residing at Guizong Monastery, a fire broke out; it was reduced to ashes in a single night. The great assembly was in a state of commotion that shook the mountains and valleys, yet Nanyuan sat peacefully as if nothing had happened.
The monk Hongzhun wished to support him and flee, but Nanyuan rebuked him. Hongzhun said, "Even if you, Master, were weary of [the world]..."
"In this world, what does the Dharma-way of Ciming rely upon? Having said this, he slowly adjusted his robes and rose; the fire had already reached his sitting mat.
He entered prison, where a district official, harboring private resentment, subjected him to a hundred forms of torture.
He remained silent, refusing to speak, doing nothing but abstaining from food. Two months later, he was released; his hair and beard were unshorn, and only skin and bone remained. Truly remarkable!
He met him halfway and, seeing him, wept and said, "Elder brother, how have you come to this? Nanchi replied, "You vulgar fellow!

You truly did not realize that I was bowing down. Later, he said to his disciples, "While I was in prison, I realized the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and the Bodhisattva’s *Vikrīḍita-samādhi* (Samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s Playful Sovereignty).
As the Sūtra says: "The Bodhisattva plays with supernatural powers (*abhijñā*) and purifies Buddha-lands."
Soil. His heart did not take pleasure in it; he criticized the Hīnayāna because it cannot bring sentient beings to fulfillment.

His disciples requested to hear his explanation. Nanyue said: "Whenever a prison official governs those who have committed crimes, he examines their true and false circumstances and must inflict severe beatings upon them.
Once the reality of their deception is fully exposed, they are released of their own accord. Although there may be cruel punishments, [the truth will emerge]."
It can indeed be explained. That one would accept death as a crime with a willing heart is because wisdom is exhausted and the passions are withered.
Yet, those who study dhyāna today are driven by the madness of frantic seeking and the disease of deception; they do not use the wisdom of insight to forge their way.
By what means was he released?
Chan Master Yiyu resided at Fachang.
When Yiyu traveled to the Western Mountains, he took note of the seclusion of the Two Peaks and stayed there for three years; only then did he respond to the invitation from Fachang.
Fachang was at Fenning in the north; amidst a thousand peaks and ten thousand ravines, there were only a few old rooms.

Upon his arrival, he practiced "sword-plowing and fire-seeding," finding it particularly peaceful and joyful. However, the monastic disciples could not endure such austerity and bitterness, so most abandoned him. For this reason, he remained a solitary practitioner.
In the fourth year of the Incheon era, National Preceptor Zu resided at Wontong-sa.
Nul offered the abbacy of Wontong to Zu and took up residence in the East Hall himself. At that time, Zu was twenty-eight years old; he had previously...

His contemporaries yielded their seats to him in recognition of his reputation; he held himself with extreme gravity and presided over the assembly with reverence and solemnity, subduing the private for the sake of the public.
Thus, the ancestral style was greatly revitalized. Chan Master Mingjue Chongxian of Xuedou in Mingzhou, the fourth generation descendant of Yunmen, entered nirvana.
This reveals his first journey abroad when he visited Chan Master Lin of Mount Lu. When [Lin] brushed aside his [Yunmen’s] spiritual capacity, the entire assembly trembled with awe.
Master Lin addressed the assembly, saying, "This is the vast and great samādhi of the Tathāgata; it is not something you can discern through a mind of grasping and rejecting.
The Imperial Son-in-law and Commander-in-Chief Li Zunxu submitted a memorial requesting that he be granted a purple robe, and the Grand Councilor Lord Jia submitted a memorial as well.

He was posthumously titled Mingjue (Luminous Enlightenment). On the tenth day of the sixth month, at midnight, he took leave of the assembly; having bathed and adjusted his robes, he lay on his side and passed away.
His disciples, including Weigai and Wenzhin, compiled his records of expositions, *nian* and *song* verses, and other collections, which were subsequently circulated in the world.
Xiangfu Yin said: "The pivotal words of the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past are like milk mixed with water, or clarified butter (ghṛta) within curd and cream.
Since Xuedou revealed their subtle essence and stripped away their vital points, one need not wait for a king of geese to separate the milk from the water;
by tasting it, the various poisons are eliminated. His verses and commentaries open the way for those who study."
His spiritual insight was no small matter; indeed, his essence was refined and harmonious, such that his realization and his eloquence were both unimpeded.
This was during the fifth year of the Gui-si era and the first year of Zhihe, the Jia-wu year.

Zu moved to Fahua; [the source] omits the details (Nü initially recommended Zu to reside at Chengtian Temple. He then yielded the position in the Eastern Hall and declined an imperial summons, recommending his secretary Lian to take his place in its stead.

Thus, he was a venerable master of profound virtue who maintained a humble mind free from self-interest. Zu later withdrew from his plans for the Tongci Monastery; therefore, this section is omitted and not recorded).

Daolung was granted the title Chan Master Yingzhi Mingwu (Enlightened Wisdom Responding to Imperial Edict). [The phrase "Faming" (Elucidating the Dharma) is appended because Daolung was summoned based on a dream; he responded with verses, and as he stayed overnight in the imperial grove, the inscription is recorded accordingly.]
Lung Guang succeeded Hui-lian. While traveling to the capital, he stayed at Jingde Temple, where he would wander through the city markets daily and return home at the second watch.

One night, unable to gain entry, he lay down beneath the gate. The Emperor dreamed that he arrived at the temple gate and saw a dragon coiled upon the ground. He dispatched an imperial messenger to investigate;
seeing Lung fast asleep, the messenger was struck with awe and asked his name before returning to report it. Upon hearing of this, the Emperor came to know of the Way.

Lungming said with joy, "This is an auspicious omen. The following day, he summoned [the Master] to the private chamber (biandian). His responses were detailed and appropriate, and the Emperor was greatly pleased.
Verses and couplets were exchanged between them, flowing continuously along the roads. On some occasions, when the Master entered for an audience, he was granted lodging within the imperial palace.
He was treated with exceptional courtesy and bestowed the honorary title Chan Master Yingzhi Mingwu. At that time, an imperial decree arrived summoning Da'jue Lia to preach at Huacheng Hall.
The Emperor summoned Daoleng to engage him in dialogue. His spiritual acuity was swift and incisive, and the Emperor was greatly pleased. The attendants all shouted "Long live the Emperor!

Daoleng immediately submitted a memorial requesting that Daoliang be appointed to replace him in the Imperial Library to await imperial inquiries and discourse on Chan in the secret palace, while he himself sought to return to Mount Lu.

Upon reading the petition, the Emperor did not grant his request; instead, by imperial decree, a Huayan Chan Monastery was established for him, where he was ordered to open the hall for teaching. Later, at the age of over eighty, he passed away.
During the height of summer, he sat in meditative stillness for seven days. His hands and feet became supple and smooth.
He returned to the Zong lineage and established the Jicui Hermitage to the south;
this Jicui Hermitage was situated on the banks of the Huangbo Creek. Disciples flocked there from all directions, even those who had already received exhaustive instruction from veteran masters.
Upon his arrival, [Liu] Nan was struck with dismay and lost his composure; he then joined the ranks of the disciples. Pan Xingsi once asked him the reason for this, to which Nan replied:
"When a father is strict, the son is filial. Today’s instruction is tomorrow’s model. It is like the earth."
That which is high is lowered; that which is hollow is leveled. When he ascends to the top of a thousand fathoms, I am there with him;
when he is exhausted at the bottom of the Nine Abysses, I am there with him. When his skill reaches its limit, delusions are exhausted and he is naturally liberated.
It is further said: "Nurturing and nourishing—this is how growth and reproduction occur in spring and summer."
Frost and snow are what bring maturity in autumn and winter. How could I wish to remain without words?
Once, while in his quarters, he asked a monk: "Everyone has their karmic conditions of birth (*jìngyuán*); where does the Venerable’s own karmic conditions of birth lie?"

"What does my hand resemble? It resembles a Buddha’s hand. What does my foot resemble? It resembles a donkey’s foot. The students could not fathom this. When someone ventured to respond, Nan said, "Namo!
Whether it is acceptable or not. He then closed his eyes and sat upright. Xingsi asked him again for the reason.

Nan said, "Those who have already passed through the barrier wave their arms and go straight on; how would they know there is a barrier official? To ask the barrier official whether it is acceptable or not—this person has not yet penetrated."
This is the section on "Guan" (The Gatekeeper).
Chan Master Fayuan resided at Fushan.
Initially, Fayuan resided at Taiping Xingguo in Shuzhou; subsequently, he resided at Tianping in Gusu; in this year, he resided at Fushan.
One day, Shanshan was discussing the Way with Wang Zhi, the Court Attendant. Shanshan drew a circle and asked Zhi, "One is not permitted to have a single horse and a solitary spear;
two is not permitted to return home in brocade robes. The magpie must not rejoice; the crow must not suffer calamity.
Speak quickly! Zhi was at a loss. Shanshan said, "The case is settled."
In the second year, the Year of Yiwei, the Master resided at Baiyun.
While the Master was at Fahua, there were so many monastic disciples that there was no room for them; the scholar-officials admired him, and he came to reside at Haiyin Baiyun.
He addressed the assembly: "If you can truly manage to break into a sweat once, then even upon a single blade of grass, you will see jade palaces and crystal halls.
If you have not yet truly managed to break into a sweat once, then even if there were jade palaces and crystal halls, they would be covered over by a single blade of grass.
Now tell me, how does one break into a sweat? After a long silence...
It is said: "I have a pair of hands that are utterly impoverished; I have never easily performed the 'Three Terraces' dance.
When Jingyin Huailian requested to return to the mountains, [the Emperor] did not grant his request, but instead bestowed upon him a camphor bowl, which he ordered the messenger to burn.

Lian offered this verse: "Six years in the imperial capital, chanting the Patriarch’s pivot; Twice in the golden hall, receiving the Heavenly Majesty. Now retiring to the green mountains, what joy could I find?
I shall return home with nothing but Your Imperial Verses filling my basket. The Emperor did not grant permission for his departure, responding with a verse of his own and further decreeing:
"The mountain is the very substance of suchness (tathatā). Where would you go? Return once more to the capital and continue to propagate [the Dharma]."
Regarding the Buddha-dharma, Huilian further presented a verse in thanks. Shortly thereafter, the Emperor dispatched an envoy to bestow upon him a camphor bowl.

After Huilian had finished expressing his gratitude, he held up the bowl and said, "In our Dharma, one wears dyed robes and eats from vessels of clay or iron. This bowl is not in accordance with the Dharma," whereupon he burned it.
When the imperial messenger returned and reported this, the Emperor sighed in admiration without end.
Xiangfu Yin said: "The patriarchs manifest their mechanisms beyond the ordinary; they often walk upon the crown of Vairocana.

Although figures such as Daolung and Huailian did not fail in their practice of the Way while frequenting the courts of emperors, to draw near to kings and high ministers is ultimately not what is appropriate for those who uphold the authentic essence of the school.
Observe how [Huailian] burned his alms bowl when confronted by the imperial envoy—how solemn!"

Ling still possesses the dignified bearing of a *seng* (monk); compared to those among the mountain recluses today who, having fortunately enjoyed imperial favor, act as if they could not do enough to avoid falling behind—how can one describe such a decline toward the secular world? It is truly beyond words.

In the first year of the Jiayou era, the year Bingshen (1056), Chan Master Huiyuan of Kaixian was appointed by Chan Master Jueju to reside at Jicui on Mount Dong. Jueju went south out of the mountains to see him.
Initially, Jueju had relied upon Xuedou Xian; when Jueju resided at Jing’e, Xian inscribed a verse on the wall and departed. Later, [Jueju] resided at...
At Kaixian on Mount Lu, many later students achieved great accomplishment. Yuan succeeded Xuedou; he relied upon Xian at Kaixian.

When the seat of Dongshan became vacant, Xian recommended [Yuan] to accept the invitation from the people of Yingjun. At that time, Nan was residing at Huangbo; consequently, [Yuan] went out of the town to meet him.
Nan remained silent without saying a word, merely burning incense and sitting upright facing him. [Yuan] himself submitted [his credentials].
When the third watch arrived, Yuan immediately rose and said, "The night is deep; it would hinder the Master’s rest. He hurried out.
The next day, each returned to the mountain. Nan asked Chief Seat Yong, "Do you know the old man Dongshan here at Lushan?
I have not met him, though I have heard his name. After a long pause, Yong stepped forward and asked, "Master, when you meet him this time, what kind of person will he be?"
Nan said, "A remarkable man. Yongtai asked the attendant, "When you accompanied the Master to see Dongshan, what did you discuss during the night conversation?
The attendant related the facts as they were. Yongtai said, "This will leave the whole world in doubt."
In the second year of the Dingyou era, Chan Master Fashou appeared at Mount Shimian.
Shou had studied under Tianyi Huai and inherited his Dharma. He appeared in the world at Mount Shimian in Huai. Aside from his staff and alms bowl, he possessed only robes.
[The lineage] was merely maintained [in name]. Disciples pursued [him], yet Xiu lamented that the ancestral Way was not flourishing and took it upon himself to sustain it.
In the third year of the Wuxu cycle, Fushan Yuan retired to Huisheng Rock.
Yuan retired to Shengyan Monastery and composed the *Nine Bands* (*Jiudai*) to expound upon the fundamental tenets of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

When Ouyang Xiu heard Yuan’s reputation, he visited his quarters while Yuan was playing a game of chess with guests. Ouyang abruptly called for the board to be cleared and requested that Yuan preach the Dharma by means of the chess game.
Yuan ordered the drum to be beaten, ascended the seat, and said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like two families playing a game of chess. Why is this so? It is because the opponent..."

One who knows the sound with their hands does not yield when the opportunity arises. If one merely strings together five notes and adds three more, they must first master a single path before they can succeed.
There is a certain class of people who only know how to live their lives behind closed doors; they do not understand seizing the corner or breaking through the pass.

When the hard joints and the tiger’s mouth are displayed simultaneously, once the position is broken, all their efforts are in vain. Therefore it is said: "The fat sides are easy to obtain; the thin [sides]..."
The belly is difficult to satisfy; when one thinks and acts, one often loses the connection. The mind is coarse, and from time to time it strikes its head against things.

Do not boast of being a master of the game, nor speak in vain of being an immortal. Let us not ask about winning the board or losing the pieces; rather, tell me: when black and white have not yet been distinguished, where does that first move fall?
