After a long silence, he said: "From of old, there are nineteen paths; how many times have delusion and awakening alternated?"
Many people offered great praise.

In the fourth year, the year Yihai (1055), Ouyang Xiu and others completed the *Jiu Tangshu* (Old Book of Tang). Xiu also composed the *Wudai Shi* (History of the Five Dynasties) in seventy-four fascicles.
In both works, he deleted all accounts concerning Buddhism and Daoism that had been recorded in the original *Tangshu*.
Xiang Yu said: "When Liu Xiu expunged the teachings of Śākyamuni and exerted himself in their refutation, it was his sincere effort to uphold the orthodox teachings (míngjiào).

However, he simply did not understand the Buddha-dharma. In his later years, after retiring from office and residing in Luoyang, he heard of the virtuous conduct and achievements of Chan Master Xiuyong.
One day, he invited Xiuyong and suddenly asked him: 'What is the purpose of the teaching of the Buddha? "
Xu Yong then engaged in a sincere discussion, his instructions profound and subtle. Xiu stood in awe and said, "I previously knew nothing of Buddhist scriptures;
their subtlety reaches such heights as this. When the time came for him to change his bedding before death, he summoned his children and grandchildren and admonished them earnestly, saying:

"Throughout my life, I was renowned in the world for my literary works and strove to denounce the Buddhists. Now, in this state of decay, I have suddenly heard these profound doctrines and am just beginning to study them."

"What can be done about fate? You all must exert yourselves; do not tread the path of regret. Thus, Baoxiu abandoned wine and meat, withdrew from sounds and sights, and sat in silent meditation with a heart extinguished of worldly desire.
He ordered an old soldier to borrow the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* from a nearby temple; when they reached the eighth fascicle, he passed away while sitting upright.
This was the final glow of Baoxiu’s life, and it was never the case that he did not take refuge in the Awakened Heaven. Now, as for these gentlemen...
When members of the great families do not know where to turn for cultivation in their later years, they merely imitate what those before them have done;
thus, they fail to diminish the Buddha-dharma by even a hair’s breadth, yet lose for themselves the benefit of a mountain.
What joy could there be in doing such a thing?
Chan Master Yiqing arrived at Fushan. Qing was the son of the Li family of Qingshe;
he was exceptionally gifted from the age of seven. He received full ordination after passing the scriptural examinations and studied the *Śataśāstra*.
Not long thereafter, he went to Luoyang to study the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* for five years. Suddenly, he had a profound realization and said: "The Dharma is beyond words; how could it ever be expounded?"
He immediately departed to travel as a wandering monk. Upon reaching Fushan, he arrived at Huisheng Temple where Yuanjian Yuan was residing.
One night, Yuan dreamed that he obtained a fine hawk and raised it; when he awoke, Qing arrived just at dawn. Yuan took this to be an auspicious sign and welcomed him with due ceremony.
He was instructed to examine the causes and conditions regarding the outsider’s question to the Buddha concerning whether he asked about existence or non-existence.
In the fifth year of the Gengzi cycle,
Chan Master Daguang Tanying of Jinshan in Runzhou, a disciple of Guyin, passed away.
Yingshou paid his respects to Dayang. Next, he visited Guyin Cong. The Grand Marshal Li Duanyuan invited him to reside in his garden retreat.
At that time, Xia Song, Wang Shu, Ouyang Xiu, along with Duanyuan’s elder brother Duanque and others, all sought the profound gateway [of the Dharma].

Cong recorded their words, which are titled the *Dengmen Ji* (Anthology of Those Who Ascend the Gate). Later, he resided at Jinshan. On the eve of the New Year in the fourth year of the Jiayou era, he dispatched an attendant...
He dispatched a letter to the scholar Diao Jingchun of Yangzhou, saying: "I shall depart tomorrow morning; there will be no time for us to meet.
Please take good care of yourself. When Jingchun opened the letter, he was greatly startled and said, "What shall we do? He replied with a parting letter and bid him farewell.

During the middle watch of the night, an official on duty reported that a boat carrying a letter from Yangzhou was approaching the shore. Xuying joyfully ordered the drums to be beaten and ascended the seat.
He recounted his original aspiration for leaving the world, expressed gratitude to those who had assisted the monastic community, and exhorted them not to be remiss in their practice.

After descending from the seat and finishing the reading of the letter from Diaoyu, the assembly crowded around him as he walked toward the abbot’s quarters. Once seated in the lotus position, he motioned for them to stand back at a distance. For a long while...
After a long time, he was transformed.
Yuantong Ne appointed Lisiji Liaoyuan as the administrative secretary at Chengtian Temple.
At the age of two, Yuan could recite the *Analects* and the poetry of various schools; at five, he could recite three thousand poems. Among his neighbors...
Everyone hailed him as a divine child. He shaved his head, received the full precepts, and traveled to Mount Lu to visit Kaixian Xian, who praised him highly.
He then visited Yuan Tong Ne, who was struck by his calligraphy and remarked, "His structural framework already resembles that of Xuedou;
he is a talent of the future. Ne subsequently appointed him to manage the records. When Chengtian Monastery’s seat became vacant, Ne selected Yuan for the position. The district...
Shou regarded him with disdain and held him in low esteem. Nan said, "Yuan’s years may be few, but his virtue is mature; even ten thousand aged bhikṣus could not refute him.
Thereupon, Yuan resided at Chengtian Monastery.
In the sixth year, the *xinchou* year, Chan Master Yiqing attained enlightenment at Mount Fu.
Having resided at Mount Fu for three years, Yuan one day asked him: "Do you remember the *huatou*? Try [reciting it]."
[Zhao]qing raised [the whisk] to look at it. Yuanfeng was about to respond when Yuanran covered his mouth. Qing attained clear and thorough awakening, whereupon he prostrated.
Yuanran asked, "Have you wondrously awakened to the profound mechanism? Qing replied, "Even if there were one, I would have to spit it out.
At that time, Attendant Ziji was standing nearby and said, "Today, Qing Huayan has been like a patient who has broken a sweat. Qing looked back and said, "Shut that dog's mouth!"
"If you speak further at length, I shall immediately vomit [in protest].

On the sixth day of the twelfth month, Chan Master Qisong went to the Imperial Palace to submit a memorial presenting the *Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma* (Chuanfa Zhengzong Ji).
He was a Chan Master who had received the purple robe for the transmission of the Dharma at the Yong’an Hermitage of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou.

Qisong went to the Imperial Palace to present a memorial, offering the *Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma* in twelve fascicles, a single scroll of the *Diagram of the Patriarchs*, and three volumes of the *Compendium for Assisting the Teaching*.
Wang Su, the Director of the Hanlin Academy, submitted a formal petition on his behalf. Qisong’s courtesy name was Zhongling and his style name was Qianzi;
he was the son of the Li family of Tanjin in Tengzhou and received the dharma-transmission record from Dongshan Cong. He resided at West Lake in Hangzhou.
For thirty years, he remained in seclusion and did not engage in frivolous social intercourse. At night, he would carry a statue of Avalokiteśvara upon his head;
he would not go to sleep until he had recited its name ten thousand times or more. From that time on, he was able to understand the prose and verse of the world without having studied them.

In the seventh year, the Renyin year [1062], an imperial edict was issued to collect the *Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma* (*Chuanfa Zhengzong Ji*) and the *Collection for Assisting the Teaching* (*Fu jiao bian*) and include them in the Great Canon (*Dazang*).
These manuscripts remained at the government offices for seventy-one days. At that time, Duke Han Qi examined them and showed them to Ouyang Xiu.
Xiu Fang took up the task of literary composition with great confidence. Upon seeing his writings, he said to Qi, "I did not expect to find such a gentleman among the monks;
I must take note of him. He conversed with him all day long and was greatly pleased. When the Emperor reached the passage, "To practice the Way for its own sake, not for fame;
to uphold the Dharma for its own sake, not for the self," he marveled at it for a long time. On the seventeenth day of the third month, an imperial decree was issued.

The court issued a proclamation; his works were included in the Imperial Canon (Dazang). An imperial edict conferred upon Master Song the title of Great Master Mingjiao (Master of Enlightened Teaching), which he declined, but the refusal was not granted.
This was the eighth year, the Gui-mao year.
Chan Master Yiqing succeeded Fushan as the lineage holder of the Caodong school.
After Qing attained realization, three years passed; Yuan then brought forth the fundamental principles of the Dongxia (Caodong) tradition and showed them to him.

Qing fully and subtly harmonized with them, whereupon [Yuan] bestowed upon him the Taiyang robe and sandals, saying: "Continue my legacy and carry on the tradition of the Dongshan school. Take good care of yourself."
Protect and uphold [this teaching]. Do not let it remain stagnant here, but cause Yuan Tongxiu to see it.
The seventh-generation patriarch of the Caodong school was named Yiqing.
He was the son of the Li family of Qingshe. Having attained the essential meaning under Fushan Yuanjian, he succeeded him.
Yang Zhengmai first resided at Haihui and subsequently moved to Touzi.
He was the seventh-generation successor in the Caodong lineage at Touzi, holding the ancestral succession for nineteen years.
Xiangfu Yin said: "To revive what has perished and continue what has been severed is for the Great Way to be held in common; this is a matter of supreme virtue throughout antiquity and the present.
When Qingzhu was at Mount Lu, he was engaged in reading the Tripitaka; it was not until the sixth year of the Xining era that he resided at Haihui in Longshu."
He truly succeeded to the seat of the patriarch Baiyun Dan. Eight years later, he moved to Touzi.
This was because the successor [to the lineage] felt that, as the authentic pulse of the Dongshan tradition already had its rightful place, it could not remain vacant for long.
Chan Master Tianbo was a successor in the lineage of Tiānyī Huáiyán.
Yuánjì studied under Tiānyī and attained realization of his fundamental intent. Huáiyán once remarked of him, "This is a 'thousand-li colt' of my own house."
When Lord Lu Gong Yanbo was stationed as governor in Weifu, he invited [Fayan] to reside at Tianbo Monastery. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The times are in decline;
few people now live to reach sixty or seventy years of age. You have entered my Dharma, yet your practice is not yet stable.
Before long, decay, illness, old age, and death will arrive. How much time remains? Why do you still remain so complacent?"
He departed in pure stillness throughout the first, middle, and last watches of the night. One day, Bo said to him, "I am entering nirvana.
Bo went personally to attend him and, holding the white lapis lazuli bottle he had been granted, prayed: "The Buddha-dharma is truly efficacious;
I pray that your relics will fill my bottle. It was exactly as he had wished. From then on, Bo devoted himself with utmost sincerity to the inner scriptures and diligently cultivated pure karma.
Emperor Yingzong (personal name Shu; reigned for four years).
In the Jiachen year, the first year of the ZhiPing era, Master Wenyue of Yunfeng on Mount Nanyue, a successor of Cuiyan, passed away.
Zhishou Yue was short and small in stature, yet possessed refined discernment. At the age of nineteen, he took up his staff and traveled through the Jianghuai region until he reached Dayu in Junzhou.
There he saw that the old monk’s quarters were dilapidated and desolate, like a roadside inn; Yue had no desire to stay. Just as he was about to depart, it began to rain.
When the rain ceased, Zhishou ascended the seat and said: "Everyone has gathered here to eat a stalk of vegetable soup. If you call it 'a stalk of vegetable soup,' you are mistaken."
"Entering hell will be like being struck by an arrow. He descended from his seat. There was no further speech. Yue was greatly startled and went to the Master’s chamber that night.
Zhi asked, "What do you seek in coming here? Yue replied, "I seek the Buddha-mind Dharma. Zhi said, "The Wheel of Dharma has not yet turned; the Wheel of Food must turn first.
You are a person of later birth with physical strength; why do you not beg for food for the sake of the assembly? I have no leisure even to endure hunger. He had no leisure.
"Shall I preach the Dharma for you? Yuanze did not refuse and immediately requested to go. Upon his return, he moved his residence to Mount Xishan at Cuoyan.
Yuanze went there once more to rely upon him. One night he visited the master’s chamber, and Zhizhe said, "Do you wish again to seek the Buddha-mind Dharma?
You do not consider that this newly occupied dwelling has thin walls and leaks, and it is cold and snowy. Day and night I have been waiting for you to come for the sake of the assembly."
Yang Yingtan said, "I cannot endure the cold; can you preach the Dharma for me? Huaiyue did not dare to refuse. He entered the city to collect charcoal and returned.
At that time, there was a vacancy for the position of *vina* (steward). Huaiyue went to the master’s quarters at night. Zhi said, "The Buddha-dharma does not fear being ruined.
The office of Hall Superintendent is now to be entrusted to you. Huaiyue could not speak in reply and departed. The next day, the gong was struck.

When Jianzhui earnestly invited him, Huiye showed an expression of reluctance; he rose with a bow as if wishing to depart. Since his labors had already been long and arduous, he desisted for the time being.
However, his resentment toward Zhizhe did not leave his mind. Later, while sitting on the ground by the rear rack, the bundle beneath the rack broke loose, and a bucket fell from the rack onto him.
Suddenly, he attained awakening, seeing at once how Zhizhe had previously employed such methods. He ran to put on his *kāṣāya* robe and went up to the sleeping quarters.
In the hall, Foyan Zhi greeted him with a smile and said, "Venerable Vinaya Master, rejoice! Your great task is now complete.
Xueyue bowed twice, perspiring profusely, and departed without uttering a single word. He served diligently for eight years until Zhi passed away. He then traveled east to the Three Wu regions;

wherever he went, the monastic communities were transformed. Xuedou especially revered him, and whenever he assembled the congregation for tea, he would specifically set out a seat for him as a mark of respect.

The ritual protocols were different. He left the world at Nanchang Cuoyan; before long, he resided at Falun Temple, where he personally supervised the supervision of grain-grinding and the reaping of crops.
He was pleased to see those arriving with bundles under their arms or on their backs, but when he saw those carrying loads on poles, he would knit his brows and say, "Not yet.
In another thirty years, you shall travel the roads on horseback. Soon after, he was transferred to Yunfeng, where he ascended the seat to take leave of the assembly.
He passed away peacefully. Upon cremation, five-colored śarīras were obtained and enshrined in a stupa north of Yuxi.
Chan Master Yihuai of Tiantaiyi was a successor in the lineage of Xuedou.
Huai succeeded Xuedou Xian. From Tiefo to Tianyi, he occupied five successive Dharma seats, all of which were in desolate locations;

wherever Huai arrived, he would miraculously manifest pavilions and halls, and the four requisites were fully provided. He later retired to Shengshou Monastery on Wujiang, and in his old age resided at Shanshan in Chizhou.
His disciple Zhicai was then abbot of Furi Monastery; he invited Huai back to serve him there. Zhicai subsequently went to Suzhou.
Before the city had returned, Huai urged him to come back. When he reached the gate, Huai said, "The time has come; I am going.
Zhai asked, "What words do you have to instruct your disciples? He then spoke this verse: "The red sun shines upon Fusang; cold clouds seal Mount Hua.
At the third watch, passing through the Iron Ring Mountains, I break off the horns of the black dragon. Zhai then asked, "The egg-shaped stupa is already completed; what then?"
"This is the ultimate matter," he said, raising his fist to show it. He then went to bed, struck his pillow, and passed away peacefully.
Chan Master Zongben appeared in the world at Ruiwang Monastery.
Ben was the son of the Guan family of Wuxi; his physical presence was robust and his speech was free of superfluous elaboration. At the age of nineteen, he took [a master] as his teacher.
Daosheng of Yong’an at Chengtian Monastery in Suzhou was highly esteemed within the monastic community; those who sought him out gathered like clouds.

Originally wearing tattered robes and with a soiled face, he attended to the well and mortar and managed the cooking and stoves to provide for the assembly. At night, he would enter the meditation hall to investigate the Way.
Daosheng said to him, "As a dhūta, you labor greatly for the sake of the assembly; are you not weary? He replied, "If I were to abandon even a single dharma..."
He did not consider this to be the fulfillment of Bodhi; truly desiring to realize it through his own body in this life, how could he dare speak of weariness? Shengyin marveled at him.

After ten years had passed, he finally shaved his head and received full ordination. He then served diligently for another three years before taking leave of Shengyin to travel widely to seek instruction from various masters.

Arriving at Jingde in Chiyang, he paid his respects to Chan Master Yihuai. Upon hearing the Master’s words, he attained realization; he then served as an attendant. None among the assembly were aware of this.
[Yihuai] was fond of sleeping, and his snoring was loud enough to be heard. Those who found it annoying reported it to Yihuai, who said, "This youth is the banner of diligence for my house.
You all shall depend upon him in the future; do not speak of this much. Yihuai resided there.
During the reign of Emperor Shousheng, the Transport Commissioner Li Fugui passed through Huai. During a night conversation, he remarked, "The Dharma seat at Rui Guang is vacant;
I wish for a monk of true realization to preside over it. At that time, Yuanben was seated in the assembly. Huai pointed to him and said, "There is no one more suited than this Way-man.
Li Fugui subsequently invited Ben to take charge of Rui Guang. On the day of the opening of the hall, the assembly gathered and struck the drum; as the drum rolled, [the sound] swirled.
The earth shook and reverberated in a circular motion, causing the assembly to recoil in alarm. A monk stepped forward and said, "This is an auspicious sign of the Dharma-thunder shaking the earth.
As soon as he finished speaking, the monk vanished. The Dharma assembly flourished daily, with the congregation constantly numbering five hundred.
Chan Master Zhenji of Cuiyan under Shishuang was about to pass away.
He manifested an illness that was extremely severe; he spread straw mats upon the ground and rolled about without ceasing for even a moment.
Attendant Zhe wept as he said, "Throughout your life you reviled the Buddhas and scolded the Patriarchs; why now have you become like this? Zhen looked at him intently and rebuked him, saying:
"Do you also hold such a view? Having said this, he sat cross-legged, called for his attendant to burn incense, and as the smoke rose, he entered nirvana.
In the second year of the Yisi era, Chan Master Fayan traveled from Ruiwang to Fushan, where he attended upon National Teacher Chuanzi, attained enlightenment, and was assigned a seat alongside him.

Yan was the son of the Deng family of Ba Xi. In his youth, he shaved his head and received full ordination. He traveled to lecture halls in Chengdu to study the *Śataśāstra* and the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi*, penetrating their profound depths.
Setting them aside, he remarked, "How can one play the lute by fixing the tuning pegs? It is impossible. Carrying his book-cases on his back, he departed through the mountain passes.
Wherever he went, there was no one whose understanding met his own expectations. He visited Renguang Ben and recounted all the causes and conditions from ancient and modern times;
however, he could not resolve the case of a monk asking Xinghua, "What is it like when [guests] come from the four quarters?
Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the middle. The monk bowed, and Xinghua said, "Yesterday I attended a village feast, and on the way back I encountered a sudden..."
During a sudden gale and torrential rain, he sought refuge in an ancient temple. He requested further instruction from Yuanben, who said, "This is a matter concerning the lineage of Linji;
you must ask one of his descendants. Thereupon, he went to visit Fushan Yuan.
When asked for further instruction on their previous conversation, Faryan said, "I have a parable.
You are just like a wood-seller from a village of three households who stands at a crossroads with a flat carrying pole, asking people, 'What matters is the Council of State discussing today?
Yanmo thought to himself, "If this is so, then there is still much that remains unfulfilled. Faryan knew his thoughts.
Yan perceived that his faculties were of a different caliber. One day he said to him, "I am old; I fear you will let your precious time pass in vain.
You should go and rely upon Baiyun. Although this elder is junior to me in years, I have not yet met him in person.

However, having seen his verse on the story of Linji’s three blows of the staff, I know he possesses a capacity that transcends ordinary men; he will surely enable you to realize the Great Matter. Yan wept as he took his leave and traveled to [Baiyun].
Baiyun saw him from afar and said, "Chuan Lazuo, have you come? He then raised the story of a monk asking Nanquan about the *maṇi* jewel for questioning.
Baiyun rebuked him. Later, Baiyun showed him the circumstances regarding the Buddha’s secret words and Kāśyapa not concealing them;
however, after a long time, he had not yet attained realization. One day, as he was hurrying up the hall from the corridor, his state of doubt—
He immediately ceased [his labor] and offered this verse of realization: "A small patch of idle land before the mountain; With palms joined, I earnestly questioned my forefather.
How many times have I sold it only to buy it back? Out of love for the pines and bamboos, it draws in the pure breeze.
The Patriarch specifically certified him, saying, "The Zen of the thorny jujube fruit belongs to you," and ordered him to take charge of the mill. One day, a monk saw him at the mill.
As he turned, he suddenly pointed and asked, "Is this supernatural power (*abhijñā*), or is it the natural order of things (*dharmatā*)? Zhenyan lifted his robes and spun in a full circle;
the monk remained silent. Before long, the Patriarch arrived and said to Zhenyan, "Several Zen practitioners have come here from Mount Lu."
In every case, there was a point of awakening and entry. When instructed to speak, he could indeed speak with a clear source; when asked about causes and conditions, he understood them clearly;
and when instructed to offer a phrase, he was able to offer one. Yet, it was simply not yet sufficient. Yuan was greatly perplexed by this.
He thought to himself, "I have already attained awakening; I can speak it and I can clarify it. Why then am I still not 'there'?
He then spent several days investigating this, until suddenly he attained realization. All that he had previously cherished was cast aside at once.
He went to see the Patriarch, who began to dance with hands and feet; Yan simply smiled. Yan later said, "Because of me..."
"Right now, I have broken out into a cold sweat, and I have clearly attained a refreshing breeze from a thousand autumns.

One day, the Patriarch addressed the assembly, saying, "An ancient said, 'It is like casting an image in a mirror. Once the image is formed, where is the mirror? The assembly offered various responses, none of which were in accord with the truth.
He brought up the question for Yan, who stepped forward and paid his respects, saying, "It is not much of a matter. The Patriarch smiled and said, "You must..."
This Way was first attained; he then commanded that a seat be shared, so as to reveal it to those yet to come.
Xiangfu Yin said: "The ancients had clear eyes and impartial minds; they did not deceive later students.

Observe how the ancient Buddha Xuefeng [treated] Fengxue (when Fengxue was with Xuefeng, he requested instruction on Linji’s 'Four Guests and Hosts. Xuefeng said: "At that time, I was traveling with Yantou and Qinshan to study under Linji. We encountered Linji...")

He has already passed away. The Elder must understand this point; one must question his descendants before one can truly know him. Later, Fengxue recounted this to Nanyuan, who sighed and said, "Xuefeng was an ancient Buddha," and he bowed toward him from afar.
One can perceive the vastness of his mind—like the clear blue sky and the bright sun—from the fact that Rui Guang traced his lineage back to the Fifth Patriarch.
Within a single word or half-sentence, the ancients could see through to a person’s entire life. Observe the Hermit of Lotus Peak.
One could recognize the descendants of Yunmen through a single turning word; Fushan Yuan knew that Baiyun possessed a quality surpassing others through a single verse.
One can thus imagine his eyes, like purple lightning and clear frost.
When it came to Yan, he threw himself into the occasion, and his "downward-borne pure breeze" was clearly realized only after the profuse sweat of his own emergence. How profound this is!
Awakening must be thorough; the Great Dharma must be clearly understood.
In short, only by not deceiving oneself can one avoid deceiving others. Buddhas and patriarchs are those who do not deceive themselves and do not deceive others.
What else is there to the study of the Way?
The third year of Bingwu.
Jicui moved south to Huanglong.
Kewen led the assembly, Qingxian served as the guest master, Huiyuan was the attendant, and De Pu [served] based on his principles from the two rivers.
Hutou came from Mianzhou to join the assembly after abandoning his lectures; his refined demeanor brought together the height of contemporary excellence, rivaling the eras of Mazu and Baizhang.
Jingyin Liai again petitioned for permission to return to the mountains, and the Emperor granted his request.

Liai submitted another memorial requesting to leave, offering this verse: "A thousand clusters of clouds and mountains, ten thousand valleys of flowing streams— With a heart intent on returning, I shall grow old upon this peak's crest.
For the remainder of my life, I vow to pray for boundless longevity; A single incense stick of pure fragrance fills the stone pavilion. The Emperor [read it].
An official decree was issued, stating: "The Chan Master Huailian of Dajue Temple has enjoyed the sacred favor of the late Emperor and has been repeatedly bestowed with imperial edicts.
Having frequently submitted his sincere petition to return to the forest retreats, we now grant his request so that he may pursue his heart’s tranquility.

Whenever he passes through minor monasteries, he shall reside there according to his own inclination; however, in the case of ten-direction Zen forests (monasteries of the public sangha), he must not be pressured or detained."

I request that you take it with you and return east; few will understand it. The Magistrate of Siming welcomed it and enshrined it at Yuyang Monastery, where the assembly constructed the Chenkui Pavilion.
When Su Shi, the Hanlin Academician, was serving as Governor of Hangzhou, he sent a letter inquiring about it, saying:

"I have learned that you require an inscription for the Chenkui Pavilion. I have already composed it. Being aged and having long neglected my studies, I do not know if it is worthy of being carved upon stone. I have seen it.

Sāṃliao said: "When the Chan Master departed from the capital, Emperor Ying bestowed upon him a handwritten edict. Its purport stated: 'He shall reside and preside over the monastery according to his own inclination.
I do not know for certain whether this was actually granted; I earnestly request that you record and show me the full text so that I may add this passage [to my records].
Liai, however, ultimately concealed it and did not let it out. Only after Liai had passed away was it found within his chest."
Dingwei, the fourth year (in the twelfth month, the cuckoo cried out in Luoyang).
Emperor Shenzong (personal name Xu, reigned for eighteen years).
Wushen, the first year of Xining under Emperor Shenzong.
In the fourth year, the Jisi (1069) year, National Teacher Hui-nan of Huanglong under the lineage of Chan Master Shishuang passed away.

On the first day of the third month, Fourth Patriarch Foyan delivered a discourse on the *Fasishi* (Book of Dharma Succession). Nan ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk’s talent is slight and his virtue..."
How could I, being so shallow, be fit to be a teacher of men? It is simply that I have not been ignorant of my original mind, nor have I deceived the various sages.

Where others had not yet escaped birth and death, I have now escaped birth and death; where others had not yet left the cycle of saṃsāra, I have now left the cycle of saṃsāra; where others had not yet attained liberation, I have now attained liberation.
"Lacking mastery before, one now attains mastery. Therefore, when the Greatly Awakened World-Honored One was with Dīpaṃkara Buddha, there was not a single dharma that could be attained.
At midnight at Huangmei, what did the Sixth Patriarch transmit? He then spoke a verse, saying:
'Attained or not attained, transmitted or not transmitted— When the root is reached and the meaning obtained, what more need be said? I recall Shoushan..."
He had previously leaked [his secret]. One day, his daughter-in-law rode a donkey while her mother-in-law led it. On the following day at noon, he sat in the lotus posture and passed away.
Upon cremation, five-colored *śarīra* relics were found. His stupa was erected on the mountain in front. To the south, he was like Cuiyan Yue; he studied under Fuchang Weishan.

At that time, it happened that he was afflicted by a cold. Having taken medicine and broken into a sweat, he went with his fellow practitioners to borrow blankets everywhere, but none were to be found.

Those who possessed paper quilts all claimed they were too worn out from old age; such cases were indeed numerous. They sighed together and said, "Master Shan is truly a man of the mountains in his true essence.
When the Dharma flourished in the south, monastics from Jing, Hu, Jiang, and Hai provinces would flock there in constant numbers of over a hundred."
There was no place to lodge for the night, and the area was frequently plagued by bandits and robbers.

Chan Master Xinghua Shaoxian, who was about fifty *li* away, provided a guest house and ordered the abbot to manage it for the purpose of receiving travelers, allowing them to stay, eat, and depart. Monks from all quarters held his conduct in high esteem.
Xian was a worthy successor of Beichan; after his passing, when his body was cremated, his eyes did not decay, and his two intestines remained coiled and intact.
It was like iron.
Xiangfu Yin said: "Huanglong attained samādhi within the prison and used the three barriers to block the vital fords of the world.
Monks from all quarters flocked to him like wild ducks; together with Yangqi, they were known as the 'Two Gates of Ambrosia. Thus it was.
Had it not been for Yunfeng Yue’s strenuous efforts in pointing this out, how could it have been that [the teaching] did not flow away like quicksilver or silver?
Alas! How can the achievement of teacher and friend ever be extinguished?
Chan Master Zuxin succeeded to the abbacy of Huanglong.

Initially, he had studied under Yunfeng Yue for three years; finding him difficult to penetrate due to his solitary firmness, he went to Huangbo, where he attained the essential meaning. Nanji [was his successor].
The assembly requested that Xinxu should remain, but Xinxu wished to appoint Yuanji to take his place. Yuanji shook his head and departed directly;
Xinxu subsequently succeeded him on the seat. Huiyuan resided at Shousheng Temple in Wujiang and sent a monk to Huanglong to present a letter of succession to the Dharma.
Looking at the inscription on the seal, he said, "I have momentarily forgotten this monk. He told the special envoy, "Do not open the letter yet;
you may have him come in person to see me, the old monk. The envoy returned with his report. Yuan immediately set out with his pack on his back and arrived at Nanchang.
Hearing that Nan had already passed away, he stayed there in deep lamentation. Just then, Zuxin came out of the city; they met and conversed.
He marveled at this, saying, "I regret that the Master did not live to see this.
Chan Master Qingxian resided at Longqing Monastery in Jizhou.
Having left home to travel afar, wherever he stayed, he rarely engaged with others; yet whenever someone approached him, he would [respond] with a single gesture.
He took his leave and went to serve Master Jicui Nan. Nan held him in high esteem. Zhang Jian, the Governor of Luling, invited him to reside at Longqing Monastery.
When Chan Master Xingwei came to dwell at Mount Yang, [the Master] followed him there.
Daowei first received the teachings of the Xianshou school from the Tripitaka Master of Taiyuan.

At the encouragement of his fellow students, he abandoned his lecturing and visited Nanxun, where he attained realization during the summer retreat at Jicui. He resided at Yangshan, where his Dharma assembly became preeminent throughout the Jianghuai region; all those among his former associates who were well-known gathered there.
Daowei managed affairs with strict ritual propriety; he once dispatched twelve members of his community on a mission, using their names [to identify them].

He entrusted the *vinaya-dhara* (karmadāna) with instructions that they should all come the following day to receive detailed instructions and attend the tea ceremony. However, one person was invariably missing.
When Wei asked who it was, the reply was, "Yongtai. While Wei was busy with his arrangements, the head seat said, "Tai has gone off to visit the mountains;
please appoint another monk to fill the vacancy. Wei agreed. Shortly thereafter, someone reported, "Tai is actually here," but the head seat concealed this fact.

[He did this] merely to deceive the assembly. Daowei’s countenance was grave and dignified, and he had him search for [the items]. Daotai himself confessed his timidity and weakness, fearing he would fail in the duties he had received;
yet the Head Seat (shouzuo) truly knew nothing of it. Daowei ordered the bell to be struck to assemble the congregation and said:

"The Head Seat has already shared the seat and transmitted the Way; furthermore, he is one whom our Master personally recognized. To deceive the masses with a darkened heart—this would be unacceptable even for anyone else."
"Would you rather willingly destroy yourself? He then left the monastery together with Tai. All quarters were moved by his impartiality.
The Chan Master was a descendant of Huanglong at Lengtang Hongyingji in Longxing.
Ying read the *Huayan Shiming Lun* (The Treatise on the Ten Clarifications of the Avataṃsaka), through which he illuminated the mind-ground (*cittabhūmi*).

He went to Jicui to receive the seal of approval (*mudrā*), and later met Cuiyan Zhen; at that time, scholars of all quarters flocked to him. While residing at Letan, for six months the administrative officials were in conflict.
When they could not be restrained, on the ninth day of the month, he said to the assembly: "That I lead this community without discipline is precisely because I lack virtue. I feel ashamed."

Huanglong called for the *karmadāna* to strike the bell to assemble the community. He recounted the beginning and end of his travels as a wandering monk, saying: "After my passing, I shall be cremated;
my remains shall be enshrined in the Puguang Pagoda (*Pǔtōng Tǎ*). This clarifies that life and death are never separate from the pure assembly."
In the third year of the Gengxu cycle, Chan Master Yuanyou established the Dailin Monastery in Tanzhou as his seat of teaching. (The rise and fall of Chan monasteries are not generally recorded;
this entry is made because Yuanyou was able to embody the standard of a true patriarch.)

Fayou succeeded Huanglong Nan. His wisdom and eloquence were innate, and his spirit surpassed his contemporaries. After Nan passed away, Fayou traveled to Xiang and Heng, where he was followed by a multitude of monastics;
his reputation grew weighty throughout Jingzhou and Chu. When Xie Shizhi governed Tanzhou, he wished to restore the Chan tradition at Donglin Monastery, a former site for the Vinaya school.
He treated Fayou with the utmost courtesy and invited him to serve as the first patriarch. Fayou joyfully consented to come. Donglin was like a honeycomb.
Like ant-hills, they appeared one after another in successive layers; the abundance of their iconography was unsurpassed in the region west of the Xiang River.
When [Wang] You leveled the site to create a spacious hall and meditation chambers to assemble scholars from all under heaven, the laborers did not dare to destroy the established icons.
Dōyū personally discarded them in the river, saying: "In the past, they were originally unformed; how could they now be destroyed? My Dharma is non-existent;
how could the sentiments of ordinary people harbor the understanding of a sage? After six years, the halls and pavilions were completed in grand splendor.
In the fourth year of the Xinhai cycle, Chan Master Ju-ne—the fifth generation descendant of Yunmen at Lushan Yuan Tong—passed away.
Ju-ne had resided at Yuan Tong for twenty years and subsequently moved to two monasteries, Sizushi Kaiyuan and another. In every forest monastery he visited, [he brought great benefit].

He was renowned as the foremost [of his peers]. Having grown old, he retired to live at Baoci Rock (Baojiyan). His conduct toward the assembly was simple and dignified; he did not speak or smile frivolously.
He frequently practiced meditative concentration (*samādhi*). At first, his hands remained naturally folded in the *añjali* gesture; by midnight, they gradually rose until they reached his chest.
His attendants would watch him constantly to gauge the time for the cock’s crow. Such was his diligence. After three months, he passed away without illness.
In the fifth year, the Renzi year, Chan Master Kewen began teaching the Dharma at Shengshou Monastery.
Wen was the son of the Zheng family in Zhongnan, Shanfu. Having torn his scholar’s robes to leave the household life, he abandoned formal lectures and traveled south, where he visited Yunju Shun.
They did not reach an accord. Having heard of the reputation of Yunfeng Yue, he traveled by double stages to visit him.
Upon his arrival, Yue had already passed away. He sighed and said, "Since that man is no more, where else could I go? Though the mountains and waters are beautiful, I have no leisure to travel them.
He spent the summer retreat at Daming and subsequently went to Huanglong. At first, they did not reach an accord, whereupon [Huanglong] remarked, "This old fellow is merely a practitioner..."
The itinerant monk did not understand my words and departed. He went to see Xiangcheng Shun and obtained insight into the application of the Southern School.
He returned to Huanglong to serve as the Head Seat (Shouzuo) and succeeded him in the Dharma. Later, Qian Yi, the Governor of Gaoyang, invited him to take charge of the world at Shengshou Monastery.
When Wén was having a meal at the home of a local official, the messenger arrived and he fled. Dozens of people who had been sitting with him were arrested.
Some of them were seen at a temple on Mount Xīnfēng, where they bowed their heads and wept, saying, "If you, Master, had not gone, our group would have suffered.
Wén said, "Because of me, you have been brought to such distress; therefore, I shall accept [the responsibility]. Thereupon, he propagated the Dharma.
Chan Master Daoguang presided over the Dharma at Lingyan in Pingjiang.
His spiritual practice was preeminent, and he was revered by those both near and far. On the day he took up residence as abbot, the Duke of Jing, Wang Anshi, sent him a poem which said:
"In the depths of a hundred flowers lies the temple, Yet it still points toward the old palaces of Wu. The events have passed and the people are gone; The incense has faded..."

The path is already empty; this morning I see you, Master, depart. Here on this ground, the spirit of our school shall be propagated. Parting sentiment mingled with homesickness lingers upon the clouds and trees to the east.
This is the record of Chan Master Chisong (Ji), the fifth generation descendant of Yunmen, known as Furi Mingjiao.
Sengjū resided at Furi Temple and later retired to the Yong’an Aranya. After his passing, he was cremated;
his eyes, tongue, and the cranial bone of his youthful body remained indestructible. The śarīra were red and white, crystalline and pure, as large as soybeans.
The ninth-generation successor of Linji, Patriarch Baiyun, entered parinirvāṇa.
Having resided at Baiyun, he manifested his transformative power at Longmen and Xinghua, occupying the seat of enlightenment on six occasions. Wherever he went, the assembly gathered like clouds.
He lived to the age of forty-eight.

The Tenth Patriarch of the Linji Lineage.
His taboo name was Fayuan; he succeeded Baiyun.

In the sixth year of the Xining era (the Gui-chou year), during the reign of Emperor Shenzong, he became the tenth-generation successor of Linji and the fifth patriarch to inherit the ancestral lineage (in the thirty-first year).
The Patriarch resided at Shuangquan Chan Monastery on Mount Shimian in Shuzhou.
Wan’an Yan said: "When the Master Yuan initially resided at Mount Shimian, he lived in solitary seclusion for two years before a Daoist priest came to inquire about the Way;
the Master then invited him to serve as the administrative head (zhishi). Another three years passed before the monk Baoliang arrived."
He visited the Daoist master morning and evening, and in all instances attained the Dharma.
Thereupon, Master Zu’s Way gradually became known to others, and students from the four quarters began to arrive in small numbers.
Although his disciples later became renowned throughout the world, throughout his life he never exceeded several dozen followers.
Caoqi Zushi resided at Baiyun Shanhuai Temple.
After the Master returned from Mount Lu to Longshu, the clergy and laity requested that he reside at Baiyun Shanhuai Temple;
he truly succeeded to the seat of Master Duan. He ascended the hall. A monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you inherit? The Master [replied].
The monk said, "Before the Age of Majestic Sound, a single arrow pierced through two layers of mountains. The Master asked, "What is this matter that has been transmitted?
The Patriarch said, "It is entirely because of the moon over Huai that it can illuminate the spring of Yingyang. The monk said, "If that is so, then one sees the tall man upon entering the water.
The Patriarch said, "One knows only that the jade of Jing is extraordinary; how could one discern the mind of the King of Chu? The monk bowed in prostration. The Patriarch—
He struck it with his whisk.
This was the seventh year, Jia-yin;
the eighth year, Yi-mao.
The Chan Master Faquan resided at Nanqian Monastery in Quzhou, where the layman Zhao Bian followed him to attain realization. Faquan was the dharma heir of Yunju Shunsi.
Zhao Bian’s courtesy name was Yuedao, and his sobriquet was Zhifeizi (The One Who Knows His Errors). Upon reaching the rank of Zhongshu, he served as a Censor-in-Chief.
Throughout his life, he always carried with him a lute and a crane. Whatever he did during the day, he would invariably burn incense to report it at night.

The Heavenly Master was originally an external friend of Tianbao. When they met at Nanchan Monastery in Quzhou, Tianbao would visit daily to seek instruction, yet Tianbao never once permitted him to utter a single word.
Later, while serving as the governor of Qingzhou, Tianbao frequently sat in meditation during his leisure from official affairs.

Suddenly, a great thunderclap resounded. He immediately attained awakening and composed a verse, saying: Sitting in silence in the public hall, leaning idly on my armrest, The source of the mind was unmoving, as still as water.
A single stroke of thunder opened the gate atop my head, Awakening that which has been my own from the very beginning.
Lifting my head to the vast azure sky, joy follows upon joy. In every land and every atom, there is nothing that is not thus. Those of middling or inferior capacity cannot hear this;
it is merely the wondrous application of spiritual powers. When Gaomo heard this, he laughed and said, "Zhao Yuedao has simply struck lucky."
Bian once replied in a letter to Fu Bi, stating briefly:

"I humbly reflect that the 'separate transmission outside the teachings' of the Western Sage was not established for those of middling or inferior capacities. Those of superior wisdom enter through sudden awakening."
Once attained, it is attained forever. The ignorant, however, remain deluded and do not return; thus there arise a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions.
Only the Buddhas and Patriarchs have transmitted mind-to-mind. When the necessity arose to benefit sentient beings and engage with the world, they employed various expedient means:
blows and shouts, fists and pointing fingers, raising eyebrows and blinking eyes, striking the mallet and holding up the whisk, as well as speech, words, and texts. Since the time of the Sage...
As time has passed, students from all quarters have forgotten the root while pursuing the branches and abandoned the source to follow the waves;
such is the case everywhere, and they are truly objects of pity. Your servant, Bai, being unworthy, was in Qingzhou at the beginning of last autumn.

Having been moved by certain realizations, I have come to know my original nature to some extent—as it is neither deficient nor superfluous. As the ancients called it, this is the Dharma-gate of peace and bliss.
Truly, faith is not in vain. Recently, I was honored by the Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant to seek out the records of the Śākyamuni’s transmission.
As I have long been favored by your benevolence and discipline, hearing this news filled me with such joy and exhilaration that I could not help but dance with my hands and stamp my feet.

I humbly observe that your Excellency’s wealth and honor reach such an ultimate height, your virtue and wisdom are so magnificent, and your blessings, longevity, health, and tranquility are so perfectly complete. I shall now withdraw.

Your leisure and ease have reached such heights that the one matter to which you have not yet paid much heed is the Tathāgata’s Great Cause and Condition (*ekamahā-kṛtya-hetu-pratyaya*). Now, having again attained realization and entry into the true nature (*tathatā*), I venture to offer my congratulations to your Excellency. Attendant Zhu had traveled to the gates of the two elders with his medical knowledge. He said to Yuanping, "Lord Du is a great man in the world; it is a pity he does not yet know this matter. Why do you not exhort him to take it up? Yuanping replied, "Your karmic affinity with this elder is more mature than mine;

I can only assist him. One day, Zhenruo summoned Zhu to examine his pulse with great urgency. Zhu told the messenger, "Go first and inform the Chancellor, saying only that you have not yet finished reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. The messenger hurried back to report this. Zhenruo remained silent for a long while before finally arriving.

Zhenruo said, "I considered you a man of broad learning and capable understanding, yet I did not expect that recently you too have fallen into the ranks of the mediocre and dull-witted. As for what is called the *Śūraṅgama*, what kind of words are these that you are so addicted to them? The subtle words of the Sage do not go beyond—"

"To abandon this and adopt that [the latter] regarding Confucius and Mencius is a great delusion. Zhu said, "Since you, Excellency, have not read this scripture, how can you know it does not equal Confucius and Mencius? From my perspective, it seems to surpass them. He then produced the first volume from his sleeve and said:

"Your Excellency, please examine this. Yan took it and looked at it silently; before he knew it, he had finished the entire scroll. Suddenly, he rose in great alarm and said, "How could such a book exist in this world? He dispatched a messenger to bring all the remaining scrolls, which he read through completely. Then, seizing Zhu’s hand, he said:

"You are truly my spiritual friend; Master An Dao knows this. Why did you not tell me? He immediately ordered his carriage to visit Zhiping. Zhiping said, "It is like a person who has lost an object and suddenly finds it again; one should simply rejoice at having found it, rather than regretting the lateness of the discovery.

It was not that I did not wish to inform you, but because your karmic affinity with Master Zhu was deep, I sent him instead. Even when Buddhas and Patriarchs transform beings, they must rely on those with whom they share common karma. Yuan Yan was greatly pleased.
(Yuan Yan, courtesy name Shichang, was titled the 'Pure and Incorruptible Chancellor' during the Qingli era and was enfeoffed as the Duke of Qi.)
Chan Master Jingduan resided at Xiyu in Huzhou.
Duān was the son of the Qiu family of Wuxing. He left home to become a monk, received full ordination, and studied the teachings of the Tiantai school.

While listening to the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, upon reaching the section on the "Seven Investigations and Eight Returns," he knelt and composed a verse, saying: "The seven places where the mind was investigated failed to find it; I am dazed and bewildered, O..."
It is difficult not to have a sudden flash of realization; it simply requires that you investigate until you see the state of no-mind.
This too is like pouring a clod of earth into the mud. The teaching of the "Eight Returns" has been transmitted for a long time; from of old, the ancestral styles have each been analyzed and divided.

Even if one reaches the point where there is no longer anything to return to, it is still like a shrimp leaping but unable to get out of its basket. He then composed a verse for a separate recitation, saying: Winding and twisting...
"With a door-knob: each time one picks it up, one more sorrow arises. It would be better to become a Zen monk; when you reach the state of no-mind, simply rest.
When Chan Master Canqi reached this point, he attained silent realization within the room. He immediately stepped out onto the courtyard, turned his body around, and threw himself down.
Canqi granted him approval (*inka*). Later, upon seeing a lion being played with, he was further awakened. Thereupon, he fashioned a lion out of colored silk.
He wore a lion skin and was thus called Duan Shizi (Lion Duan). He resided in Xi-yu, which was close to Huzhou.
On snowy mornings, he would enter the city dressed in colorful robes; children vied with one another to shout and chase after him, while he begged for money from those he encountered.
Whenever he obtained something, he would immediately give it to the poor. He frequently recited the *Lotus Sūtra* and was also fond of singing the lyrics of the "Fisherman.
There was a mad monk named Houtou who deluded the masses with heterodox ways;

while he was eating meat with Lü Gongfang, the Governor of Runzhou, Zhi ended by walking straight up to him and pointed, saying, "At this very moment, what is the Buddha? Houtou was so distressed that he had no reply.
Duan struck him on the head, pushed him over, and departed. There was also a sorcerer named Buto who excavated an image of a Buddha from outside the city walls of Xiuzhou and erected a stupa upon it;
the entire city venerated it with faith. Duan saw this, seized him, and asked:
"What is the Buddha? [The Master] did not rely on conjecture or deliberation; he simply took a step and departed.
The ninth year was Bingchen;
the tenth year was Dingyi.
When the Patriarch was residing at Taiping,
he addressed the assembly: "Were one to take the waters of the four great oceans as a single inkstone and Mount Sumeru as a single writing brush,
and were someone to write the five characters 'The Meaning of the Patriarch’s Coming from the West' in the midst of empty space, Taiping would descend from his seat and perform a full prostration."
He sat on his sitting mat and prostrated to his teacher. If one cannot transcribe [the teachings], the Buddha-dharma will have no spiritual efficacy.
A monk asked, "What is the matter of the Linji lineage? The Patriarch said, "The five heinous crimes hearing thunder. He asked, "What is the matter of the Yunmen lineage?"
The Patriarch said, "A red banner flashes. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter of the Cao-Dong school? The Patriarch said, "The letter is sent, but it does not reach home.
[The monk] asked, "What is the matter of the Guiyang school? The Patriarch said, "A broken stele lies across the ancient road. The monk bowed.
The Patriarch said, "Why do you not ask about the matter of the Linji school? [The monk] said, "I leave that for the Master. The Patriarch said, "The patrolman."
He committed the offense of being out past curfew. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Patriarch said, "Bare-chested and barefoot. [The monk] asked, "What is the Dharma?
The Patriarch said, "A general amnesty, with no exceptions. [The monk] asked, "What is the Sangha? The Patriarch said, "Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat."
The first year of the Yuanfeng era, the year Wumu (1078 CE), Chan Master Daokai arrived at Haihui and attained realization.

In his youth, Daokai studied the art of fasting from grains and lived in seclusion on Mount Yiyang. Later, he underwent the *śrāmaṇera* ordination by reciting the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*. He then went to visit Qingzhu at...
In the Sea Assembly, Nanquan asked, "The teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are like the daily tea and rice of a household. Aside from these, is there anything else for the sake of others?
Nanquan said, "Tell me, when the Son of Heaven issues an edict within the realm, does he still require the aid of Yao, Shun, Yu, or Tang?
As Guizong was about to offer a word in response, Nanquan struck him on the mouth with his whisk and said, "From the moment you first conceived this intention."
"Thirty blows for you early on! At this, Xuefeng Kai was suddenly enlightened; he prostrated himself and then departed. The Patriarch called out, "Wait a moment, *śramaṇa*! But Kai paid him no heed.
The Patriarch said, "Have you reached the stage of non-doubt? Kai covered his ears with his hands.

Later, when Kai served as the head cook (*karmadāna*), the Patriarch remarked, "The duties of the kitchen are no easy matter. Kai replied, "I am not afraid. The Patriarch asked, "How do you prepare the rice porridge?"
"Is it steamed rice? Kai said, "The laborers wash the rice and set the fire; the practitioners cook the gruel and steam the rice.
The Patriarch asked, "What are you doing? Kai said, "Out of compassion, Master, please let them go about their work in peace.

One day, while attending the Patriarch as they walked through the vegetable garden, the Patriarch handed his staff to Kai. Kai took it and followed along. The Patriarch said, "This is what is appropriate."
"Is it so? Guishan said. "Carrying the Master’s shoes and holding his staff for him would not be considered an extra burden.
Mazu said, "There is another companion here. Guishan said, "Which one of them does not accept the teaching? Mazu stopped there.

That evening, he asked Guishan, "The conversation we had earlier was not yet finished. Guishan said, "I ask the Master to bring it up. Mazu said, "Born in the hour of the Rabbit; born in the month of the Dog."
Jiakai immediately came to light the lamp. The Patriarch said, "Your coming up and going down has never been in vain.
Jiakai replied, "Being by the side of the Master, it was only natural to act thus. The Patriarch said, "Every household has its servants and maids."
Kai said, "The Master is advanced in years; we cannot do without you. The Patriarch said, "You are so earnest. Kai replied, "I shall have my share in repaying your kindness.
This was the second year of the Jiwu era.
Chan Master Chenghao resided at Taiyang.
Hao was the son of the Wang family of Mizhou; having seen Guangfeng of Beita clarify the essentials of the awakened mind, he attained a mastery that moved as freely as the wind.
In the *Mahāśvara-samādhi*, it is prescribed that one should wear a loincloth (*goṇī-kaupīna*), inscribe the names of the patriarchs of successive generations upon it, and don it.

It says: "Only Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are slightly superior [to these]. Furthermore, one should write [the names] upon a sash. Those from various quarters called this the "white cloth loincloth" (*hào bù kūn*).
A monk imitated this practice. When Hào saw him, he rebuked him, saying: "What principle do you possess to dare to act in such a way? At that time...
"It will be of no avail to vomit blood. Before half a year had passed, that monk indeed died from vomiting blood.

When Zhang Shangying was serving as an envoy to the southwestern region of the capital, he heard of his reputation and invited him to reside at Taiyang Monastery in Yingzhou. At that time, Guoyin was already advanced in years and leading the assembly;

Guoyin was greatly delighted and said, "The head seat of my mountain is now appearing in the world. He gathered a vast assembly of both monastics and laypeople and requested him to ascend the seat to preach.
Xin Yan. Hào ascended the seat and said, "I, Hào, have resided at Guyin for ten years, yet I have never drunk a single drop of Guyin’s water nor chewed a single grain of Guyin’s rice.
If you do not understand this, come to Taiyang and I shall explain it to you.
Carrying his staff, he descended from the seat and departed without looking back.
In the third year of the Gengshen cycle, Chan Master Jingyin Daozhen responded to an imperial decree to preach the Dharma for the posthumous benefit of Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian.
Daozhen was the son of the Dai family of Gutian; having traveled everywhere with his single almsbowl, he attained the essential meaning under Fushan Yuan and subsequently went north to visit Jing...
Because of Yuanlian, he was appointed to the foremost seat among the assembly. Upon Yuanlian’s return home, [Fahai] succeeded him on that throne.

On the day he opened the hall for his first sermon, an imperial messenger descended to offer incense and bestowed upon him purple robes and the master title "Juezhao" (Awakened Illumination). In the capital, there were myriad reports—both favorable and unfavorable—and the doors of the nobility and high officials were filled with visitors.
Having seen him once, ten thousand mouths spoke in diverse ways; all considered him a practitioner of true substance, and there was none who did not [hold this view].

He was treated with even greater reverence. In the spring, when the Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian passed away, an imperial decree was issued for him to come to the Qingshou Palace to preach the Dharma.

An expansive seat was prepared, and the audience was permitted to engage in question-and-answer sessions. Those from high and low, from left and right, heard the Dharma and attained what they had never experienced before; their cries of joy shook the palace precincts.
Furthermore, the Imperial Edict was bestowed upon Chan Master Jingzhao, who transmitted it to Dongshan.
Entering the hall, Dongshan said: "In the school of Dongshan, if you wish to speak, speak; if you wish to act, act. You may save your eyebrows, but you will lose your head."
He pinched his own nostrils and then shouted, "Long rain, no sun. *Chān*!
Daoyang Hao moved from Yuyuan to Taiyang.
While Hao resided at Taiyang for several months, Li Shenyan, the Commissioner of Transport for Jingnan, and Sun Jingxiu... [together...]
He was invited to reside at Jade Spring Jingde Chan Monastery in Dangyang. His spiritual acumen was solitary and sharp; students were unable to approach or settle upon him.

At that time, there was a vacancy for the position of Head Seat (Śraddhācārya). The Rector said, "Such-and-such a person and such-and-such a person have both established the monastic community at such-and-such places."

He was sought after by the assembly of meditators, and it would have been appropriate to invite him to serve according to the precedents of various regions. Huìhào rebuked him, saying, "Dù Dū! He said it again:
"Mèng Bālang! Mèng Bālang! One day, as Huìhào passed before the kitchen, he saw them preparing evening noodles and asked:
"Is there a guest passing by? He replied, "The assembly of monks is preparing medicinal gruel. Emperor Hao called for the administrator and praised him, saying:
"In the past, when I practiced Chan, I drew water and pounded rice for others.

Now, seeing this finished rice and flour being steamed and prepared, it is no different from making offerings to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Arhats. Having eaten my fill, I no longer have any concern for practicing or studying. (100)
With such thoughts, the fragrant scent of the five flavors feeds eighty-four thousand households of worms. When you open your eyes, you are captivated by external objects;

when you close your eyes, you follow the transformations of dreams. You do not know that the Lord of Stipends, the Judge of Fate, and King Lue-sheng are following you to inventory and audit your records of provisions.
They have instructed you that the day for you to undergo suffering is near. Thereupon, the assembly of disciples... [did not...]
He could endure the solitude. He slandered [Fayan] to the county magistrate, saying, "The Elder cannot settle the assembly;

he does nothing but come and go up and down the hall, inspecting the minor details. The magistrate summoned Huishao to the county seat and rebuked him, saying, "A great *sadhaka* (Great Good Knowledge) should not be wandering back and forth between the two corridors and the mountain gate instead of sitting upright within the abbot’s quarters. Huishao replied, "Great..."
The Buddha Tongzhi (Supreme Wisdom-Penetration) sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, yet he did not perceive the Buddhadharma before him and failed to attain the Way of Buddhahood.
The official thought, "Is this man sitting because he is a Buddha? Or is he sitting because he has killed a Buddha? The official was bewildered and, with even greater reverence, paid him homage.
Huanglong Xin retired to Xiyuan.
Having resigned from his duties, he resided at Xiyuan and named his hall "Huì" (Obscurity). He said, "What I have declined is merely worldly affairs;
now I wish to devote myself exclusively to the practice of the Buddha-dharma. He posted this notice at the gate to demonstrate his commitment to Chan study. —Xie Jingwen.
He was appointed to guard Tanzhou. Xuedou Daoci declined three times before going, intending to remain at Mount Daimiao. When Jingwen asked for the reason, Daoci said:
"Before Mazu and Baizhang, there was no institution of abbotship; practitioners merely sought one another out along the shores of empty, quiet, and secluded places.
Although the position of abbot exists later on, kings and ministers honor and revere such a person as a Teacher of Gods and Humans."
Now it is not so. His name is registered with the government authorities like that of a common subject with a household record; he is merely dispatched by the *wubo* runners to be summoned.
How could this be done again? Jingwen then did not dare to trouble the Master with matters of the temple, wishing only to have an audience with him.
When the Master arrived at Changsha, Jingwen received his instructions on the Dharma, hearing things he had never heard before.
By imperial decree, Donglin was reformed from a Vinaya monastery into a Chan center, and Huitang Xin was appointed to uphold the Chan dharma of Letan Changzong.

Changzong had spent twenty years coming and going at the gate of Huanglong before emerging into the world to reside at Letan. In this year, by imperial decree, Donglin was reformed from a Vinaya residence into a Chan seat.
Scholar Wang Shao was appointed as the Governor of Nanchang and wished to invite the Master [to serve there].

The mind was his master. When the mind arose, he took charge on its behalf; when it perceived the need for a general retreat, he knew it instantly. Emperor Yao issued proclamations to various commanderies, ordering them to search for him everywhere.

In a remote valley along the Xintu River, he finally responded to the summons. Monastics from all over the world gathered there at the mere mention of his reputation. His disciples spoke among themselves, saying:
"Master Huiyuan has a prophetic record stating that seven hundred years after my passing, there will appear a Great Being in human form."
Shi Ge established my place of practice; now his words have been fulfilled.
Chan Master Xingcong resided at Shengshou Monastery.
Cong was a dharma heir of Yuanzhao Ben, who also resided at Shengshou. When Su Ziyou (Zhe) was exiled to Gaoyang, he visited Cong and attained realization.
He subsequently visited Shun of Hongzhou. When Shun showed him the kōan regarding the "pinching of the nose," Zhe attained great enlightenment upon hearing these words.
He presented a verse, saying: "In middle age I heard the Way and realized my former errors; By chance I met the old master Shun. Pinching the nose, I directly entered the true face;
Shaking my head, I would not accept any other tongs or hammers. Withered vines and tattered robes—what business do you have with me? White wine..."
"Blue salt—'Who am I? The moon rises over the eastern eaves; a cup of nectar as smooth as molasses.
Chan Master [Xuedou] was a descendant of Huanglong who traveled to Yangshan, a man of great stillness."
Weili was extremely strict in his personal conduct. While residing at Mount Yang, he sat in a deep forest during a summer night and bared his torso to feed the mosquitoes.
He subsequently suffered from intestinal inflammation that did not subside for ten days; he then cut off about a foot of it with a knife, though the flow of blood would not stop.
His disciples wept and said, "Master, why do you alone not endure this a little longer? He replied, "Because they obstruct my practice of the Way. He then prostrated himself upon his bed.
Above, he was of no benefit to the world. Was death not better for him than life? On a day in the eleventh month, he preached a verse and passed away.
Upon cremation, five-colored śarīras were obtained; his bones and stones were joined together by cords. A stūpa was erected to the east of the monastery.
In the fourth year, the Xin-you year, National Teacher Qing moved from Haihui to Mount Touzi.
From Baiyun Haihui, the Master himself moved to reside at Touzi; his disciples progressed even further, with many attaining secret realization through hidden penetration.

It was exceedingly numerous. This indeed fulfilled the prophecy that "different sprouts would flourish. Initially, when the mountain was first opened during the Da Tong era, there was a record stating:
"If my stupa turns red, it shall be my second coming. The local people happened to repair the stupa until it took on the color of agate;
not long after, the Patriarch took charge of the monastery.
Chan Master Mumozhe moved from Yuelu to Daguang Miao.
Mumozhe was the son of Wen of Wenchuan. When Cuiyan Zhen was traveling as a wandering monk, Mumozhe was able to recognize his potential.
Zhen was one who would flaunt his own strengths to outshine others, earning him the nickname "Zhen the Chest-Puncher. For twenty years, Mumozhe associated with him without ever making a mistake.
Lilongzhen said to people, "Thirty years from now, Quzhe will perform great Buddhist services. After Zhizhen passed away, he enshrined his remains in a stupa on Mount Xi.

He observed the mourning period for three years before departing to travel through the Xiang region. Carrying only a single bowl, he moved like clouds and birds; whether one leaves or stays depends on the weight of the monastic community.
When Xie Jingwen was the governor of Tanzhou, he invited him to reside at Yuelu Monastery, and shortly thereafter, he was transferred to Daopei.
The assembly numbered two thousand fingers (individuals), yet there were no external constraints; everyone regulated themselves.

Only after the morning gruel did he receive his disciples to inquire about the Way, which was called "entering the chamber. While at other places such inquiries occurred only once or twice a month, Master Zhe conducted them without fail every day.

After the evening meal was concluded, Zhe personally engaged in manual labor, treating his attendants as if they were strangers passing by. For fourteen years, he offered incense in the morning and lamps in the evening.
At night, he performed prostrations and inspected the lamps along the corridors of the hall with a bundle of thatch;
when weary, he would cover his head with his cassock and take a brief nap in the Hall of the Three Sages.
The Chan Master [Dongshan] entered nirvana at Longqing, under Huanglong, on the seventh day of the third month.
When his body was cremated, the scent of the smoke reached forty *li* in every direction—east, west, south, and north.
Throughout the grasses, trees, sands, and pebbles, golden-colored śarīras were found everywhere; the total amount collected amounted to several *hu*.
Su Che wished to compose a record for them but harbored doubts about the matter. While he was lying ill with a fever, he dreamed of someone rebuking him, saying:
"Why do you doubt the Master's affairs? To doubt is to be ill. Within the dream, Che composed an inscription which said: "I examine..."

The Honored One who heads the three realms has not limited his mastery to this alone; however, out of compassion for the narrow-minded and inferior of the world, he has merely shown these minor aspects.
Chan Master Yiyu of Fachang, a successor of Beichen, attained stillness.
Among those who encountered [Hui]bei Chan, Xian was the most long-standing; he succeeded to his Dharma and resided at Fachang. His style of solitary austerity was revered by all quarters.
The two senior monks Ying and Sheng, as well as Huanglong Nan, Danning Kuan, and Baojue Xin, all went to visit him.
His Dharma resonance was resonant and clear, striking with a ringing clarity. Xu Xi, the Grand Marshal of the Dragon Diagram (Longtu), was a friend from his days as a commoner. He was about to—
On the day before his passing, Huà composed a verse for Xǐ, saying: "This year I am seventy-seven; when traveling, one must choose an auspicious day.
Yesterday I consulted the tortoise-master, who reported that this morning is favorable. Xǐ was greatly startled and called for Wéiqīng to go together with him.
They encountered [Huà] sitting in the main hall, where he had entrusted the affairs of the monastery to the *jian-sì* (superintendent), saying: "I have resided on this mountain for thirty years."
"Because I must protect and cherish that which is permanently established, I have personally presided over it every time. Now I am departing; you all must be alert and vigorous.
Having finished speaking, he raised his staff and said, "Tell me, to whom is this being entrusted? Both Xì and Qīng were struck with silence.
He then cast the staff to the ground, lay down upon his bed, rested his head upon his arm, and passed away.
Xiangfu Yin said: "Fayu and Xian of Xinghua were both dharma heirs of Beichen Xian, making them the fifth generation of Yunmen.
Fayu maintained his Way amidst thousands of crags and ten thousand valleys with a stern and austere demeanor, living alone in a dilapidated hut;
whereas Xian possessed talent and capacity, tending to a thousand followers as if they were but one or two, performing great Buddhist services throughout the Jing and Hu regions."

In the interim, [the influence] spread to the Man and Mai peoples, all of whom admired the Way and turned toward transformation. When Zhang Dun opened the Mei Mountains, he invited Xuánxiàn to go there.

Upon hearing that Xuánxiàn had arrived, the elders of the Man tribes all joined their palms and listened to his instructions; thus the Jing-Man region was settled, and this was due to Xuánxiàn’s efforts.

One was solitary and austere; the other was perfectly harmonious. Together they raised the banner of Beichan (Beishan), and both masters flourished with great influence in the north and south during this period.
Thus, the Way of Shaoyang (Shitou Xiqian) was greatly revitalized.
Thereafter, as it declined and fell into disrepair, it gradually became beyond recovery. Alas! Is it not because of the individuals involved that the Way rises or sinks?
In the fifth year, the *wuxu* year, Chan Master Daokai returned north to Yishui.
Having taken his leave of Touzi, he returned to Yishui and resided at Mount Mian. He subsequently emerged from seclusion to take up residence at Xian-dong in Yishui.
Ruiguang had originally been at Qionglong in Wu, but he returned to reside at Ruiguang.
His Dharma assemblies flourished daily. Chen Xiang, the Governor of Wulin, ordered Ben to choose between two monasteries, Chengtian and Xingjiao;

however, the people of Suzhou crowded the roads to block his departure and entreat him to stay. Furthermore, due to the earnest invitation from Jingci Monastery, an official letter was issued [to transfer him there].
He addressed the clergy and laity, saying: "I have borrowed this master for three years to plant blessings for this region. He has resided here for nine years;
this year, Imperial Attendant Zeng Xiaoxu shall escort him back home to comfort the longing of the people of Suzhou. He then resided at Qionglong Fuzhen.
Chan Master Puzi moved from Taiping to Huayan in the Eastern Capital.

Puzi was the son of the Xie family of Jianyang. In his youth, he gained renown as a candidate for the jinshi examination, but he renounced that path to enter the monastic life. Later, he visited Fushan Yuan to receive the Dharma.
People of Shu invited him to reside at Ganlu Temple, and he subsequently moved to Taiping. His reputation for the Way spread widely throughout the capital. The people of the capital...
The scholar requested to reside at Huayan Temple in Dongjing.
Chan Master Huizhi lived in seclusion on Mount Heng.

Initially, Zhì had pursued his studies in lecture halls, but upon meeting Dongshan Wumen, he attained sudden enlightenment. Wumen said, "Although your Zen is of an extraordinary caliber, it is a pity that..."
"Your conditions are not yet sufficient," [the Master] replied. He understood his intention, bowed in farewell, and departed. He lived as a hermit on Mount Heng for over twenty years.

When scholar-officials visited his dwelling, he did not pay them much heed or respond to them. When people asked for the reason, he said, "Those men of wealth and status are eloquent, learned, and widely informed.
I am but a monk who eats his daily rice; my speech is dull and slow, and I have nothing worth saying. It is simply that I am naturally simple-minded."

Go! A verse says: Ten thousand affairs are all brought to rest, entrusted to the simple and innocent; Its traces allow wild deer to visit at times. Without removing his hempen robe, he uses his fist as a pillow;
For many lifetimes, his dreams have remained in the Green Ivy Hermitage. Question: What is the purpose of your dwelling in the mountains?
Zhì said: "I dwell in the mountains; alone I shut my wooden gate, with no other pursuit. Three pieces of firewood arranged in the shape of the character 'pin' (品)."
Huikai did not need to wield his brush for his literary brilliance to be revealed.
When Xueyu came to pay his respects to Dongshan, Xueyu was then leading the assembly at Daowu.
He took several monks with him to visit Yungai Zhi. Before Zhi had spoken more than a few sentences, [Xueyu] had already exhausted [his understanding].
Zhi knew what was within him. He smiled and said, "I observe that the Senior Monk’s temperament is extraordinary; why then do your words and breath sound like those of a drunkard?
Yue’s face flushed and he broke into a sweat, saying, "I pray for the Master’s compassion. Zhi spoke with him further, piercing him with his words.
Yue was utterly bewildered and subsequently requested to enter the room [for formal instruction]. Zhi said, "This old monk has no merit; the Way does not accept me."
He was trusted by others, yet he had been relieved of his duty of receiving prostrations from the head seat.

One day, [Yuanwu] became certain that [Foyan] would slander him, so he asked Yue, "Have you ever seen Master Fachang Yu? Yue replied, "I have read his recorded sayings; they are sufficient for one's own understanding."
He did not wish to see him. [The Master] asked, "Have you ever seen Master Wenzhong of Dongshan? He replied, "That man from Guansi has no sense.

He drags around a hempen skirt that reeks with the stench of urine; what excellence does he have? [The Master] said, "You should simply take up your investigation at the place where it reeks with the stench of urine.
Zhiyue then went to visit Dongshan and profoundly grasped his profound and essential meaning.
In the sixth year, the *guihai* year, the seventh patriarch of the Cao-Dong school, Tōji, entered *nirvāṇa*.

The patriarch’s *Go-i* (Five Ranks) discourse states: "The vast sky is of one color; how can stars and moon be distinguished? The great earth is without partiality; withering and flourishing [are one]."
They are inherently distinct. Therefore, within the Dharma there is no separate dharma; how could delusion and awakening ever reach one another? The mind does not exist as a self-sufficient mind;
it is provisionally expounded through words and symbols. These words are both partial and complete, direct and ultimate, comprehensive and harmonious. As for this Dharma:
