Not falling into the duality of right and wrong, how could he be concerned with the myriad phenomena? The profound intent was already harmonized within the moon reflected in water; the source of the school and its branches merged in the Golden River.
Not falling into empty stillness, he returned to the path and attained the wondrous. At the end of the fourth month, he manifested a slight illness.

He wrote a letter to take leave of his patrons, ascended the seat to recite a verse of farewell to the assembly, and passed away while seated. His remains were cremated, and five-colored *śarīra* relics were found. A stupa was erected for them.
To the northwest of the temple, Yunkyung Tyeong said:
"Fushan Yuan had already succeeded to Xianye; he further followed Taiyang and fully attained the principle of 'reciprocal transformation' (*huixu*).
He then composed the *Nine Bands* (*jiudai*) to clarify the origins of the 'correct,' 'deviant,' and 'combined' bands. Taiyang [bestowed] leather shoes directly..."
He entrusted it to him. Later, he obtained Touzi Qing and thereby succeeded to the True Dharma.
Fushan may truly be said to have produced two dragons from a single drop of ink.
He was the eighth patriarch of the Caodong school.
His taboo name was Daokai. He was the son of the Cui family of Yishui and succeeded to Toudi.
In the seventh year of the Jiazi cycle, Sima Guang presented the book he had compiled for imperial inspection; it was granted the title *Zizhi Tongjian*.
The eighth patriarch of the Caodong school, Master Fuyong, succeeded to the lineage (for thirty-five years).
Moving from Xian-dong to Longmen in Western Luo, he ascended the hall and said: "To call it 'one phrase' is already to bury the ancestral wind;
to accommodate the present age is to cause the universal path to decline. Therefore, one borrows function to clarify status, employing action within the essence."

Abiding in the state, one clarifies the function by means of the position; the essence resides within the sphere of function. If both essence and function are clearly manifest, it is like the two leaves of a door opening wide;
one must not fixate one’s attention upon the door leaves themselves. As the Old Man of Xinfeng said: "The peaks are rugged and extraordinary;
the cranes do not pause their flight. The numinous trees stand tall and remote; the phoenixes have no place to perch. Only when this is so can one achieve success without abiding therein.
Like a flash of lightning, it is difficult to pursue; in the mere interval of a thought, one has traveled ten thousand miles.

By Imperial decree, Zongben, the Chan Master of Xiangguosi Temple, was summoned. Mingfeng (the temple was converted from the Vinaya school to the Chan school, praising the Emperor for his ability to know the Way).

The Emperor issued an edict to expand the Xiangguosi Temple, reorganizing its sixty-four courtyards into eight Chan and two Vinaya halls. He summoned Zhenben to serve as the first patriarch of Huelin Monastery.

Upon his arrival, the Emperor dispatched an envoy to inquire after his well-being. After three days, an imperial decree was transmitted for him to expound the Dharma at the Three Gates of the monastery for the sake of the officials and commoners.
The following day, he was summoned for an audience at the Yanhe Hall, where he was questioned regarding the Way and granted a seat.
Muben immediately sat in the full lotus posture. The Emperor asked which temple he had originally served as a monk at.
Muben replied, "Chengtian Yong'an Temple in Suzhou. The Emperor was greatly pleased and granted him tea. Muben then raised his cup and drank deeply; he then swirled it and shook it.
The Emperor said, "The Chan school is just beginning to flourish; you should guide it well. Muben replied, "Your Majesty’s knowledge of this Way is like the sun shining."
"Your Majesty, how could your servant dare to be negligent? He then took his leave. The Emperor watched him depart and said to those around him, "He is truly a monk of wisdom and virtue.
Xiangfu Yin remarked, "The Buddha’s regulations for those who have left home dictate that one should beg for food with a single bowl and dwell for a night beneath trees or among tombs."

In form, they study the Way, yet they are entirely without regard or attachment. Since the climates and customs of the Eastern Land of the Quaking (China) differ from those of Western India, begging for food is inconvenient; thus, they have further adopted the practice of using bowls for meals. Because the faculties of people here are weak, they are unable to sleep in the open air; consequently, they established monastic groves (*saṃghārāma*). Although these were not intended to seek sustenance or comfort, such expedient methods already deviate from the Buddha’s regulations. As the times have declined further, the Buddha... [text ends]...

The prohibitions were not observed, and descendants flocked there in great numbers, occupying the grounds and settling in colonies. Famous mountains and great monasteries were transformed into anthills and honeycombs;
Buddhist temples and cloisters became like taverns and brothels. The tradition of Chan study fell silent and was unheard of.
Seeing this with weary eyes and a cold heart, who could restore order? Emperor Shenzong opened up Xiangguo Monastery to establish both Chan and Vinaya schools.
Truly, if a sovereign in the Dharma-ending age honors the Way and values the Dharma, he shall not fail the entrustment of Vulture Peak;
therefore, I have specially recorded this to show it to the world.
By imperial decree, Fashou of Jiangshan was appointed to propagate the Dharma at Fayun Temple.
Fayan Wenyi successively presided over Qian, Xixian, Jiangshan, and Changlu, each with assemblies of a thousand monks. He was then known as "Iron-Faced Wenyi.
When Fayun Temple was newly established in Bianjing, an imperial edict summoned Wenyi to serve as its founding abbot for the first generation.

On the day he ascended the hall, an imperial messenger descended to present incense and a robe of *mòná* (worn-out rags). The Imperial Prince, the King of Jing, paid his respects at the seat of the Dharma and transmitted the imperial decree.

He conveyed the imperial decree regarding the ritual of the Emperor’s personal visit and was granted the title "Yuántōng" (Perfect Penetration). Day and night, officials and scholars came to him to inquire about the Way.
At that time, Sīmǎ Guāng had recently ascended to high office; fearing that the Buddhist Dharma was becoming too prevalent, he was actively attempting to suppress it.

Fǎxiù said to him, "Your Excellency is brilliant and a hero among men, yet you could not have attained such a state without the aid of the Buddha-Dharma. Have you suddenly forgotten your original vow? Wēn... [text ends]
The Duke’s mind consequently became somewhat lax. Li Bashi (Li Gonglin) was skilled at painting horses. Xiu rebuked him, saying, "You are a scholar-official who has gained fame through painting;
moreover, you paint horses, hoping that others will praise it as a masterpiece. To have such mastery is enough to be feared—it could lead one into the belly of a horse.
From then on, Li Gonglin ceased his brushwork. Xiu then urged him to paint an image of Avalokiteśvara to atone for his transgression. Huang Ting... [text ends]

Sengjian composed licentious verses, which people vied with one another to circulate. Sengxiu also rebuked him, saying, "How can you so willingly apply the subtlety of your calligraphy and ink to such things?
Jian laughed and said, "Will you then place me within the belly of a horse?

Sengxiu replied, "By using licentious language to stir the lustful hearts of the people of the world, it will not stop at the horse's belly; I fear you will instead be born in the *naraka* hells. Jian repented and apologized.
Xiangfu Yin said: "When Master Wen first did not understand the Buddha-dharma, it was simply because his resolve to uphold the orthodox teachings was so earnest.
He once saw his discourse on the Buddha which stated: 'The Buddha was likely a sage from the Western Regions.
As a person, he was pure and frugal, possessing few desires; he was compassionate and kind, loving all things. Therefore, he wore tattered and patched robes and ate vegetarian food.'"
They eat coarse food, dwell among crags and in the wilds, and cast out their wives and banish their children; thus they maintain themselves with extreme frugality, fearing to trouble others.
Even regarding plants, trees, insects, and fish, they do not dare to kill them recklessly, desiring to coexist with all creatures without harming one another.
All these practices are intended to purify the person and remain unencumbered by worldly things.
"Indeed, those such as Ling Zizhong and Jiao Xian in China come close to this. Such were the words of Lord Wen (Ouyang Xiu).
It is no wonder that he did not understand the Buddha-dharma and sought instead to manage it;
what Lord Wen perceived was merely what is shown when a Buddha first renounces worldly glory to enter the mountains and study the Way. How could he have known [the Buddha's true nature]?
The vastness of this [Dharma] and the profound depth of its principles are such that even the Three Sages and Ten Holy Ones have yet been unable to fathom them;
how then could those like Boyang and Jiaoxian hope to approach it? Because they were of inferior capacity, they regarded the precious throne as a rare treasure and were struck with wonder at it.
The dark-skinned slave and the white ox—these are the Buddha’s discarding of precious robes to don tattered rags; it is for the sake of delivering sentient beings.
How could the Buddha truly be like this? Nevertheless, later on, after the Duke of Wen (Ouyang Xiu) heard the Dharma from the two dukes Fu (Shen) and Han (Zhao), he had a silent realization.
Regarding Fan Zhen’s discourse on the marks of emptiness (*śūnyatā-lakṣaṇa*), he playfully addressed him in verse, saying: "There is no need for heavenly maidens..."

[The Master] dispersed [the assembly]. Having already understood and moved the mind of meditation, he said again: "This humble son has been enlightened for a long time; Jingren has now fallen back into delusion. He said again:
"Once you have reached the shore, what need is there for a raft? One brandishes the hoe without using gold. Let the floating clouds come and go as they will;
the bright moon remains in the heart of heaven. If this were indeed so, then Master Wen’s final path would certainly not have involved making such statements as those previously cited.

The insights of men wax and wane with the times. Since Lord Wen had not yet attained a profound understanding of the Buddha-dharma, he hastily took up the pen for the national history and proceeded to engage in reckless disparagement and excision.
Consequently, he caused doubt and error among later generations, undermining right view and causing them to fall into the net of delusion.
How can he escape the blame for this failure in slandering the True Dharma? May future gentlemen, I pray, refrain from even a single [such act].

At that time, those who measured with a ladle and held counting sticks recklessly attempted to fathom the heavens and gauge the ocean; it was only because they were driven by empty fame that they could do so.
When Qingyuan arrived at Taiping to attend upon the Patriarch, he [did not act thus].
Huiyuan was the son of the Li family from Linqiong. When he first read the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage:

"This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination. He questioned his lecturer about this, but the lecturer could not answer. Huiyuan sighed and said, "Scholastic learning and the terminology of names and characteristics are not the means for resolving the great matter of birth and death.
He then traveled south to visit various masters in succession until he met the Patriarch at Taiping. Thereupon, he went forth to beg for alms.
In Luzhou, Yuan was once struck down by the ground during a sudden rainstorm. Amidst his distress, he heard two people exchanging harsh insults.

One who was offering counsel said, "You are still preoccupied with your vexations. Upon hearing these words, Yuan attained a realization. When he returned home, whenever anyone questioned him, Yuan would simply say, "I am not as good as you;
you understand it well enough yourself. At that time, Yuan was seventeen years old.
Chan Master Fayuan Anji was a descendant of Tianyi.
Born into the Xu family of Linchuan, he received the essential instructions and secret keys from Tianyi Hui. Returning to Linchuan, he resided at Ruyi Yuan on Mount Huang.
There, amidst dilapidated buildings and crumbling walls that could not shield him from wind and rain, he spent ten years until a great mansion was completed as if by transformation. He then departed.
Hui'an retired to Yuen'en Temple in Wuning, where there were only a few thatched rooms and a broken bed without a wooden slat frame; he found particular joy in these humble conditions.
The District Magistrate, seeking to mobilize the local elite, plotted to renovate the temple entirely. Hui'an laughed and said, "The Dharma is fundamentally for the salvation of people.
To force this upon them now before they have awakened their resolve is called 'worldly activity,' not 'Buddhist practice. Hui'an [then] with the Dharma...

Regarding Daoxiu’s brothers: Daoxiu once sent a letter inviting An to return to secular life. Upon reading it, An laughed and said, "I initially thought Daoxiu possessed some brilliance, but from this point forward, I know he is merely deluded.
A man who has left the household life should distinguish the matter of the Dharma among graves and beneath trees, as if his head were on fire.
Now, for no reason, he has erected a great house at a major thoroughfare to support several hundred people."

"A frivolous fellow! This is truly opening one's eyes to urinate upon one's own bed. Why should I even deign to converse with him? Yet, from this point on, my school will become increasingly diminished.
In the seventh month, he ordered his disciples to collect the official documents of the abbot’s quarters and burn them together, entrusting the affairs of the monastery to a single monk.
In the eighth month, he passed away.
Chan Master Linji [Linji] of Shishuang was a successor of Huanglong.
While under Huanglong Nan’s guidance, Linji’s intellectual acuity was sharp and penetrating; his fame resounded throughout the monastic community.
He was ranked among the peers of Wen of Guansi and Ying of Shaowu. He established the Dharma at Shishuang. At that time, Zhenjing Wen was at Dongshan, yet Linji did not...

He was well-known to his acquaintances, who held him in deep respect. He sent a verse to the monks, which said: "Those who wander to the four seas in search of dhyāna—yet fail to reach Xinfeng—are truly deluded.
On the eighth day of the third month, he shaved his head, bathed, and delivered a sermon with profound sincerity before passing away in stillness.
Upon cremation, his relics were of five colors.
In the eighth year, the year of Yi-chou (1065), Dongshan Wenzhi arrived in Jinling. Prime Minister Wang Anshi invited him to reside at Baoning Temple.
Wenzhi declined the invitation from Dongshan and traveled east through the Three Wu regions until he reached Jinling. At that time, Wang Anshi was residing at Dinglin Temple.
Upon hearing that Wen had arrived, he hurriedly stepped out of his shoes to welcome him, regretting that they had met so late.

Greatly delighted to hear the Dharma, he donated his residence to establish a temple called Baoning and invited Wen to be its founding abbot. He petitioned the court, which granted him the title Zhenjing.
Scholars and officials visited there without a single day passing. Wen, unable to endure the labor, eventually returned to Gaoyang and built a hermitage at the foot of Jiufeng.
It is said that in his final years, scholars came from afar to him.
This was during the first year of the Yuanyou era of the Zhezong reign (the Bingyin year). Zhezong’s personal name was Xu.
The Patriarch himself moved from Tàipíng to Báiyún Hǎihuì.

Entering the hall, he preached the Buddha and expounded the Dharma; he raised his mallet and held up his whisk—ten thousand miles of white clouds. When Dēishān entered the gate, he struck with his staff;
when Línjì entered the gate, he shouted—ten thousand miles of white clouds. Yet even after this, suchness is not permitted, nor is its absence permitted.
"It is not so. It is not so, nor is it not so—neither is acceptable. This too is ten thousand miles of white clouds.
Or perhaps someone might come forth and say, "Venerable sir, for you to speak thus—it too is ten thousand miles of white clouds."
This talk is like "the dwarf watching the play," following others up and down. Thirty years from now, it will be a source of great laughter.
But tell me, what is there to laugh at? It is the laughter of ten thousand miles of white clouds.
Qingyuan Shi returned from begging alms in Feichuan and sighed, saying, "My task has finally been accomplished. He then went to visit a desolate county; how could he have known...?
Having resolved his own matter, he then composed a verse to take his leave. The Patriarch sent him off with this verse:

When we parted before the Pavilion of the White Crane, The peach blossoms were like brocade and the willows like eyebrows. On this day next year, leaning against the balustrade to look, I shall find as before but one or two green branches.
Chan Master Shanzhou Ji of Huili Temple under Yuquan passed away.
Shanzhou Ji succeeded Yuquan Fang. On the full moon of the twelfth month, he bathed, purified his hair, and spoke this verse:
"The mountain monk dwelt at Ruijun; I have never manifested words or phrases. Seventy-three years have come; Seventy-three years have gone. Thus he spoke.
He passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. Three days later, his beard and hair grew back.
Chan Master Zanyuan Jie of the Ciming lineage succeeded to Jiangshan.
Yuan resided at Jiangshan during the early Xining era. When Wang Anshi was appointed as Chancellor, his prestige shook the world; there was not a month that passed...
Hao Yuan had never previously given instruction. When his younger brother, Shi Anshang, asked about the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma, Yuan said:
"The Buddhas and patriarchs are no different from ordinary people. That which makes them different is simply their ability to protect their own thoughts.
A tree atop a high tower must have a root; its root lies in the tiniest sprout. Water that surges to the heavens must have a source; its source lies in a mere trickle. Pure and serene...
Within the mind, there is no reason for thoughts to stir; how precarious and perilous it is! It is worse than a towering pavilion.

To let them run wild and rampant is worse than a flood reaching the heavens. How could such things be stirred? The Buddhas and Patriarchs transmitted the Dharma to one another, invariably exhorting: "Guard and uphold it well yourself. They asked, "Is this all there is to the Buddha-Dharma?
They replied, "The most beautiful is not ornate; the ultimate words are not prolix. Indeed, ornamentation—*hua*—[is but a distraction].
To be entangled in worldly affairs is to be far removed from the Way; yet the common world persists in this way.

When Master Shen Gong discussed the methods for governing the world, he still said that effective governance does not depend on many words, but rather on how much one puts them into practice. How much more so must this be true for the supramundane Dharma?
When Anshi retired from the government, his boat reached Shitou; the carriages and horses of the scholar-officials filled the valleys as they entered.
It was already past the second watch when Yuan came out to welcome him. After exchanging a single bow, he withdrew. Shi sat toward the eastern side; officials and guests filled the seats.
Shi looked around and asked where Yuan was. An attendant replied, "He has been asleep for some time. Shi then proceeded to serve the meal to his guests.

Suddenly, news arrived that the kitchen and storehouse were on fire, and the flames had reached the Chaoyin Hall. The assembly scrambled in panic, vomiting their food as they fled in disarray like distressed bees or agitated ants;

yet Yuan continued to eat and drink as usual, looking up at the rafters with a steady gaze. When he had finished his meal, he made no inquiry about the disaster. On another occasion, he once went outside the city walls.

A madman entered the monastery, killed a monk with a blade in his hand, and then committed suicide; their corpses lay side by side. Those on the left and right ran to report this, and a crowd gathered on the road, brandishing weapons.
From the Bai Gate (Baixia men) onward, the procession returned with a great throng of followers. Yet when they passed the place where the corpses lay, [Huiyuan] never once looked at them.
He ascended to his chamber and sat upright. His attendants stood by his side, hoping that Yuan would have something to say, yet he closed his eyes as he had done on ordinary days.
Thereupon, they gradually withdrew and ultimately did not inquire further. One day, he suddenly said, "I wish to return to Eastern Wu;
prepare my belongings with haste. Shortly thereafter, he passed away.
Chan Master Shao Dengji succeeded to the Dharma at Yiquan.

Having studied under Yiquan, Dengji attained awakening through the instruction of Master Fang. He resided at Shengquan, where his Way and Dharma flourished greatly. One day, he ascended the seat and spoke this verse:
"At fifty-three years of age, I have no attachment to going or staying. When facing death, what shall I do? [Not...]"
He used his mouth to murmur prayers and entered a state of profound stillness. Two days later, hearing the sound of a bell, he suddenly regained consciousness.
Thereafter, his four elements were light and at ease; his body frequently produced *śarīra* relics. During great droughts, his prayers for rain were invariably answered.
In the second year, the *dingmao* year, Huilin sent Ben back to the Wu region to reside at Lingyan.
Ben requested to return home on account of his old age and thus withdrew from Huilin. On the day he departed the capital, carriages and horsemen belonging to princes and high officials escorted him.
They were closely associated. Benhuai said, "The months and years cannot be toyed with; old age and illness do not wait for anyone.

Only through diligent cultivation without indolence can one truly act as a true companion. Those who heard this were moved without exception. Upon reaching Wu, they were welcomed to reside at Lingyan.
He closed his door and remained in a state of profound stillness, yet scholars seeking him out appeared one after another along the road.
The Chan Master followed Yue to reside at Doushuai;
after Yue received the essential instructions on the meaning of Dongshan’s teachings, he stayed at Luyuan, where he attained penetration under the senior practitioner Qing Su.
Che. That year, he resided at Long’an Toushuai.
Chan Master Chunbai was expounding the Dharma at Zhaojue.
Bai had studied under Huangbo Weisheng; when Sheng returned to Shu, Bai followed him, carrying his headcloth and alms bowl. It happened that the military governor of Chengdu submitted a memorial.
Zhaojue was renamed Shifang. Shengju submitted his report to Kaifa.
In the third year of the Wuchen cycle, Chan Master Yuanji resided at Cuoyan.

Daji received the secret transmission of Huanglong and bore the burden of the monastic community. Disregarding cold and heat, he cleared fields and planted pine trees, remaining steadfast in his single office for ten years without change.
When Huītáng Xīn wished to succeed Huanglong on the patriarchal seat, Daji fled, saying:
My late master cautioned me that before reaching the age of fifty, I must not act as a teacher. When I returned to my ancestral home, I was forty-eight years old.
At that time, Foyin Yuan encouraged me to accept the invitation of Xie Jingwen to reside at Cuiyan in Hongzhou.
In the fourth year, the Jih-si [year], Chan Master Shanben was appointed to reside at Jingci.
Shanben was a descendant of Dong Zhongshu; he visited Master Ben of Hui-lin, who looked upon him with particular regard. Shanben silently grasped his meaning.
The gist is this: he succeeded to both positions at Jingci Temple, where he was then acclaimed as the "Great and Small Ben.
Daolin Yu moved to Yunju;
Wang Anshang once sought the Dharma from Yu, who invited him to reside at Yunju. Yu said, "I shall take these bones back with me."
He was buried at the summit of Mount Feng.
The Chan Master was originally from Nanbu and resided at Daolin;
there he studied under Baizhang Huaiyu, receiving his certification. When Huaiyu moved to Yunju, Nan succeeded him on the seat.
In the fifth year, the Gengwu year,
Master Furong moved to Taiyang;
Jiufeng Wen took up residence at Guizong.
Wen resided at Gao’an for six years before moving to Guizong. Zhu Shiying of Xianmu followed him to inquire about the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma;
Wen replied to him with a letter.
Chan Master Dajue Huailian of Yuezhou, the fifth generation descendant of Yunmen and the Great Awakened One of Yueda, passed away.
Huailian had succeeded Ledu Tangcheng; he died without illness at the age of eighty-one.
Chan Master Fayun Yuantong Fashou of the sixth generation under Yunmen passed away.
As he was about to enter extinction, he called for his attendant to change his robes. Sitting upright, he spoke this verse: "When coming there is nothing; when going, it is empty.
North, south, east, and west—the affairs are all one and the same. To dwell in the six realms of existence brings no benefit. Fashou remained silent for a long time. Then the Inspector... [text ends]
Sihui stepped forward and said, "Master, why do you not speak the final word? Xiu replied, "Be careful, be careful.
Having spoken these words, he passed away.
Yangfu Yin remarked, "The Way of the Yunmen lineage was transmitted through six generations until it reached Yuan Tong Xiu, who caused it to flourish greatly. Xiu...
The dwelling he occupied was more magnificent than the wondrous world below; his preaching of the Dharma was like falling clouds and rain.
His majestic radiance could have allowed one to receive wings from him and soar through the heavens. Yet, those of his own school, Yan and Nanfang, laughed at him, deeming him a fool. Alas!
The Way is surely not such that it must reside within vast courtyards and gateways. When the sun reaches its zenith, it declines; when water fills to the brim, it overflows.
This is true even for the practice of the Way, let alone other matters. Master Yuan’s secluded mountains and desolate counties never saw more than a hundred followers throughout his life;

Master Fu Rong’s defiance of imperial edicts and endurance of exile led him to spend his final years in a lakeside hermitage—this cannot be said to be anything other than following one's natural destiny.
The essential resources for reaching far-reaching goals.
*Zongtong Bianian*, Volume Twenty-one;
*Zongtong Bianian*, Volume Twenty-two.
In the sixth year of the Yuanyou era, the *xinwei* year of Emperor Zhezong, the Master moved from Haihui to Dongshan.
Upon entering the monastery, he burned incense before the Patriarch’s stupa and pointed with his finger, saying: "At that time, he departed with his whole body in this very manner; now..."
He asked again, "Do you remember me coming here before? He replied, "How can this be verified? [The Master] said, "This shall serve as verification. Thereupon, he prostrated himself.
Later, the Magistrate of Huangmei invited him to open the hall for formal teaching. He delivered these words:
"For example, when an ox passes through a window lattice, its head, horns, and four hooves all pass through; why then does its tail fail to pass?"
Yun’gai retired to the West Hall.
Zhi resided at Yun’gai for ten years, daily tilling the vegetable garden with a hoe. He found the Zen grove inconveniently cold and damp;
his aspiration for the Way grew thin, and he would shake his head and refuse to admit those who came to study under him. Having retired to the West Hall, the monks of Xiangzhong heard of this.
His reception hall and chambers were filled to capacity.
Chan Master Changzong Jiji was a descendant of Huanglong at Donglin Guanghui Temple.
He was the son of the Shi family of Jianzhou. Having received the secret transmission from Huanglong, he resolved his will to greatly support and protect the teachings of the North.
Zong resided at Donglin. His fame reached the Son of Heaven, who issued an edict for him to reside at Zhixhai in Xiangguo Temple.

Zong repeatedly declined, citing his status as a mountain recluse and his old age and infirmity, stating he could not comply with the imperial decree. After two months, he received the imperial permission as requested and was granted the purple robe.

The Master’s title was Guanghui; he was later also granted the name Juezhao. When Su Shi visited Mount Lu, he stayed at Donglin Monastery and discussed the "Discourse on the Insentient" with Changzong.
He attained a realization, and at dawn, he presented this verse: "The sound of the brook is the broad and long tongue;
How could the color of the mountains not be the pure body? Last night, eighty-four thousand verses were spoken; How shall I bring them forth for others to see another day?"
Everyone approved of him. He possessed a great affinity for monastics; under his staff and whisk, the assembly constantly numbered seven hundred.
Such prosperity of the monastic seat had never before been seen in his time. On the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, he passed away after his bath.
Chan Master Cong Yueji succeeded Bao Feng at Doushuai Zhenji.
Yueji inherited the Dharma from Bao Feng Wen and resided at Doushuai. In his quarters, he established three questions to test practitioners.
"Those who part the weeds and gaze upon the wind do so only to seek the realization of their nature. Where, then, does the nature of the person before you reside? If you recognize your own nature..."
Only then can one be liberated from birth and death. When the light of the eyes falls to the ground, how does one achieve liberation?
If one can liberate oneself from birth and death, one will know the place of departure. When the four elements separate, where does one go?

When Zhang Shangying was serving as the Fiscal Commissioner (Cao) of Jiangxi, he visited Donglin Zong, who certified his realization and said: "I have a disciple who attained the Dharma and resides at Yuxi. It was he—
Cizhu was like an ancient mirror; one could converse with him. When Ying arrived at Fuben Ning, the various Chan masters went out to welcome him.
Cizhu was the first to pay his respects, and finally he asked Doushuai Yue, "I have heard that you, Master, are quick-witted and skilled in literary composition. Yue smiled and said:
Congyue was the ninth-generation descendant of Linji. If one were to discuss literature with the Commissioner, it would be exactly as if the Commissioner were discussing Chan with Congyue.
Ying silently took note of this and asked, "How far is Yuxi from here?
He replied, "Thirty li. He asked, "And Doushuai? He replied, "Five li. They then passed through Doushuai. Previously, Congyue had dreamed that he was wrestling with the sun with his hands.
Jue addressed the Head Seat, saying, "The image of the sun’s revolution is unfolding; Zhang Yuzhang shall pass by here. I must strike him deeply and pierce him with painful words.
The Head Seat said, "Scholars and officials loathe those who offend them; they may even give rise to further strife.
Yue replied, "Even if it causes affliction, it will at least cause him to withdraw from my monastery. As they were conversing, Ying suddenly praised Zong.
Duke Yue was not yet willing to accept his words. As the conversation continued until late at night, they discussed matters concerning the Chan school.

Yue rose, burned incense, and requested the Buddhas of the ten directions to bear witness, saying, "Since Donglin has certified Master Yunshi, does Master Yunshi have even the slightest doubt regarding the teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
He replied, "I do. Yue asked, "What words do you doubt? He replied, "I doubt the words of Xiangyan regarding the single..."
The Verse on the Feet. Regarding the story of Deshan’s alms-bowl: [Yunyan] said, "Since you have doubts about this, everything else is merely intellectual speculation and mental interpretation;
how could it ever reach the realm of great peace and bliss? Furthermore, as for Yantou’s words regarding the "final phrase"—is it existent?
Is it non-existent? [Yunyan] said, "It exists. Yantou laughed heartily, returned to his quarters, and shut the door. For an entire night, Ying...
He could not sleep peacefully. At the fifth watch, he rose from his bed and accidentally overturned the urinal. Suddenly, he attained great enlightenment.

He knocked on the door of the abbot’s quarters and said, "I have already caught the thief. [The abbot] asked, "Where are the stolen goods? Yunyuan was speechless. Zhiyue said, "Director of Administration, you may go now;
let us meet tomorrow. The following morning, Yunyuan presented this verse: "The drum is silent, the bell has sunk; the bowl is carried out."
[He] returned. A single thrust from Yantou was like a clap of thunder; indeed, he could live for no more than three years. [Yunmen] asked, "Was it because he had received a prediction from him?
Yue then said, "Studying Chan is only for the sake of severing the life-root; otherwise, one merely gives rise to interpretations based on words."

You, Master, have already deeply realized such teachings. Yet, when it comes to the ultimate subtlety, they cause people to remain unaware and unknowing, falling instead into the realm of limited categories.
Thus, I offer this verse as proof: In the midst of ordinary conduct, every step is as it should be.

Though dwelling amidst sound and form, how could one linger in being or non-being? The single mind is without variation; the myriad dharmas are not distinct. Rest now, without differentiating essence from function.

Do not discriminate between the refined and the coarse; when facing the opportune moment, let nothing obstruct you. Responding to phenomena without constraint, the sentiments of right and wrong are exhausted, and both the ordinary and the sage are eliminated.

Who gains and who loses? What is near and what is distant? To take the head as the tail, or to point to reality as being empty—turning one’s body within the realm of Māra, shifting one’s feet upon the path of heterodoxy—there is ultimately neither opposition nor compliance, and no violation of the essential practice. Thus, he was invited to Jianchang.

There was Fu Song, who recorded these events. Ying was titled the "Inexhaustible Layman" (Wujin Jushi). Later, he composed the *Fahufa lun* (Treatise on Protecting the Dharma) to manifest his resolve.
In the winter of that year, after bathing, he gathered the assembly and spoke this verse: "Forty-eight years; saints and ordinary beings have all been slain.
Not a hero am I; the road at Long'an is slippery. He then passed away suddenly. While Ying was in office, he dispatched Wen... [text ends].
A memorial service was held. A request was made at court, and an imperial edict conferred upon him the posthumous title of Great Master Zhenji (True Tranquility).
The Chan Master Chenghao of Yushan, the fifth generation descendant of Yunmen, resided at Yushan Temple.
The temple buildings were vast yet dilapidated and leaking; successive abbots had found it difficult to carry out repairs. Chenghao said:
"I have a karmic affinity with this mountain, but no affinity with the monastics. I am merely repairing the temple of this life to wait for the monastics of future lives.
He demolished the existing structures entirely and rebuilt them from the ground up. While residing on the mountain, Fajie Hao possessed neither brush, inkstone, nor books;

his chests and trunks contained no extra clothing, bags, or money. He sent a messenger to Jiangxi to say to Zhang Shangying: "I am old and sick, nearing death. I wish to obtain [the land of] Baizhang..."
"Hu Sù may serve as his successor. Yíng used this to propose Sù; however, Sù was unwilling to go. On the [blank] day of the twelfth month, he recited a gāthā to the assembly and passed away.
Sū Shí sought an audience while disguised in humble attire. Hào asked, "What is your honorable office and noble surname? He replied, "My surname is Chéng."
This is indeed weighing with the scale of the elders of the world. Huihao let out a shout and asked, "Tell me, how much does this one shout weigh? Su Shi had no reply.
This Chan Master was De Puji of He Shan under Huanglong.
Puzhu Heshan once said to the assembly, "When venerable masters of various quarters pass away, the monastic communities invariably perform memorial rites.
I consider this to be a mere empty formality. When I die, you should perform the first memorial rite for me. He then ordered that preparations for the memorial service be made from that time forward.
Because the assembly considered him old and fond of joking, they said, "When will the Master pass away? He replied, "When your offerings cease, I shall go.
Thereupon, they curtained off the main hall and seated Baopu in its center. They set out the sacrificial offerings and read the ritual texts;

as the disciples knelt and bowed to present the food, Baopu ate his fill with complete composure. From the chief disciples down to the laborers of the manor, each took his turn performing the rites day by day.
The funeral rites were suspended. It was said that they would proceed the following day once the snow cleared; however, when the time came, the clear sky suddenly turned to snow.
When the snow ceased, Puan sat upright, burned incense, and passed away.
Chan Master Huiyuan of Baoben under Huanglong also entered nirvana.
Originally residing at Chengtian Monastery, he once took his alms bowl to Huzhou. A local person there said, "A Chan master makes his home wherever he goes;

why do you alone favor Gusu? He was thus earnestly entreated to stay and not return. Consequently, he resided at Baoben Monastery. In the winter months, he ascended the seat, delivered a verse, and passed away.
Throughout his life, Yuan’s conduct and regulations followed those of Master Nan; for three years, his side never touched the edge of his mat.
Ten years later, the Tiantai master Yuanjing passed away at Longjing.
Jingzhu ascended to Upper Tianzhu and remained there for seventeen years. During the Yuanfeng era, he took his leave and returned once more; after another three [years]...
In his later years, he sat upright and diligently cultivated pure practices. Once, while eating with the monk Sengxi Zhong, Zhong observed a light like a firefly between [Fahai’s] brows;
reaching out to grasp it, he obtained a *śarīra*. Furthermore, [Fahai] obtained *śarīra* from the places where he slept and arose.
As he was about to pass away, he entered the Fangyuan Hermitage, sat in meditation, ceased all speech, and abstained from food and drink. He said to Canliao Daohan:

"My pure karma is about to be fulfilled. If there are no obstacles for seven days, my vow shall be realized. On the seventh day, he spoke a verse to the assembly and passed away with auspicious signs.
This was the seventh year of the Renshen cycle.
Keqin returned to Mount Dongshan to attend upon Master Chuewu as his attendant; Huiqin subsequently arrived and remained there to manage the calligraphy.
Keqin was the son of the Luo family from Pengzhou. From childhood, he could memorize a thousand words a day. Once, while wandering through a temple, he saw Buddhist scriptures.
Three times he returned to his state of despondency, as if he had recovered an old possession, saying, "I am surely a śramaṇa from a past life. He immediately left home and shaved his head.

When the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* was bestowed upon him, he suddenly fell ill and was on the verge of death. He sighed and said, "The true path to the nirvāṇa of all Buddhas does not lie within words and phrases.
That I sought it through sound and perceived it through form was why I have come to this point of death. Thereupon, he abandoned [the text].
He departed and traveled on foot out of Shu to visit Yuyuan Hao, Jinluan Xin, Dayue Zhe, and Huanglong Xin; all of them designated him as a vessel for the Dharma.
Finally, he visited the Patriarch (Zhaozhou). The Patriarch once said: "The Chan that people have attained by visiting various quarters is like a crystal bottle;
one must cherish and protect it without letting go. However, do not let me see it—use an iron hammer!"
"One blow will surely shatter it. One day the Patriarch asked, "The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning are like a vine leaning against a tree;
how do you understand this? Wumen struck out with a shout or offered various responses, exhausting all his skillful means, yet the Patriarch gave him no approval. The Patriarch said:
One must wait until mental consciousness is completely purified and all calculations are forgotten before one can understand;

yet even at such a state of non-calculation, if one speaks in barbarian tongues or Chinese, it still does not accord with the Patriarch’s intent. "Qin" refers to forcibly altering or displacing others, or uttering insolent words.
He departed in a fit of indignation. Nanyue said, "Wait until you are struck by a severe fever, and only then will you think of me.
Upon reaching Mount Jin, he was so exhausted by a case of *shanghan* (febrile illness) that he tested his usual insights and views, but none proved effective.

Reflecting upon his ancestors’ words, he made a vow to himself, saying: "When my illness has slightly abated, I shall return to the Fifth Patriarch. Upon seeing him, the Patriarch said with joy, "Have you come back?
He immediately ordered him to attend the hall, and he entered the quarters of the attendant. After a day of diligent service, he asked the Patriarch:
"The Second Patriarch said that when he sought the mind, it was ultimately unattainable. What, after all, is this? The Patriarch replied: "You must seek it for yourself."
Only then did Chan begin to attain these benefits; others could not exert such effort on your behalf.

During the latter half of the month, Chen the Judicial Intendant visited the Patriarch to inquire about the Way. The Patriarch said, "Judicial Intendant, when you were young, did you ever read the *Xiaoyan* (Light and Elegant) poems?"
There are two lines that are quite similar: "Frequently calling for Little Jade, yet originally there was no business;
it is simply that one wishes for the patron to recognize the voice. When the Provincial Commissioner responded with "Yes, yes," the Patriarch said, "But be careful.

Later, when Qin returned from outside and was standing in attendance, he asked, "I heard the Master recite the poem about 'Little Jade. Does the Provincial Commissioner understand it? He replied, "He only recognizes the voice."
He said, "It simply requires that you, the patron, recognize the sound. Since he had already recognized the sound, why was it not so?
He asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? [Dongshan] replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Wumen suddenly attained awakening;
he hurriedly went out and saw a rooster flying onto the railing and crowing with its wings spread. He then said to himself, "Is this not it?"
Sheng then tucked incense in his sleeve, entered the room, and upon meeting De, presented this verse: "The golden duck's fragrance has faded within the brocade curtains;
Amidst the reeds, one returns home, supported while drunk from singing. This youthful episode of refined elegance— I allow only the fair lady to know it alone. The Patriarch said:
"The great matter of the Buddhas and patriarchs is not something that those of inferior capacity and weak roots can attain. I shall assist you..."
"You are joyful. Guishan then addressed the elders throughout the mountain, saying, "My attendant has attained Zen.
From then on, wherever he went, he was esteemed as the foremost. One day, someone requested instruction regarding Linji’s "Four Guests and Hosts," asking, "What are they like?
Guishan said, "They are merely a set of milestones; what idle matter is this? He further remarked, "In my place here, it is rather like..."
"Sumo wrestling before the horse: fall down and it is finished. Qín, a son of the Wáng clan from Shūzhōu, received the tonsure in his childhood.

He constantly contemplated the saying, "This one reality alone is true; the other two are not real," and through tasting its meaning, he attained realization. Thereupon, he traveled extensively to consult renowned masters.
He had been coming and going at the Master’s gate for many years, yet he resented that the Master would not provide him with a seal of certification (*yinju*).
He left together with Foyin Keqin; when Keqin returned to serve the Master, he attained thorough realization. When Lingxun suddenly arrived, he intended to depart elsewhere.
Keqin insisted that he register as a resident monk and said, "I have been separated from you, brother, for over a month. How are you compared to when we last met?"
He said, "This is what I have doubted. He then entered the hall. One day, he heard the Patriarch cite a monk’s question to Zhaozhou:
"What is the master’s house style? Zhaozhou replied, "This old monk is deaf; ask with a loud voice.
When the monk asked again, Zhaozhou said, "You ask about my house style, yet I already know yours. Daoyin [immediately]—
Da Huo’s doubts were resolved. He said, "I beg the Master to point out the ultimate principle. The Patriarch replied, "The myriad phenomena of the universe are all sealed by a single Dharma.
Da Huo prostrated himself with great earnestness. The Patriarch then appointed him to oversee calligraphy.
Jingci’s Ben was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Fayun Monastery and was granted the title Dàtōng (Great Penetration).
Shitai’s Jie received a memorial of request from Su Shi.
Jie succeeded Huelin’s Chong and resided at Shitai in Yangzhou; at that time, Su Shi was the Governor of Yangzhou, and Jie requested his retirement. Su Shi [composed a memorial].
He led his subordinates to the stone pagoda and ordered the drum to be beaten to assemble the multitude.

From his sleeve, he produced a memorial and had Chao Wujiu read it aloud, saying: "How could the Great Being have ever preached the Dharma? Who produced the sound of the golden mane? Sentient beings each open their own hall;
what concern is this for the stone pagoda? Departing, do not manifest signs of action; staying, likewise follow conditions. Only observe the precepts."
Venerable Elder, you have opened the gate of non-duality and bestowed the inexhaustible treasury. To lament our long separation from West Lake is but a matter of chance;
yet, to stay for a while for the sake of Dongpo is nothing that cannot be. With a single prostration, we once again listen to the striking of the gavel.
As the boat turns back at the ferry crossing, the colors of the clouds and mountains remain as before; with the autumn rains having passed, the bells and drums have been renewed.
Regarding the sound of this [inscription], the precepts were then established once more at Seoktap (Stone Pagoda).
In the eighth year, the *gengyou* year,
Master Yungbong moved from Taeyang to Daehong.

The Patriarch himself moved from Taiyang to Dahuang in Suizhou. He invited all the famous officials and nobles of the time [to join him], whereby the spiritual influence of the Dongshan school spread widely throughout the northwest.
Chan Master Jingzhao Daozhen of Jingyin on Fushan passed away.
Zhen Xing was quiet and retiring, appearing as though he were unable to speak. He maintained his person with extreme simplicity; he did not change his single cotton skirt for twenty years.
Residing in the capital, he remained withdrawn and never left his door, remaining the same for thirty years. He had no personal preferences or indulgences.
On the western wall of Xue’s quarters, he requested Wen Yuke to paint ink bamboo, saying, "I shall let travelers behold it so that their minds and eyes may feel cool and refreshed;

this 'Lord of the Snows' can serve as my substitute for preaching the Dharma. At that time, [the Emperor] was concerned about the confusion regarding the Buddha-dharma and lamented the defects of nominalism and conceptualization;
he therefore established the two monasteries of Hui-lin and Zhi-hai at the Imperial Palace Temple (Shang-shi). Whoever presided over...
The Dharma must necessarily come to one of its own accord; he chose it for himself. On the seventeenth day of the eighth month, he said to his disciples, "In three days, I shall depart.
When the time arrived, he bathed, recited a verse, sat in the full lotus posture, and passed into stillness. He was eighty years of age.
In the first year of the Shaosheng era, the *jiashu* year (1094), Qingyuan returned to Dongshan and took up his duties as a receptionist. There he attained realization;
however, when he went to visit Guizong, his understanding was not in accord with Wen. He eventually traveled to Jiangshan, where he happened upon Weiqing, who said to him: "Recently, I have seen..."
A certain venerable elder in the capital remarked, "It seems there is a karmic affinity [between you and Master Yan]. Qing said, "Master Yan is the preeminent patriarch in the world;
why would he abandon him to travel afar? What is called a "karmic affinity" refers merely to a teacher of intellectual understanding.
"This merely accords with your original resolve," he said. Yuan agreed. After more than a year, he returned to Haihui. The Patriarch commanded him to contemplate:
"If one kills father and mother, one repents before the Buddha; but if one kills the Buddha and the Patriarch, where does one repent? Yunmen replied, "Exposed.
This case was later entrusted to him as the master of the reception hall. Once, sitting alone on a cold night, he stirred the ashes of the brazier and saw a single spark of fire.

He consented. Suddenly filled with joy, he said, "Probing deeply, there is something; the affairs of my entire life are just like this. He immediately rose and examined the *Lamp Records* on the desk.
